text: Two-phase goto: try networkidle2 (max 30s), on timeout fall back to domcontentloaded with remaining budget. Translate common proxy errors (ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED, ERR_PROXY_CONNECTION_FAILED, ERR_ABORTED) into actionable messages with host context.
how: Wrap scout.py/research.py fetch calls in navigateForCapture logic. Use puppeteer's waitForNetworkIdle with idleTime:500, concurrency:2. Map error codes to user-friendly strings via explainProxyRefusal().

title: Single user agent constant for browser and Node fetches
text: Define one `CAPTURE_USER_AGENT` (Chrome 131 on macOS) used by both puppeteer navigation and Node `fetch` for assets. Prevents anti-bot edges from serving HTML to browser but 403 to asset fetcher (observed on openai.com favicon).
how: In our asset downloaders (Muse, Cloudflare, Pollinations), set `User-Agent` header to match the Chrome version we run. Store in shared config; update when Chrome binary upgrades.

title: Color usage statistics separate brand accents from surface colors
text: Per-color stats: `bgCount` (background occurrences), `interactiveBg` (on <a>/<button>/role=button), `areaBg` (fills >50k px²), `textCount`, `maxArea`. Brand primary = high `interactiveBg` + chromatic; surfaces = high `areaBg` + low `interactiveBg`; text colors = high `textCount`. Top 48 colors returned.
how: When building brand kits from reference sites, use `interactiveBg` rank to pick accent color for CTAs/highlights, `areaBg` for section backgrounds, `textCount` for body copy. Avoids picking hero-section blue as brand accent.

title: PNG IHDR height validation to detect clipped renders
text: After every full-page screenshot, read the first 24 bytes of the PNG buffer to parse actual IHDR height. If produced height > MAX_PLATE_HEIGHT_PX (16384), discard the file and mark omitted. Catches silent clipping from lazy-load triggers during capture.
how: Add `pngHeight(buf)` utility to review.py; after each frame write, verify dimensions match expected 1920x1080 (or 4K). Log and retry chunks where height mismatches.

title: WebGL stall watchdog with dual-miss detection
text: Every 4s, send `Runtime.evaluate({expression:'1'})` via CDP with 8s timeout. Two consecutive misses (timeout or error) triggers `onStall()`. Errors count as answers (page alive). Returns `{stop()}` for cleanup. Prevents hung GPU processes from stalling render workers.
how: In doctor.py render worker monitor, spawn a WebGL stall watcher per Chrome tab. On stall, kill tab, mark chunk for retry, increment GPU-hang metric. Uses existing CDP connection from puppeteer.

title: Scroll screenshot tiling with 30% overlap and percentile naming
text: Viewport height * 0.7 step. Positions distributed across scroll range: `finalPositions[i] = round(i * (positionCount-1) / (count-1)) * step`. Filenames `scroll-XXX.png` where XXX = scroll percentage (0-100). Includes full-page plate as last file. Caps total files at `maxScreenshots` (default 21).
how: For long-form reference captures (e.g., competitor long-reads), add `capture_scroll_tiles(url, max=21)` to scout.py. Use tiles as visual reference for pacing/structure analysis in research.py.

title: Consent banner auto-dismiss before capture
text: Evaluates 30+ selector patterns for cookie accept/close buttons, clicks matches, waits 400ms, then detects navigation via `performance.timeOrigin` change. If changed or clicks>0, runs `waitForPageReady` (network idle + readyState). Re-runs overlay sweep on new document.
how: Add `dismiss_consent_banners(page)` to any future site-capture utility (e.g., capturing competitor landing pages for reference). Run before scroll tiles and token extraction.

title: Agent-friendly CLI contract: no ANSI, no prompts, clean stdout
text: Tests enforce that in CI/agent mode (CI=1, CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1): stdout/stderr contain no ANSI escape codes, no interactive prompts (regex '\(y/N\)|Yes / No'), no update nags. --help prints plain text. Unknown flags exit 2 with suggestion on stderr only.
how: Audit all studio scripts (ideas.py, scout.py, publish.py) for accidental color libraries, input() calls, or progress bars that leak ANSI. Add a --ci flag that disables them; set CI=1 in cron/GitHub Actions.

title: EPIPE handling as normal teardown, not crash
text: Install error handlers on stdout/stderr that catch EPIPE (code 'EPIPE') and exit cleanly: if render already delivered (artifact validated) exit 0, else exit 1. Prevents 'head -1' or agent pipe close from turning success into crash.
how: In any Python script that writes to stdout (e.g., stats.py, publish.py), wrap sys.stdout.write in try/except BrokenPipeError and sys.exit(0 if render_delivered else 1). Set a global render_delivered flag after video file is finalized.

title: Dotenv loading policy: project .env before browser selection, with opt-out
text: Load .env from CWD early, before any browser/engine initialization. Capture command can opt out via HYPERFRAMES_NO_CAPTURE_DOTENV=1. Provider keys (API tokens) are yielded after load for immediate use.
how: In plan.py and compose.py, add a load_project_env() call at top that reads .env from project root. Allow HYPERFRAMES_NO_DOTENV=1 to skip for specific runs (e.g., CI). Ensure GEMINI_API_KEY, MUSE_COOKIES etc. are loaded before any API client init.

title: Workspace build gate blocks commands until dependencies ready
text: Preview command checks studio workspace build (checkStudioWorkspaceBuild) before importing its module. If missing dist/, prints formatted problems and exits 1 without loading the command. Prevents cryptic import errors.
how: In preflight.py, add a check for required built assets (e.g., HyperFrames dist, Muse browser binary, FFmpeg) before starting render. Print actionable fix commands (e.g., 'bun run build', 'install ffmpeg') and exit 2.

title: Structured pipeline event logging with run IDs
text: Every CLI run gets a runId (UUID). Telemetry events include command, success, exitCode, durationMs, runId. Events are NDJSON, flushed on exit. Enables tracing a video from idea to publish across scripts.
how: Generate a run_id at start of each video pipeline (ideas.py -> research.py -> plan.py -> compose.py -> publish.py). Pass via environment variable or file. Each script appends NDJSON line to events.log with its stage, status, timing.

title: JSON error envelope for machine-readable failures
text: All CLI errors under --json emit a single-line JSON envelope: {ok:false, error:{code:'usage_error'|'runtime_error'|'unknown_command', message:string, hint?:string}}. Non-JSON runs print human text. Exit codes: 2 for usage, 1 for runtime, 0 for success.
how: Modify plan.py, research.py, publish.py, etc. to accept --json flag and output this envelope on error. Update doctor.py and Telegram approval bot to parse it for automated retry/alerting.

title: Exit code sanitization after validated render
text: In finalizeCli(), if isRenderSucceeded() is true, force exitCode=0 regardless of later throws. Telemetry success field uses commandSucceededForTelemetry() which returns true if renderSucceeded OR commandFailed is false. Post-render throws are logged but not scored as failures.
how: In compose.py, after ffmpeg passes review.py checks, write a sentinel file (e.g., .render_ok). In doctor.py and any wrapper, read this sentinel before deciding overall success; ignore subsequent exceptions.

title: Background checks in detached child, main process reads only caches
text: CLI launches update/skills checks via a detached child (launchBackgroundChecks) that refreshes caches. Main process only reads cached results (cachedUpdateCheck) — zero network latency on the critical path. Background child runs independently, next run sees fresh cache.
how: Refactor scout.py (runs twice daily) to write its radar results to a cache file (playbook.md) in a background subprocess (using subprocess.Popen with start_new_session). Main pipeline reads only the cache. Add a --refresh flag to force foreground update.

title: Telemetry flushSync on process exit, not await flush()
text: Register a synchronous process.on('exit') handler that calls flushSync() (non-blocking) to deliver queued events. Avoids awaiting flush() which can hang on EPIPE. Telemetry events include command result, CLI errors, and render success.
how: In stats.py, implement a flush_sync() that writes pending metrics to a local NDJSON file (or sends via UDP). Register atexit handler to call it. Ensure doctor.py and publish.py also flush on exit.

title: Lazy command loading with dynamic imports for fast startup
text: All 50+ commands are loaded via dynamic import() only when invoked. commandLoaders map holds thunks. --version and --help exit before any heavy imports. Reduces cold start from ~80ms to ~10ms.
how: Restructure studio scripts (ideas.py, research.py, etc.) as subcommands under a single CLI entry (e.g., studio.py). Use importlib.import_module lazily. Keep heavy deps (Gemini, yt-dlp) out of the root module.

title: Did-you-mean suggestions for unknown commands and flags
text: On unknown command, CLI suggests closest match (Levenshtein) or redirect map (e.g., 'rendr' -> 'render'). On unknown flag, suggests similar (--out -> --output). Output goes to stderr, exit 2, never full help.
how: Add a simple difflib-based suggestion in studio.py for subcommands and common flags. Print 'Did you mean X?' on stderr. Keep error messages under 8 lines.

title: Aspect-ratio auto-detection from composition HTML
text: Parse the root `<div data-composition-id>` data-width/data-height attributes via regex (tolerance ±0.05) to infer 16:9, 9:16, or 1:1; return structured result (matched/no-match/no-dims) so the render call preserves the authored ratio without a manual flag.
how: Add detectAspectRatioFromHtmlString() to compose.py/compose_lab.py; call before render to set aspect_ratio variable; surface no-match as a warning in preflight.py.

title: Ranged parallel downloads with resume and atomic replacement
text: Split large assets into 8 MB parts, fetch up to 8 parallel ranged GETs; on connection drop, resume from last byte with exponential backoff (250/500/1000 ms); write to a staging file, verify byte count matches content-length, then atomic rename preserving mode; clean staging on abort/error; handle symlinks and existing file preservation.
how: Replace simple fetch in image/video asset download (Muse, FLUX, Pollinations) with downloadToFile(); use in doctor.py for self-repair asset fetches; configure partBytes/connections via env.

title: Atomic file staging with symlink preservation and mode retention
text: Write downloads to a unique staging directory (.hf-download-XXXX); on success, chmod staged file to match previous file's mode (0o777 mask), then renameSync over destination; this preserves existing symlinks (optionally replaceLink to break them), hard links, and read-only files; cleanup staging on any error.
how: Adopt createStagingDir/resolveWritePath pattern in publish.py and thumb.py for all output writes; ensure doctor.py's atomic replacement uses same staging prefix.

title: ANSI-aware visible-length utilities for aligned dashboard logs
text: Strip CSI SGR sequences (including 24-bit truecolor) with regex \u001b\[[\d;]*m; visibleLength() returns printable char count; padEndVisible() pads to target visible width preserving ANSI overhead. Enables clean column alignment in colored CLI output.
how: Integrate into dashboard (Today, Runs, Approvals, Channels) and stats.py report rendering; use for Telegram approval message formatting and 09:00 report alignment.

title: Frame-grid cut snapping
text: Cut video only when the source is constant frame rate: r_frame_rate and avg_frame_rate must agree within 0.01, else keep the whole file. Snap every cut point to the nearest source frame (start x fps must be an integer within 1e-6) and audio cut points to the millisecond; floor seconds to 1e-6 so a cut never rounds past its first frame.
how: In our trim/proxy step, read fps via ffprobe, compute the allowed cut grid, and skip trimming for VFR sources. Add a unit test asserting each planned cut lands on an integer frame index.

title: Bitrate ceiling derived from a byte cap
text: To fit a byte cap with ffmpeg: maxrate = floor((maxBytes x 8 x 0.85 / seconds - audioBitrate) / 1000) kbit/s, applied as both -maxrate and -bufsize. If the result is under 1000 bit/s, apply no limit. For VP9 alpha, constant-quality mode ignores -maxrate, so also pass -b:v with the same value.
how: Before any proxy or upload encode, compute the ceiling from the target cap and the clip's real duration, then assert the output file size is within the cap and fail with the file name and both sizes if not.

title: Media-type-aware re-encode ladder
text: Pick a re-encode preset by probing, not by extension: video -> libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -pix_fmt yuv420p + aac 320k +faststart; audio -> wav pcm_s16le; still -> png; alpha (pix_fmt yuva*/rgba*/argb* or ALPHA_MODE=1) -> libvpx-vp9, since ffmpeg's native VP8/VP9 decoders drop the alpha plane; HDR (color_transfer smpte2084/arib-std-b67) -> libx265 10-bit with -color_primaries/-color_trc/-colorspace. Never flatten an animated image to a still.
how: Use this ladder in our ffmpeg proxy step and any future upload path: probe once with ffprobe, pick the preset, then verify the output's pixel format, colour tags and alpha plane before it enters the render.

title: Re-validate cached uploads with HEAD
text: Key an upload cache by host + SHA-256 of the bytes + the encode variant and cut list, so changing either forces a new encode. Before reusing a cached URL, HEAD it with a 10 s timeout and reuse only if the response is 200 and content-length equals the cached size; on 404, size mismatch, timeout or error, upload again.
how: In our media cache, store size with each entry and add a HEAD check before reuse; treat any mismatch as a miss and overwrite the entry. Keep the cache write atomic so a crash cannot leave a half-written entry.

title: Unicode-normalised path matching
text: Match asset references to files by NFC-normalised path: a page naming media/videéo.mp4 must resolve a file stored decomposed as media/vidéo.mp4, and the reverse. Normalise both the reference and the on-disk name before comparing, and report the path as the page wrote it.
how: In our asset resolver (image/clip fetch and compose), normalise both sides with unicodedata.normalize('NFC') before lookup, and add a test with a decomposed filename so accented Hinglish titles never break a render.

title: Encode a snapshot; abort if the source changed
text: Hash and encode a private snapshot of the staged bytes, never the live file. After the encode or upload, re-check the source's size and mtime; if it changed mid-run, abort with 'changed on disk' and write no cache entry, so stale bytes can never be published under a fresh key.
how: In our media prep step, copy the file to a temp dir before hashing/encoding, then compare size+mtime after; on mismatch, fail the run and skip the cache write. Reuse the same check for render inputs.

title: Trim source clips to the windows actually played
text: Before rendering, compute each source file's played windows from the scene plan (data-start, data-duration, data-media-start, playback-rate), cut only those windows with ffmpeg, and rewrite each clip's data-media-start to its new offset in the trimmed file. Skip trimming when the file is looped, script-named, variable-bound, carries a #t= fragment, or is retimed by script.
how: Add a trim planner before compose/render: read the scene plan's clip windows, produce trimmed mp4s into a cache dir, and patch media-start in the generated HTML so HyperFrames sees the trimmed timeline. Log each trim (source, windows, seconds kept) into the run log.

title: Structured progress events with attempt tracking
text: Emit typed progress events: {phase:'initialize'}, {phase:'upload', percent, sentBytes, totalBytes, attempt}, {phase:'complete'}. Report at most every 10s or 5% gain. Include attempt number (1-based) so dashboard shows restarts. For multipart, aggregate completed parts + live part bytes.
how: Extend stats.py / dashboard to consume these events from upload functions. Add attempt field to existing progress logging in doctor.py and publish.py.

title: Polling with abort signal and size-scaled timeout
text: Poll async jobs (render, generation) every 2s default, max 60min. Accept AbortSignal for Ctrl+C. On each tick, call onTick(detail, elapsedMs). For completion checks that may 409 'still checking', retry with exponential backoff (500ms→5s) up to a budget: 30s base + 500ms per MiB, capped at 10min.
how: Refactor any polling loops (e.g., waiting for Muse/Cloudflare generation, YouTube processing) to use this pattern: injectable sleep/clock, abort signal, per-tick callback, size-aware timeout for finalization steps.

title: Strict CLI flag parsing rejecting trailing garbage
text: Parse integers with regex ^-?\d+$ (reject '10abc', '10.5'), floats with ^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$ (reject '10seconds'), enums against closed set. Enforce min/max bounds. Exit with formatted error box on failure. Return undefined for missing flags so callers set defaults.
how: Apply to studio's CLI entry points (ideas.py, research.py, publish.py args). Replace argparse with custom strict parsers or add validation layer.

title: SHA256 checksum for asset integrity end-to-end
text: Compute SHA256 of file/bytes before upload. Send checksum in createAssetUpload request and again in completeAssetUpload. Server verifies both match uploaded content. For files, stream hash during read to avoid double I/O.
how: Add sha256 computation to asset upload helpers (thumb.py, publish.py). Store checksum in brain.jsonl for deduplication. Verify on download.

title: Idempotent upload initialization with idempotency keys
text: Generate a unique idempotency key per asset (e.g., sha256+size+timestamp) and pass to createAssetUpload. Safe to retry initialization on network errors without creating duplicate assets. Server returns existing asset_id if key matches.
how: When uploading project zips or media to cloud storage, compute key = sha256+size, pass as header/query. Handle 409/422 by reusing returned asset_id.

title: Media fragment (#t=) detection to avoid trim errors
text: If any clip's src URL contains a media fragment (#t=start,end), skip trimming for that source — the fragment already selects a subrange in the uncut file. Treat as unbounded use requiring full file.
how: In compose.py preflight, scan all video/audio src attributes for '#t='. If found, mark source as no-trim and keep full file.

title: Complete upload retry only on 409 with size-scaled budget
text: After PUT, call completeAssetUpload. On 409 'still checking', retry with exponential backoff (500ms→5s) up to budget: 30s + 500ms/MiB, max 10min. Any other error (400, 500) surfaces immediately. Complete is idempotent so retries safe.
how: Apply to any multi-step upload finalization (e.g., after multipart upload to R2, call CompleteMultipartUpload with same retry logic).

title: Multipart resumable upload for large assets
text: For files >16MB, request multipart plan from server (part size, count), save upload plan keyed by SHA256+size to config dir. On restart, list held parts via API, resume only missing parts. Upload up to 3 parts in parallel, each retried independently from its own start. Report progress as completed parts + live part bytes.
how: In publish.py or asset upload helper, implement multipart logic for Cloudflare R2 / S3 uploads: create multipart upload, upload parts with retry, save progress to ~/.studio/uploads/{sha256}-{size}.json, resume on next run.

title: Variable values as mount attributes, not baked into files
text: Pass tuned variable values via data-variable-values attribute on the mount element (single-quoted JSON with escaped quotes). Keeps composition files byte-identical to registry so reinstalls detect edits, and allows multiple mounts of the same block with different values.
how: In plan.py/compose.py, when inserting a block snippet, read variable values from the scene plan and emit them as data-variable-values on the host div instead of rewriting the block file. Update preflight.py to validate attribute presence.

title: Composition ID contract for reliable block mounting
text: Every block composition must declare data-composition-id on its root element (inside <template> if templated). The host snippet must carry the same ID. Lint rule host_missing_composition_id catches mismatches. Without it, the block won't mount at render time.
how: Add a check in preflight.py: for each block reference, verify the installed composition file has a data-composition-id and that the snippet includes it. Fail preflight if missing. Update compose.py to inject the ID when generating snippets.

title: Tag-based bulk install for category-driven workflows
text: Registry items carry tags. CLI add <tag> installs all blocks with that tag (e.g., html-in-canvas, captions). Resolves each item with dependencies, installs sequentially, aggregates results. Fails individual items but continues others; reports summary.
how: In scout.py/playbook.md, tag blocks by style (lab, classic, mythology). Add a bulk-install step in ideas.py or a new setup script: hyperframes add lab-look --json. Use for new project bootstrap or style refresh.

title: Transitive registry dependency resolution with topological install order
text: When installing a block, recursively resolve registryDependencies, topologically sort (dependencies first), compatibility-gate all items before any write, then install in order. Roll back all listed files on any failure. Track each installed item with requested flag for telemetry.
how: Extend scout.py/playbook.md to declare block dependencies. In doctor.py or a new install step, implement resolveItemWithDependencies equivalent. Before rendering, run compatibility gate (CLI version vs minCliVersion). Use receivedWrites pattern to list files before write and undo on failure.

title: Received-files ledger for provenance and safe publishing
text: Maintain .hyperframes/received-files.json listing every file written by registry installs (including dependencies). On failed install, undo only files that were listed but not actually written. On re-install, preserve files the user edited (detected by content diff). Excludes user's own config and public-registry installs.
how: Add a received-files.jsonl in each project dir. In compose.py/render pipeline, record every written asset path. In doctor.py, compare ledger vs disk to detect drift. In publish.py, filter out _ext/ files that match ledger entries (external assets).

title: Compatibility gate before any filesystem writes
text: Gate all resolved items (including transitive deps) against current CLI version via minCliVersion in registry item. If any item requires newer CLI, throw before writing a single file. Collects non-fatal warnings (deprecation notices) from all items.
how: Add a version check in doctor.py or pre-render step: read hyperframes.json registry items' minCliVersion, compare with studio's HyperFrames version. Abort with clear message if incompatible. Surface deprecation warnings in dashboard.

title: Force vs preserve edited files on re-install
text: Default behavior preserves files that differ from registry content (user edits). --force overwrites. On re-install, diff installed file vs registry source; if changed, add to preserved list and skip write unless --force. Report preserved files with relative paths.
how: In compose.py or a new sync step, before writing a block/component, compute hash of existing file vs registry source. If different and not --force, log as preserved. Add --force flag to render pipeline for CI updates.

title: JSON output for CLI automation and CI integration
text: All commands support --json flag emitting structured summary: ok, installed[], warnings[], errors[], snippet, written[], preserved[], variablesApplied[]. Tag installs and multi-name installs aggregate results. Enables programmatic parsing in CI/CD.
how: Add --json to publish.py, stats.py, doctor.py. In GitHub Actions / Cloudflare Workers, parse JSON to decide next steps (e.g., fail build on errors, post snippet to Telegram). Update dashboard to ingest JSON logs.

title: Auth credential rollback on verification failure
text: On login, write new credential, then verify via /v3/users/me. If verification fails (reject or empty identity), roll back to previous credential (including user block). Preserves foreign top-level keys (cross-CLI compatibility). Telemetry tracks success/failure with user ID.
how: In doctor.py or a new auth module, apply same pattern for API keys (Gemini, Muse, Cloudflare): write candidate, verify with a test call, rollback on failure. Keep previous working keys. Log to brain.jsonl with provider and status.

title: Offline engine fallback guidance with readiness probes
text: `status-guidance.ts` shows interactive users a table of local engines (Kokoro voice, MusicGen music) with ready/missing status and exact `pip install` hints. Non-interactive/CI gets a terse `HEYGEN_API_KEY` + fallback line. Agent mode asks the human to run `auth login`.
how: Adapt for `voice_gate.py` and `music` selection: when cloud TTS/BGM fails or keys missing, print a similar table from `resolveVoice()/resolveMusic()` (already in brain) with `doctor.py` install hints. Keeps pipeline running offline without silent failures.

title: Atomic manifest writes with per-row progress
text: The batch manifest is written atomically via `replaceFileAtomically` after every row start/completion/failure. Each row gets `startedAt`, `completedAt`, `renderTimeMs`, `reference_background`, and `error`. Manifest path is derived from the common output directory.
how: Modify `doctor.py` and `render.py` to write a `render_manifest.json` atomically after each scene/chunk. Include `reference_background` (already tracked) and `renderTimeMs`. Enables resume, debugging, and `stats.py` without parsing logs.

title: Device authorization flow for headless/CI servers
text: `auth login --device` uses OAuth 2.0 device code flow: prints a verification URL and user code, polls for approval. Explicitly disabled in CI (`isCI()` check). Tokens are revoked on verification failure. No browser needed on the server.
how: Add `hyperframes auth login --device` to the server setup docs for the render workers. Use when setting up new Cloudflare/Modal/GCP runners where a browser isn't available. Store the resulting OAuth tokens in the credential file for `publish.py` API calls.

title: HTML source discovery for music element (priority, muted, roles)
text: The beat analyzer finds the music track by parsing the composition HTML: prefers `#music` element, then `data-timeline-role=music`, ignores `muted` videos and `voiceover` roles, prefers local child sources over remote, handles uppercase tags/attributes, skips comments/scripts.
how: Reuse this logic in `compose_lab.py`/`mix.py` to auto-detect the music `<audio>` element for beat analysis and loudness metering. Avoids hardcoding `id=music`; respects `data-timeline-role` and `muted`.

title: Beat-synced cuts via CLI beat analysis
text: The `beats` command analyses audio (WAV/MP4) and writes a JSON file with beat times and strengths (0–1). It rejects ambience-only tracks, requires ≥2 beats and ≥50% heard, and outputs a standard format the renderer can consume for frame-accurate cut points.
how: Add a `beats.py` step after `mix.py` mastering: run `hyperframes beats <project>` on the mixed music bed, parse the JSON, and feed beat times to `compose_lab.py` for `speed ramps for beat-synced cuts` (already in brain). Use `--json` for machine parsing.

title: Telemetry identity stitching across anonymous and authenticated sessions
text: On successful login, `telemetryIdentity(user)` returns a `distinctId` and traits. `identifyUser()` is called before `trackAuthLoginCompleted`, stitching prior anonymous usage to the identified account. Works under opt-out.
how: Add a lightweight telemetry module to `dashboard.py`/`stats.py`: generate a local `machine_id` on first run, send anonymous events (render duration, success/failure). On `auth login` (if added for HeyGen), call `identify` to link history. Respects `TELEMETRY=off`.

title: Capture output never merges
text: When a capture directory already exists, write to capture-2, capture-3 ... up to capture-99 instead of reusing or merging the old folder; if all are taken, stop and ask for an explicit output name. This keeps a re-run's screenshots, assets and manifests from silently mixing with a previous capture's files.
how: In our site-capture step, resolve the output dir with the same suffix loop before any write, and record the chosen directory in the run log so later steps (asset catalog, design tokens) read the fresh manifest rather than a stale one.

title: Versioned phase events without URLs
text: Report capture/render progress as one-line JSON phase records on stderr: {schema, phase, status, remainingMs, reason}, with phase from a fixed enum (browser, navigate, extract, tokens, screenshots, assets, style, done) and status ok/degraded. Never put the captured URL or path in the record: URLs often carry tokens, and a degraded phase still needs to report the remaining budget.
how: In scout/capture logging, print one JSON line per phase with a fixed schema field and phase enum, strip query strings from any URL we log, and keep degraded phases visible so a partial capture is not mistaken for a complete one.

title: Progress UI must die with the process
text: A live progress spinner keeps the event loop alive, so a failed command can hang forever instead of exiting. Every exit path - success, thrown error, abort - must stop the spinner, and the failure path must print the normalised error before exiting non-zero. Test it: after a forced failure the process must exit within a few seconds.
how: In our render/doctor workers, wrap progress output in try/finally so the spinner or heartbeat is always cleared, and add a test that injects a render failure and asserts the worker exits within 5 seconds with a non-zero code.

title: Gap-report command baked into search envelope
text: Every search result (JSON or terminal) includes a ready-to-paste `feedback --search-miss` command with the query and tier. Shell metacharacters are escaped; non-ASCII queries preserved. Only omitted when query has no searchable tokens.
how: In ideas.py when scoring yields <3 viable ideas, auto-generate a Telegram message: 'No strong ideas for "{topic}". Report gap: npx hyperframes feedback --search-miss "{topic}" --wanted "<angle>" --tier words'.

title: Source dimensions vs display dimensions in manifest
text: Manifest stores both width/height (display box) and sourceWidth/sourceHeight (intrinsic video resolution). Downloader prints source dims; composition snippet uses source dims for aspect logic.
how: When Muse/FLUX returns video metadata, store intrinsic resolution separately from composition box size. Use intrinsic for Ken Burns zoom limits and aspect-ratio decisions in compose.py.

title: Consent model: record answer, survive concurrent runs, fail loudly on write error
text: localModelStatus reads last saved consent; assumeLocalModelConsent/recordLocalModelConsent handle race where another process saves 'no' during install. If write fails, warn and do not overwrite memory state.
how: For any future on-device model (e.g., local LLM for hook generation), store consent in brain.jsonl with atomic write; on startup read last value; if write fails, log warning and keep previous consent in memory.

title: Manifest-driven asset selection with collision guard
text: Video manifest stores index, URL, filename, sourceWidth/Height, heading, caption. pickManifestEntry resolves by index or URL; findFilenameCollision prevents two entries mapping to same safe filename (URL-encoded variants).
how: Extend our brain.jsonl or a new assets manifest to include source dimensions and captions; before downloading any clip, check for filename collisions across the manifest and refuse if found.

title: Two-tier search with consent-gated semantic model
text: Word-match tier (always on) ranks by shared vocabulary; on-device semantic tier (33 MB model) requires explicit consent. Consent is recorded, survives restarts, and can be revoked. Unattended runs get a JSON hint instead of a prompt.
how: For our ideas.py/research.py topic search: keep keyword scoring as tier 1; add optional local embedding model (e.g., sentence-transformers ONNX) as tier 2 behind a one-time Telegram consent; store consent in brain.jsonl; show 'run with --semantic' hint in JSON when tier 1 returns thin results.

title: Append-only project history with seen-pointer catch-up
text: Each app turn (ask/did/files) appended as JSONL. catch-up reads turns after last seen timestamp, prints human-readable log, updates seen pointer to newest turn shown. Control chars in file names/history escaped as \xXX.
how: Add .hyperframes/history.jsonl to each project; plan.py and compose.py append turn records; new CLI command `studio catch-up` shows what changed since last run; Telegram bot can push daily digest.

title: JSON envelope with tier, unindexed count, and warnings
text: Catalog --json returns {query, tier, tier_detail, dropped, unindexed, top_score, shown, total, warnings, report_gap, results[]}. unindexed = registry items missing from vector index (stale artifact). warnings carry consent/model errors.
how: Make ideas.py --json output include tier (keyword vs semantic), unindexed count (topics not in our trend DB), top_score, and a gap-report command. doctor.py can alert when unindexed > threshold.

title: Control-character escaping for terminal-safe logs
text: All user-supplied strings (file names, history text) passed through terminalText() which replaces control chars with \xXX escapes. ANSI color codes stripped in test assertions.
how: Add terminalText utility to our logger; apply to every console.log in plan.py, compose.py, review.py so Telegram logs and dashboard never contain raw escape sequences.

title: Finding crops for visual debugging
text: Auto-generate cropped PNGs around each layout finding (bbox + padding) named finding-NN-<code>.png. Attach to check report for quick Telegram review without full video.
how: In review.py, after vision review, use ffmpeg to crop finding frames from rendered MP4 using bbox + 10% padding. Save to artifacts/findings/. Include in Telegram approval message.

title: Contrast sampling strategy
text: Sample WCAG AA contrast at 5 evenly distributed times including first and last layout sample (e.g., 0.5, 2.5, 4.5, 6.5, 8.5s for 9 samples). Reduces browser captures while covering full duration.
how: Modify preflight.py's contrast pass to call selectContrastTimes(layoutSamples) instead of checking every sample. Reuse existing Gemini vision for contrast judgment.

title: Transition-boundary sampling
text: Optionally sample at every tween start/end boundary plus segment midpoints to catch transient overlaps at transition seams. Capped by --max-transition-samples with dropped count reported.
how: In plan.py/scene planner, emit transition boundaries. In preflight.py, add atTransitions flag; merge with regular samples, deduplicate, cap. Use existing GSAP label API.

title: Audio source readability check
text: Inspect each audio element: unreadable (corrupt/unsupported codec), silent (no audible content), or missing. Report as findings with severity (error for unreadable, info for silent). Runs even if browser lint fails.
how: Add inspectAudio step in preflight.py using ffprobe/ffmpeg via Python subprocess. Parse duration, codec, loudness. Integrate with existing audio pipeline (mix.py).

title: Check caching with content-addressed keys
text: Cache full check result keyed by project hash, check options, CLI version, and browser identity. Return cached pass instantly if nothing changed. Invalidate on any file/option change.
how: Implement checkCacheKey in doctor.py/preflight.py: hash index.html + composed assets + options JSON + hyperframes version + Chrome version. Store/load from .hyperframes/cache/checks/.

title: Unattended destructive ops need explicit opt-in
text: Never auto-bypass a destructive confirmation because the process is unattended or because --json was passed. In non-interactive runs require an explicit opt-in flag (e.g. --no-confirm) and fail with a message telling the caller how to acknowledge it. A declined prompt and an API/system error should get different exit codes.
how: In doctor.py's auto-repair (deleting held videos, clearing stale jobs) and publish.py's auto-approve path, require an explicit --force/--yes flag when triggered by cron or Telegram; otherwise log 'needs explicit approval' and leave the item untouched. Use distinct exit codes for 'declined' vs 'failed'.

title: Owner-stamped render dirs with liveness check
text: Each render writes owner.json (pid + machine stamp) into its work dir. A cleanup sweep deletes a dir only when its owner pid is dead; a dir with no owner record counts as abandoned only after 6 h idle. Live renders (pid alive) and user-named folders such as work-in-progress are never touched. Report bytes reclaimed per dir and support a dry-run that removes nothing.
how: At render start write renders/<job>/owner.json with the pid; delete it on success. Add a doctor.py sweep (every 10 min) that lists dead-pid dirs and ownerless dirs idle >6 h, logs bytes, and only deletes after a dry-run report shows no live pid.

title: Symlink-safe recursive delete guard
text: Before any recursive delete, realpath the target and the allowed parent, then require relative(allowed, target) to be neither absolute nor starting with '..'. If the target resolves outside the allowed folder (e.g. a symlinked .hyperframes/artifacts dir), skip it instead of deleting. Applies to snapshots/, artifacts/{snapshots,checks}, render dirs and temp caches.
how: Add a delete_under(parent, target) helper in doctor.py and route every rm -rf of render dirs, snapshots, caches and held videos through it. Log 'skipped: resolves outside parent' with both realpaths so a misconfigured path is visible instead of silently deleting user files.

title: Fail-soft sweep with error ledger
text: Wrap each cleanup step in its own try/catch: one locked or unreadable directory must not abort the rest of the sweep. Collect per-step error strings, keep going, and exit non-zero if any error occurred. An unreadable history folder still allows other leftovers to be reclaimed, and the report lists both what was removed and what failed.
how: In doctor.py's disk-clean step, run each sweep (render dirs, proxies, snapshots, extract cache) through an attempt() wrapper that records errors and continues. Emit one JSON line per error and mark the run 'degraded' so the Telegram/dashboard shows partial failure.

title: Composition-scoped missing-asset check
text: Validate missing assets only against the page actually being rendered, not the whole project: a missing image referenced by index.html must not fail a render of alternate.html that never plays it. The error must name the exact missing path and the composition that references it.
how: In preflight.py, parse the selected composition HTML for src/href references and check only those against the asset manifest; keep the project-wide scan as a separate warning. This removes false 'missing asset' failures that currently block otherwise good renders.

title: Outside-project reference blocklist
text: When packaging a project, any reference escaping the project root is excluded by default and reported per file with a reason: 'received' (came in with an imported project), 'blocklisted' (secret-like name such as .env), 'file_type' (not an allowed asset type) or 'not_approved'. Inclusion requires an explicit opt-in flag; each exclusion is also emitted as a machine-readable event.
how: In the asset-packaging step of compose/preflight, resolve every src/href to a real path, flag any that leaves the project dir and print one line per file with its reason. Never auto-include; require an explicit --include-outside-files equivalent and log exclusions to the run log.

title: 60-second render heartbeat
text: While a long render holds the same status, emit one heartbeat line every 60 s (status, elapsed seconds, job id) so a slow render never reads as a hang; log immediately on any status change. Re-encode progress is emitted once per whole percent, or once per second when the total duration is unknown.
how: In the render worker wrap the wait loop with a 60 s timer that writes a structured heartbeat event to the run log and the dashboard Runs panel, plus an immediate log on status change. Apply the same per-percent/per-second rule to any ffmpeg re-encode step.

title: Polling with progress reporting and resume
text: Poll render status every 2s (configurable), max 60 min. On TTY, single-line carriage-return updates; on CI, one line per status change + heartbeat every 60s. Timeout yields resume command: `hyperframes cloud get <render_id>`.
how: Enhance doctor.py's 10-min check: for active cloud renders, poll with same logic. Add --poll-interval and --max-wait to publish.py. Store render_id in brain.jsonl for resume after crash.

title: Direct-to-S3 upload with presigned URLs
text: Upload project zips up to 200 MB via three-step direct upload: POST /v3/assets/direct-uploads → PUT to presigned S3 URL → POST /v3/assets/{id}/complete. Avoids API proxy limits and streams large archives reliably.
how: Add cloud_upload.py using the same three-step contract. Replace any multipart API upload in publish.py with this flow; reuse .hyperframesignore for file filtering. Handle 200 MB cap and 95% zip budget.

title: Variable validation against declared schema
text: Extract data-composition-variables JSON from entry HTML; validate --variables keys and types before upload. Strict mode fails on undeclared/mistyped variables; lenient mode warns. Prevents render-time errors.
how: Create validate_variables.py: parse index.html (or --composition entry), compare with variables dict. Call from plan.py after script generation, before render. Add --strict-variables flag.

title: Offload heavy media to cloud assets
text: Files larger than OFFLOAD_MIN_BYTES (default 5 MB) are uploaded to cloud asset store via direct upload, replaced in zip with asset references. Cached by content hash; re-encodes video to target codec. Keeps zip under 200 MB limit.
how: In compose.py, after gathering media, call offload_heavy_media(project_dir, file_map, entry_path). Use Cloudflare FLUX or HeyGen assets as backend. Update zipPublishFileMap to include only references.

title: Idempotency keys for safe render retries
text: Generate a deterministic idempotency key (1-255 chars, [A-Za-z0-9_:.-]) per render job — e.g., SHA256 of project hash + variables. Pass to upload and render submit endpoints; server deduplicates retries within 24h.
how: In publish.py, compute key = hashlib.sha256(f'{project_hash}{variables_json}').hexdigest()[:64]. Pass as Idempotency-Key header to cloud upload and render APIs. Store in brain.jsonl for traceability.

title: Webhook callback for fire-and-forget rendering
text: Support --callback-url (HTTPS) and --callback-id; webhook fires on render termination regardless of CLI polling. Combine with --no-wait to submit and exit immediately. Enables async Telegram notification.
how: Add callback_url, callback_id to render submit payload. In publish.py, when auto-approve score passes, call render with --no-wait --callback-url pointing to our webhook endpoint that posts to Telegram approval channel.

title: SVG gradient text contrast uses weakest gradient stop
text: For SVG <text> with fill=url(#gradient), the rendered color varies across glyphs. The audit resolves the gradient's stop colors (following href chains), parses stop-color/stop-opacity, and judges contrast against the weakest (lowest contrast) stop. Pattern fills (url(#pattern)) are skipped — no single color to judge. Borrowed gradients via href are resolved recursively (max 8 hops).
how: If we ever use SVG text with gradients (e.g., kinetic titles with gradient fill), apply same rule: compute contrast per stop, take minimum. Our current caption system uses HTML/CSS, but lab look kinetic titles could use SVG. Add gradient-stop parsing to contrast audit.

title: Occlusion-aware contrast: skip only when fully covered
text: Elements with data-layout-allow-occlusion are allowed to sit behind other layers. The audit probes 5×3 grid points (5%,25%,50%,75%,95% × 25%,50%,75%) via elementsFromPoint. If ANY probe reaches the text element (or its transparent composition hosts), it audits contrast normally. Only when ALL probes hit an occluder is the element skipped. Transparent composition hosts (data-composition-id, data-hf-inner-root) are walked through; opaque hosts block.
how: Mark our caption containers with data-layout-allow-occlusion when they intentionally sit behind glass panels or UI overlays. Ensure composition host divs are transparent (no background) so audit walks through. This prevents false failures on layered lab-look scenes.

title: Sub-composition path resolution ignores network shares
text: When data-composition-src points to a UNC path (//host/share, \\host\share, \\?\UNC\...), the parser never touches the filesystem — it treats it as external and leaves source undefined. Only relative paths inside the project are resolved and read. This prevents hangs on unavailable shares and keeps project portable.
how: In our asset-resolution (resolveCompositionSrc), adopt same guard: if src starts with //, \\, or \\?\UNC, treat as external and skip local read. Our compositions are local, but this hardens against accidental absolute paths.

title: Composition inventory CLI
text: Command lists all [data-composition-id] elements in project index.html with duration (resolves declared, clip ends, script estimates), resolution, element count, and sub-composition source. Outputs human table or JSON. Handles external sub-compositions via resolveCompositionSrc, template-wrapped subs, and duration derivation from GSAP timeline durations in scripts.
how: Add hyperframes compositions --json to doctor.py or a new inventory step to validate project structure before render. Use duration/resolution to catch mismatches early. Feed JSON into dashboard for project overview.

title: Telemetry join keys link feedback to render IDs and check results
text: buildTelemetryJoinKeys creates `fid=feedback-uuid tid=install-uuid renders=render-a,render-b! check=exit1:text_overlap*4,contrast_low*1 check_age=13m`. Recent renders newest-last, `!` suffix = failed. Last check includes exit code, top error codes (truncated 24 chars), minutes since check. Fits <400 chars for env cap.
how: In stats.py, when logging feedback or approvals, append join keys to results.md. In review.py, include last check exit code and top error codes. In Telegram approval message, show `renders=...` so we can jump to exact render job.

title: Structured feedback with repro publishing and consent gate
text: feedback.ts accepts rating (0-10) or comment-only (missing feature). Person vs agent source (email only from HYPERFRAMES_FEEDBACK_EMAIL env, never in telemetry). --file-issue publishes minimal repro (stages project, approves outside files, uploads to public URL), opens pre-filled GitHub issue. Soft lint warnings for missing reproduction packet markers (REPRO COMMAND, EXPECTED/ACTUAL, EXACT ERROR, OUTCOME, WORKAROUND). Ack before async submit.
how: In Telegram approval flow, when owner reports issue, run `hyperframes feedback --rating 3 --comment "..." --file-issue --yes` to auto-publish repro and create GitHub issue. Add lint warnings to our playbook.md for bug reports. Store feedbackId in brain.jsonl for traceability.

title: Skill documentation contracts enforce reproduction packets
text: Tests enforce: hyperframes-cli skill teaches actionable reproduction packets (REPRO COMMAND, EXPECTED/ACTUAL, EXACT ERROR, OUTCOME, WORKAROUND). Mandates COMPOSITION_STRUCTURE block for visual defects (elements: video=, attributes:, timeline:, buildCompositionCensus pointer). Cloud archive size remediation: `cloud render --dry-run --json`, never ignore large assets, .hyperframesignore with dynamic paths.
how: Add reproduction packet template to our playbook.md. In preflight.py vision review failures, require COMPOSITION_STRUCTURE block. For large asset uploads, add dry-run check and .hyperframesignore equivalent.

title: Docs command with markdown rendering and topic registry
text: docs.ts renders markdown in terminal: H1 bold, H2 dim bold, list items with bullet, inline code accent-colored. Topics registry includes motion-blur, audio, transcribe, compositions, gsap, rendering, data-attributes, examples, troubleshooting. Tests ensure every topic has a file and examples.md lists all registry examples.
how: Add `hyperframes docs` equivalent to our CLI for quick reference. Keep our playbook.md in sync with a topic registry. Use same markdown rendering for Telegram help messages.

title: Frame-accurate video diff with SSIM, cuts, person gates
text: diff.ts compares reference vs render frame-by-frame: mean SSIM, p05, worst 4x4 cell; detects missing content/texture spans; matches cuts; measures duration/sound offset; scores person framing, text carry, lipsync lag; scores drawn elements (offset, ink ratio); computes layer benefit per frame. Outputs human + JSON, side-by-side video, contact sheet.
how: Integrate into review.py after render: call `hyperframes diff original.mp4 render.mp4 --json --segments segments.md --sbs --out .hyperframes/diff`. Parse JSON for pass/fail, worst moments, person gates. Use contact sheet for vision review. Add thresholds to preflight.py.

title: Docker detection skips project-local binaries
text: checkDocker finds docker via findTrustedExecutable (PATH outside project). If only found in project's node_modules/.bin, reports Not found with hint: skipped path, 'CLI only runs helper programs from folders outside the project', and install URL. Prevents using project-local docker that may be wrong version.
how: In doctor.py, when checking Docker, replicate logic: search PATH excluding project folder. If only project-local found, warn and treat as missing. Add to our render worker health check.

title: Deprecation test harness for CLI commands
text: deprecationTestHarness.ts provides shared mocks (fakeCdpSession, resolveProjectMock, bundleToSingleHtmlFailureMock, lintProjectFailureMock) and helpers (runAndCaptureStdio, runAndFindJsonLogCall, runAndParseJsonEnvelope) so inspect/validate/layout tests assert shared deprecation envelope (stderr notice, JSON _meta.deprecated) without real project/Chrome.
how: Create similar test harness for our CLI commands (plan.py, compose.py, render.py) to test deprecation warnings and JSON error envelopes. Use in CI to catch breaking changes.

title: TTS documentation accuracy gates
text: Tests ensure tts.md and tts-to-captions.md do not advertise unsupported flags (--provider, --words) and reference heygen-tts.mjs. Prevents docs drift from actual CLI capabilities.
how: Add test in our pipeline: grep our TTS docs for flags not in actual TTS command (Gemini TTS). Fail CI if mismatch. Ensure voice gate docs match voice_gate.py implementation.

title: Rasterize fallback: SVG → PNG retry then placeholder
text: Component import tries SVG render; on RENDER_FAILED retries once as PNG; if both fail, leaves placeholder with data-figma-rasterize marker (no src) so gap is visible. One bad node doesn't abort whole import.
how: In visual generation, when a clip/image fails (Muse timeout, FLUX error), retry with a simpler prompt or lower resolution, then insert a branded placeholder card with error code instead of crashing the render. Log the gap for review.py.

title: Structured telemetry with phase and reuse flags
text: Each import command tracks {phase: 'asset'|'component'|'tokens', reused: boolean, durationMs, entryCount, unresolvedBindings, rasterizeFailures}. Enables funnel analysis (first-run NO_TOKEN → success).
how: Extend stats.py's telemetry to include phase (idea, script, voice, visual, edit, publish), reuse/cache-hit flags, and error codes. Send to a local JSONL + Telegram 09:00 report. Tag each video run with a runId.

title: Token import with enterprise fallback to styles metadata
text: Figma variables require Enterprise; on REQUIRES_ENTERPRISE they fall back to published styles metadata (names, types) — values resolve later at component import. Never fails silently.
how: When using external design systems (Brandfetch, Figma, Canva APIs), implement tiered fallback: primary API → public metadata → local defaults. Log which tier was used. Apply to our thumbnail brand kit fetching.

title: Batched render API calls with single request
text: Batch multiple node renders into one Figma /v1/images call (renderNodes) instead of N individual calls; the code collects missIndexes, calls renderNodes once with all nodeIds, then maps results back. Cuts API latency and respects rate limits.
how: In compose.py/compose_lab.py, when generating multiple similar visual elements (charts, cards, panels), batch their generation prompts or render calls into a single API request where the provider supports it (e.g., Muse batch, FLUX batch). Add a batching layer in the render step.

title: SVG sanitization before freeze
text: On SVG download, they sniff first byte (<, ?, BOM) then decode, strip <script> and event handlers, re-encode. Prevents XSS in downstream HTML compositions.
how: In compose_lab.py when using SVG assets (icons, charts from Muse/FLUX), add a sanitizeSvg pass before writing to .media/. Use a small allowlist of tags/attrs (svg, path, rect, circle, fill, stroke).

title: Grade comparison sheet for color grading QA
text: CLI renders a grid of candidate grades/LUTs on a reference frame (with optional 'original' baseline cell), outputs a single PNG comparison sheet. Caps at 16 cells, warns on truncation, handles JPEG orientation via sharp.
how: Build a grade-compare.py tool for our color grading: feed a reference frame + list of LUTs/presets → render grid sheet → review in Telegram approval. Integrate with mix.py's color grading step. Use 9:16 cells for Shorts.

title: Safe index regeneration in finally block
text: After batch asset import, index.md regenerates in a finally block so partial successes still update the index; failures don't leave it stale.
how: In publish.py and stats.py, move results.md/index.md regeneration into a try/finally around the main loop. Ensures dashboard always reflects completed items even if later items fail.

title: Content-length pre-check before buffering download
text: downloadRender checks Content-Length header against MAX_FREEZE_BYTES cap before reading body; rejects oversized responses early.
how: In mix.py (music/SFX download) and visual asset fetch, add a HEAD request or stream check for content-length > cap (e.g., 50MB) before downloading full body. Saves bandwidth and disk on bad URLs.

title: Deterministic asset IDs via nextId with type prefix
text: nextId(projectDir, 'image') yields image_001, image_002… based on existing manifest entries. Guarantees no collisions and stable ordering.
how: Replace ad-hoc UUIDs in our pipeline (visuals, audio, scripts) with a deterministic nextId(type) that scans manifest.jsonl for highest suffix. Use in compose.py, plan.py, voice gate for reproducible filenames.

title: Byte-bounded slug for render directories
text: Filesystem folder names cap at 255 bytes, not characters. Devanagari and emoji titles cost up to 4 bytes per character, so a 100-character Hinglish title can exceed the limit. Cap generated slugs at 80 characters and 200 UTF-8 bytes, and validate the length before creating any file.
how: In the render-dir naming step, slug the title, then check Buffer.byteLength(slug,'utf8') <= 200 and length <= 80; truncate on grapheme boundaries and append a short hash to keep names unique. Reject with a clear message instead of a raw ENAMETOOLONG.

title: Transactional multi-file rollback for composition rewrites
text: Treat a stage that rewrites several files as one turn. Record the pre-change bytes of every file it touches; if any part fails, restore all recorded files (redoing parts already applied) so the project is never half-updated. Undo must be all-or-nothing: on a conflict, parts already undone are put back before refusing.
how: In compose.py and doctor.py, wrap multi-file patches in a turn: snapshot each target file's bytes before writing, then on exception restore every snapshot and re-raise. Add a test that injects a failure on the second of three writes and asserts final bytes equal the pre-run bytes.

title: Composition metadata preflight: expected vs actual duration
text: Read the root composition's data-duration; if absent, compute max(start + duration) over all elements. Compare with the duration plan.py expects and fail preflight when the gap exceeds 0.5 s or 2%. Also report resolution, element count and track count. Parse with a DOM parser so commented-out or script-string markup is ignored.
how: In preflight.py, parse index.html with DOMParser, find the root by data-composition-id, and compare its duration to the sum of scene durations in the plan. Emit a structured code such as DURATION_MISMATCH that doctor.py can act on automatically.

title: Same-inode guard before writing derived media
text: Before ffmpeg writes an output next to its input, compare device+inode (and realpath) of source and destination. If they are the same file — via hard link, symlink or aliased folder — write to a suffixed name (original.h264.mp4, then original.h264-2.mp4) so the source bytes and codec stay intact.
how: In the trim/transcode helpers used by preflight and mix.py, stat both paths before running ffmpeg; if dev+ino match, pick the next free suffixed output name and record it in the manifest. Test with a hard link and with a symlinked folder alias.

title: Exclusive single-writer claim per project
text: Only one writer may mutate a project at a time. A claim is exclusive: a second concurrent claim is refused with the holder's name and exit code 2, not queued silently. A claim left open is released after an idle window (60 s), so a crashed writer cannot block the project forever.
how: Add a lock file with owner pid and last-write timestamp to the project dir; compose.py and doctor.py claim it before writing while render only reads. Reclaim a crashed run's lock after 60 s of no writes and log refusals as structured pipeline events.

title: Regex-based Resolution Presets
text: Instead of heavy DOM parsing, use regex to patch canvas dimensions (data-width, data-height) and CSS/viewport tags in HTML templates. This preserves template indentation and comments while ensuring byte-for-byte accuracy.
how: Replace our current manual layout adjustments with a regex-based patcher in compose.py that targets data-attributes and CSS blocks.

title: Hierarchical Duration Resolution
text: When probing media, use a fallback hierarchy for duration: stream duration -> frame count/fps -> format duration. This prevents render failures when one metadata source is missing or unreliable.
how: Update our probe logic to use this fallback chain when calculating the duration for the composition manifest.

title: Project Scaffolding CLI
text: Implement an 'init' command that standardizes project structure, including package.json, template injection, and hyperframes.json configuration. This ensures consistency across all studio projects and simplifies onboarding new templates.
how: Create a new CLI command that copies template directories and injects dynamic metadata (name, resolution) into index.html files.

title: Media Placeholder Patching
text: Automate the injection of media (A-roll, audio) into HTML templates by replacing placeholders (e.g., __VIDEO_SRC__, __VIDEO_DURATION__) at runtime. This allows for cleaner, template-agnostic HTML files.
how: Implement a patcher in the render pipeline that replaces placeholders in HTML before the browser render phase.

title: GSAP Timeline Surface Analysis
text: Analyze GSAP timelines to extract tween start/end times, staggers, and durations. This allows for automated detection of unresolved timing issues, infinite repeats, or stagger-related duration errors before rendering.
how: Add a pre-render step that parses the GSAP script in the HTML to validate timeline consistency and predict total composition duration.

title: CSS @keyframes comment-stripping before selector parsing
text: CSS comments before @keyframes leak into next rule's selector if not stripped. Strip all /* ... */ comments upfront, then parse @keyframes blocks, then parse animation-name/animation shorthand on remaining rules. Prevents corrupted selector matching for --shot onion-skin.
how: In thumb.py/cover generation, when parsing CSS for animation triggers, pre-process with stripCssComments(css) before collectKeyframeBlocks(). Ensures @keyframes rise {..} .dot {animation: rise} maps correctly even with /* Grain animation */ comment above.

title: Anime.js registration detection via __hfAnime push
text: Anime.js timelines/animations are only surfaced if registered via window.__hfAnime.push(timeline) or window.__hfAnime = [...]. Unregistered calls are ignored. Targets parsed from .add(selector) and targets/duration properties. Use as onion-shot candidates alongside GSAP/CSS.
how: In scout.py/playbook.md, document that Anime.js scenes must register with window.__hfAnime.push(tl) for preflight detection. Add check in preflight.py: if anime calls found but __hfAnime not pushed, warn 'Anime.js timeline unregistered — onion-skin will miss it'.

title: Multi-stroke trace compositing with pen-up detection
text: Composite ≥2 drawn position strokes on one element into a single trace; treat 0-duration set() as pen-up jumps (excluded from strokes). Only targets with ≥2 strokes become traces; single strokes stay as normal tweens. Path travel threshold: 0.5px on x or y to count as a drawn stroke.
how: In compose_lab.py preflight, add trace grouping to surfaceComposition(): filter tweens with isDrawnStroke (method≠set, has path, pathTravels >0.5px), group by target, sort by start time, emit SurfacedTrace for targets with ≥2 strokes. Use in review.py to visualize complex paths (e.g., kinetic title underline + panel slide).

title: Template-fragment traversal for sub-composition motion extraction
text: Sub-compositions wrap markup+script+style in <template> (inert DocumentFragment). querySelectorAll doesn't traverse templates. Must walk document + every template.content (including nested templates) to find elements and inline scripts/styles. Order: document matches first, then template contents in discovery order.
how: In compose.py/compose_lab.py, replace document.querySelectorAll with compositionRoots(html).flatMap(root => root.querySelectorAll(selector)). Update inlineScriptText/inlineStyleText to query templates. Ensures scout.py/preflight.py catch motion in template-wrapped scenes (Puraan Ki Katha myth cards, Kaise Tech lab panels).

title: Onion-skin screenshot for 3D motion self-verification
text: Capture real element over timeline at equal-time steps (default 9 samples) as PNG: 'path' layout shows ghost markers at real positions + vector path; 'strip' layout captures true per-time pixel filmstrip ONLY for SVG targets, else falls back to one live frame + vector markers. Orbit camera presets (front/iso/top/side/rear-iso) or yaw,pitch degrees. Ghost mode composites translucent canvas/WebGL frames (older fainter).
how: Add --shot flag to review.py: render composition with HyperFrames, call captureMotionPathShot() with selector from collectShotSelectors(). Save PNG to artifacts/, attach to Telegram approval. Use for lab look 3D panel rotations, HUD orbits, kinetic title paths. Gate: require SVG for strip filmstrip, else warn.

title: Concurrency cap for external API calls
text: maxConcurrent (default 50) caps simultaneous Step Functions starts from the CLI side, distinct from per-render chunk parallelism. Prevents hitting AWS account concurrency limits. The semaphore is in the orchestrator, not the worker.
how: Add a global asyncio.Semaphore in api.py (or a new rate_limiter.py) for Gemini, Muse, Cloudflare calls. Set default based on free-tier quotas (e.g., 10 concurrent). Wrap each external call with `async with semaphore:`. Log when waiting.

title: Aspect-agnostic resolution flag threading
text: outputResolutionAspectAgnostic=true threads through SerializableDistributedRenderConfig so the Lambda worker's compile stage remaps landscape → portrait/square when the composition orientation demands it. Canonical presets (portrait-4k) omit the flag.
how: In compose.py/compose_lab.py, add a config flag `aspect_agnostic: true` when using generic presets like "1080p". At render time, inspect composition's data-width/data-height orientation and swap width/height if needed. Pass flag to HyperFrames core.

title: Parameter override system for runtime config
text: SAM parameter overrides (ChromeSource, VideoImageUri, LambdaMemoryMb, ReservedConcurrency) are sent as a list of Key=Value strings. Omitted parameters use CloudFormation's UsePreviousValue on redeploy. VideoImageUri always sent (empty string) to allow removal.
how: Adopt a similar pattern for render.py: build a config dict with defaults, override with CLI flags, then pass to HyperFrames core. Use a three-tier precedence: composition defaults < project config < CLI flags. Document each parameter in a central schema.

title: Dry-run mode for batch jobs
text: --dry-run skips all AWS calls and emits a manifest with status: "would-invoke" for every entry, allowing linting of batch files without cost. The same config building and variable validation still run.
how: Add --dry-run to batch_render.py: validate variables, build render plans, estimate frame counts and duration, output manifest with predicted S3 keys and costs. Useful for QA before large personalized campaigns.

title: Cache directory isolation with ownership checks
text: foreignWritablePath detects if a cache directory is writable by another user (via uid mismatch). sealCacheInstall makes the installed artifact read-only. Concurrent installers verify independently; a folder that changes ownership during download aborts.
how: In the asset download cache (Muse, Cloudflare, FLUX), before writing, check os.stat(cache_dir).st_uid == os.getuid(). After writing, os.chmod(file, 0o444). If uid mismatch, raise and skip cache. Use a per-user subdir under /tmp/hyperframes-cache-$UID.

title: Clip-path and mask region parsing for true visible bounds
text: Parse CSS clip-path (inset, circle, ellipse, polygon) and single-layer gradient masks (linear/radial) into axis-aligned rectangles in viewport coordinates. Use these regions to crop text/client rects before overflow/overlap checks. Ignore unparsable shapes (assume fully visible).
how: Add clip-path/mask parser to preflight.py (port clipPathRegion/maskRegion from layout-audit.browser.js). Apply cropping to text rects before container-overflow and canvas-overflow checks.

title: Text overflow fix hints with font-size shrink calculation
text: When text overflows container, compute limitingRatio = min(containerWidth/textWidth, containerHeight/textHeight). If <1, suggest shrink font-size from current to ~current×limitingRatio. Also suggest container resize to neededWidth/Height. Include in error message for actionable preflight feedback.
how: In preflight.py's text overflow error, add fixHint with calculated shrink percentage and target font size. Use existing fontSize from style. Format as 'shrink font-size from 48px to ~36px, or widen container to 1080px'.

title: Deterministic stack state file with field validation
text: Persist render stack config (bucket, ARN, region, memory, concurrency) as JSON in .hyperframes/lambda-stack-<name>.json. Validate every field on read: bucket regex, ARN regex with 12-digit account, region regex, memory integer >0, function name ^[\w-]{1,64}$. Reject symlinks, oversized (>64 KB), malformed JSON, region/ARN mismatch. Case-insensitive stack name guard.
how: Create state.ts equivalent for our Cloudflare/doctor.py: writeStackOutputs/readStackOutputs/requireStack with same validation. Use in doctor.py to verify render worker config before jobs.

title: Lambda warm invocation with payload and profile support
text: aws lambda invoke --function-name <name> --region <region> --payload '{"Action":"warm"}' --cli-binary-format raw-in-base64-out --output json, optional --profile. Timeout 120 s. Throw on non-zero exit, FunctionError in response, or spawn ENOENT. Clean up temp output file.
how: Add warmFunction equivalent in our render worker pool (doctor.py): on worker start, POST /warm to our render API with {action:'warm'}. Mirror error handling and timeout. Use before first render job to eliminate cold starts.

title: Arm64 video image push with local override and repo tagging
text: Push arm64 OCI tarball to ECR repo named <stack-lower>-video tagged with hyperframes:stack=<stack>. Validate architecture=arm64, os=linux. Allow local override via HYPERFRAMES_LAMBDA_VIDEO_IMAGE env var (tarball path). In checkout builds, refuse release image (code mismatch) unless --video-arch x86_64. Clean up extracted layout dir after push.
how: Adapt for our Cloudflare Workers: build arm64 render image, push to Cloudflare Container Registry with tag hyperframes:stack=<env>. Validate arch via manifest. Add env var override for local dev images. Integrate into deploy script.

title: Canvas content at edge ignores full-bleed gradients
text: Audit flags drawn text touching canvas edge (canvas_content_at_edge) but stays silent on smooth gradients (color-grading canvas). Use data-layout-allow-overflow on canvas elements that are color-grading stand-ins (data-hf-color-grading-canvas).
how: In compose.py, when using canvas for color grading, add data-hf-color-grading-canvas and data-layout-allow-overflow.

title: Panel out of canvas severity and exemptions
text: Painted panels (solid background, borders) extending outside canvas trigger panel_out_of_canvas (warning for hero-sized, info for bleeds). Gradient-only glows (radial-gradient) and unpainted elements are ignored. Borders count as content.
how: Design intentional bleeds with gradient-only backgrounds or use data-layout-allow-overflow on hero panels.

title: Invisible text detection covers ancestor gradients/images
text: Audit detects transparent text via color, webkit-text-fill-color, and ancestor background-clip:text with missing/transparent backgrounds. Works across Chrome versions; pre-150 flags layered descendants (transform, opacity, filter, clip-path, view-transition) as invisible.
how: Avoid transparent text without stroke. For gradient text, ensure ancestor has valid background-image. Test with Chrome >=150.

title: Font-metric band tolerance for glyph ink spill
text: Audit allows vertical glyph ink spill within font-metric band (~7px for 36px font) on non-clipping boxes. Only flags overflow beyond that band.
how: No code change; awareness that tight line-heights are safe and won't trigger false text_box_overflow.

title: Video measurement toolkit for reference analysis
text: CLI commands: measure cuts (hard cuts + continued shots), events (cuts/flashes/appears/disappears/holds + sound onsets/beats), energy (motion magnitude correlation between ref/render), curve (ease/duration/overshoot of one element), face (face box + GSAP transform to match ref), extract (frame-exact still/clip/audio as project media with ledger).
how: Use in research.py and scout.py: run measure events --map on reference Shorts to get cut timestamps, hold durations, beat grid. Use measure curve on hero moves to copy easing. Use measure face to size presenter overlays. Feed results into brain.jsonl.

title: Exit-code pattern for reliable piped JSON
text: Commands never call process.exit(); they set process.exitCode and return. Ensures stdout drains before Node exits, fixing Windows pipe truncation. Verified by tests that mock process.exit to throw.
how: Audit publish.py, stats.py, doctor.py, and all CLI entry points: replace any process.exit(code) with process.exitCode = code; return. Add vitest check that mocks process.exit to throw.

title: Event-preserving frame thinning for vision review
text: When sampling frames into a strict budget cap (e.g. 12–24 tiles for Gemini vision review), uniform subsampling skips one-frame visual flashes and blurs hard cuts into apparent dissolves. Anchor `[onset - 1, onset, onset + 1]` around each detected visual change or cut. Allocate at least half the frame budget to these mandatory onset clusters and distribute the remainder evenly across the duration to maintain steady-state context.
how: In `review.py`, replace uniform interval frame extraction with this onset-anchored thinning logic before assembling the contact sheet for Gemini's post-render audit.

title: Run-length select filter for single-pass multi-frame extraction
text: Extracting multiple specific frames using repeated `ffmpeg -ss` calls is slow and causes seek drift. Compress sorted frame index arrays into consecutive runs (`runsOf`), compile them into a combined FFmpeg filter expression (`eq(n, k)` and `between(n, a, b)`), and reset presentation timestamps with `setpts=N/(fps)/TB`. Decode the raw stream into numbered PNGs in a single process pass without gap duplicates.
how: In `research.py` and `review.py`, use this filter pattern whenever extracting arbitrary review frames from source reference clips or rendered compositions.

title: Multi-channel motion signature for frozen-frame detection
text: Classify motion via 11 DOM channels (box geometry, opacity, font-variation-settings, clip-path, background/box-shadow paint, border/outline color, text content, control values, generated content, media pixels, color/text-shadow/fill/stroke) plus composition-level CSS counter state and media currentTime. Quantize position to 2px and opacity to 0.08 buckets for liveness; use coarse 8px media downsample for sweep guard. A frame is frozen only when all channels match across samples.
how: In review.py's vision review, replace or supplement Gemini frame checks with a local Node script that injects motion-signature.browser.js into the rendered page, samples at 2–3 points per scene, and flags scenes where signature is identical (frozen) or only audio time advances (blank video).

title: Content-visibility and layout-ignore handling for motion scope
text: content-visibility:hidden skips contents but not the host box; data-layout-ignore opts elements out of liveness signing (they may animate off-timeline) but keeps them as counter owners. A keepsMoving scope that is itself data-layout-ignore is still measured; opted-out descendants inside are excluded. Table-cell hosts skip contents; table-caption hosts do not.
how: In compose_lab.py, mark decorative ambient layers (glow, vignette, grain) with data-layout-ignore so they don't trigger false frozen-frame alerts. For off-screen preloaded scenes, use content-visibility:auto with containment to pause their motion signature until scrolled in.

title: Media time tracking for A/V sync verification
text: Video currentTime advances under seek even when pixels are unreadable (WebGL canvas); audio currentTime advances but is separated in the signature (AUDIO_TIME_SEPARATOR \u001f) so it counts as timeline running but not as moving picture. Both are bucketed to 0.1s for liveness.
how: In review.py, after render, extract video/audio element currentTime at multiple seek points via a headless check. Flag scenes where video time is static but audio advances (video freeze) or vice versa (audio desync).

title: On-device Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 for deterministic transcription
text: Parakeet model (sherpa-onnx or parakeet-mlx) runs locally, no API cost, with glibc 2.32+ requirement. Install via 'hyperframes models install parakeet' (650 MB). Models list command reports runner (sherpa/parakeet-mlx) and install status. Cancellation (Ctrl-C) cleanly aborts download with exit 130.
how: Evaluate adding a local transcription step in caption.py for Devanagari/English captions: extract audio via ffmpeg, run Parakeet via sherpa-onnx Node binding, align with existing Gemini captions for verification. Keeps pipeline free and offline.

title: Workspace voice clone inventory with teammate-clone warnings
text: The voices command lists all clones the HeyGen workspace can use, explicitly warning that HeyGen does not identify owners. A clone must only be used when the person confirms it's theirs or owner agreed; never select by count/language/name. Missing IDs may still be teammate clones.
how: If we ever integrate HeyGen for avatar/lipsync (paid), wrap voice selection in a gate that requires explicit owner confirmation logged in brain.jsonl. For now, document in voice gate that Gemini TTS (Charon) is our primary and this rule applies to any future paid voice clones.

title: Scope resolution for static wrapper elements
text: Standard composition uses static `.clip` wrapper with animated descendants. Resolver: if scope selector matches an animated target → sample only that; else → sample all animated descendants of scope; else → error with nearest animated elements. Pure function `resolveShotSelectors(scope, animated[], isDescendant)` keeps logic testable; DOM check runs in browser.
how: In plan.py/shot targeting: when user selects a container (e.g., `.clip`), auto-expand to its animated children. Add to compose_lab.py shot helper: pass scope selector, resolve animated descendants via DOM query before sampling.

title: Quantized liveness buckets for motion detection
text: Quantized signature buckets positions into 2px grid; moves within bucket don't change quantized hash. Exact signature catches sub-pixel changes. Use quantized for 'sweep_static' gate (ignore micro-jitter), exact for 'sweep_live' (detect any animation). Test: 0.6px move changes exact but not quantized.
how: In preflight.py: compute both signatures. If quantized unchanged → sweep_static passes. If exact changed but quantized same → log micro-motion warning. Threshold configurable per scene type.

title: Nested composition audio source resolution
text: Audio `src` attribute resolved relative to the scene file declaring it (e.g., `compositions/intro.html` → `../assets/voice.wav`), not project root. Prevents path errors in mounted scenes. Duplicate target ID check across all compositions (root + nested) before measuring; errors with file list if same ID appears in multiple files.
how: In mix.py: when processing `data-composition-src` scenes, resolve audio paths against scene file directory. Add validation in plan.py: scan all composition files for duplicate audio IDs; fail early with locations.

title: Deterministic equal-time sampling with windowing
text: `sampleTimes(duration, n, from, to)` returns N timestamps: clamped to [0, duration], equal spacing, rounded to 1ms. Windowed sampling (from/to) enables dense inspection of one phase. Single sample (n=1) returns window start. Used for both marker and ghost capture.
how: In motion-shot command: expose `--samples`, `--from`, `--to`. In review.py: for drop-off analysis, sample last 2s at 30fps (60 samples). For hook verification, sample first 3s at 10fps.

title: SFX Autoplay Priming
text: Bypass browser autoplay restrictions for SFX by priming Audio objects: play them muted and immediately reset to `currentTime = 0` upon the first user interaction (click/keydown).
