how: Add a small 'unlocker' script to the HyperFrames base template that listens for the first interaction to initialize all SFX `Audio` instances.

title: Trim-Aware Loudness Measurement
text: When measuring loudness for normalized clips, only measure the specific time window defined by `data-start` and `data-end`. Measuring the full source file leads to inaccurate gain calculations for trimmed clips.
how: Update the FFmpeg measurement command in our pipeline to include `-ss` and `-t` parameters based on the clip's authored trim points.

title: EBU R 128 Per-Clip Normalization
text: Normalize individual audio/video clips to a specific LUFS target or match a reference clip. Limit gain boosts to +12dB and ensure true-peak does not exceed -1.5 dBTP to prevent clipping during the final mix.
how: Integrate into `mix.py`. Use FFmpeg `ebur128` filter to measure clips, calculate required gain, and update `data-volume` attributes in the HyperFrames HTML before the final master render.

title: Cross-Origin SFX Cues
text: Trigger SFX from within a composition iframe by sending `postMessage` events to the parent window. This allows the parent to manage the audio engine and bypass iframe-specific autoplay blocks.
how: Modify the GSAP SFX trigger logic to emit `window.parent.postMessage({type: 'hf-sfx', name: '...' })` instead of playing audio directly inside the frame.

title: Host-app detection to prevent orphaned background processes
text: If HYPERFRAMES_DESKTOP_PROJECT env var is set, background preview is refused with error code host-app-owns-preview, suggesting --foreground instead. This avoids a background server outliving the host run and locking project history.
how: In doctor.py and any CI entrypoint, check for a similar env (e.g., STUDIO_MANAGED_RUN=1) and disable background workers, forcing foreground execution so the orchestrator can reap them.

title: Agent-readable selection/context JSON with compact/full detail
text: --selection and --context output JSON with schemaVersion, server info, selection (compact: only key fields; full: entire snapshot), lint summary, and capabilities. Control characters in strings are preserved in JSON but escaped in human output.
how: Enhance Telegram approval (Studio360) to send a --context --json payload when requesting approval, giving the owner (or auto-approver) structured scene data: currentTime, target element, thumbnail URL, lint errors.

title: Deterministic PID reporting (server PID over launcher PID)
text: publicPreviewPid(serverPid, fallbackPid) returns the server's own PID if valid (>0), else the launcher PID. This ensures the reported PID is the actual long-lived process for stop/kill operations.
how: In doctor.py's process tracking, store the child's PID (from spawn) and also query the actual render worker PID (e.g., via a /health endpoint) to use for subsequent stop signals.

title: Cross-platform spawn with windowsHide
text: All child_process.spawn calls pass { windowsHide: true } to prevent console window flashing on Windows. This applies to Vite, Studio dev server, and local Studio mode.
how: Ensure every subprocess.Popen / asyncio.create_subprocess_exec in the pipeline (ffmpeg, yt-dlp, Muse CLI) sets creationflags=subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW on Windows (Python 3.7+).

title: Port validation and conflict resolution with explicit port forwarding
text: parsePort() validates 1-65535. findPortAndServe() scans from startPort, reuses existing server for same project unless --force-new, and returns {type: 'reused'|'started', port}. Explicit --port is forwarded to all lifecycle calls.
how: In publish.py's warm-up schedule or any local server (e.g., thumbnail preview), use a similar port scanner that prefers a fixed port but falls back deterministically, and expose the chosen port via JSON for downstream steps.

title: Shell argument escaping for generated commands
text: stopBackgroundCommand() uses shellArg(path, platform) to produce a safely quoted command string for POSIX (single quotes, escape singles) and Windows (double quotes, escape doubles). Paths with $(), &, backticks fall back to 'run from project folder'.
how: Add a shell_quote() helper in utils/shell.py and use it wherever the pipeline prints a command for the user to copy (e.g., doctor.py repair instructions, render re-run commands in Telegram).

title: Bounded port scan window (MAX_PORT_SCAN=100)
text: When scanning for existing services on a port range, limit scan to a fixed window (e.g., 100 ports) from the start port to avoid runaway scans. Only probe saved custom ports outside the window explicitly.
how: In any port allocation logic (e.g., preview server, render worker ports), define MAX_PORT_SCAN=100 and scan only [start, start+MAX_PORT_SCAN). For saved custom ports, probe directly.

title: Process descendant verification before kill
text: When stopping a managed service, verify the live server PID is a descendant of the recorded wrapper PID (using process tree). Kill the wrapper (not the server) for clean shutdown. If wrapper identity changed, kill the server directly.
how: In doctor.py's kill logic, use psutil to check parent-child relationship between wrapper PID and server PID. Kill wrapper if descendant, else kill server.

title: Concurrent launch isolation via pre-launch port snapshot
text: Before launching a new background process, snapshot all same-project ports. After launch, only consider servers on new ports as the started instance. This prevents two concurrent launches from adopting each other's servers.
how: In any parallel render/preview startup, record active ports before spawn; after spawn, wait for a server on a previously unseen port.

title: Wrapper identity birth token for PID reuse detection
text: Record a process birth token (e.g., start time) when launching a background worker; on later status/stop, verify the PID still matches that token to avoid killing a recycled PID. Only retire session when token mismatches or PID not signalable.
how: In doctor.py and render worker launch, capture process start time via psutil.Process(pid).create_time() and store in job metadata. On health check, compare; if mismatch, treat as new process and clean up old job.

title: Atomic state file writes via temp-file rename
text: Write critical JSON state files (session, job status) to a temporary file (pid.tmp) then atomically rename into place. Readers see either old or new complete file, never partial. Clean up temp files on error.
how: Modify brain.jsonl, results.md, and any pipeline state writes to use temp-file + os.rename pattern. Ensure temp files are cleaned in finally block.

title: Log tailing on background process failure
text: On background process startup failure, include the last N lines (e.g., 5) of its log in the error message for immediate debugging.
how: In render worker launch and preview server start, capture log file path; on failure, read last 5 lines and attach to exception/error report sent to Telegram.

title: Cross-platform state directory resolution
text: Resolve state/cache directory using priority: HYPERFRAMES_CACHE_DIR (custom), XDG_STATE_HOME (Linux), LOCALAPPDATA (Windows), ~/.local/state (fallback). Ensures consistent locations across OS.
how: Create a utility get_state_dir() in our pipeline config module used by all scripts for writing session, cache, logs.

title: Preferred port handling with force-new replacement
text: If a specific port is requested, reuse existing server on that port even if another owned server exists. For GPU policy changes, stop owned server and start new one on same port. Fail with clear error if port mismatch and not force-new.
how: In preview server management (if we have one), implement port-specific reuse and replacement logic. For render workers, maybe not needed.

title: Robust project ID extraction from URLs
text: parseUpdateTarget() handles full URLs (https://hyperframes.dev/p/hfp_abc123), scheme-less (hyperframes.dev/p/hfp_abc123), with query/hash, and bare IDs, falling back to last path segment. Returns trimmed ID.
how: Use in publish.py when processing YouTube or HyperFrames project links; replace ad-hoc parsing with this logic.

title: Explicit visibility messaging for re-publish
text: CLI states exactly what was requested: 'Public — anyone with the URL', 'Private — authentication required', or 'Unchanged — keeps this project's current setting' for in-place updates. Warns if committed target not updated (new project created).
how: Update Telegram approval cards and publish.py logs to mirror this wording; include 'Requested visibility' line and mismatch warning.

title: Credential ownership enforcement for updates
text: --update and --space require OAuth login (not API key). Resolution happens once before bake; upload uses same credential even if login expires mid-publish. Fails loudly if env API key present.
how: In publish.py, resolve credential once, pass to upload; reject update/space if credential type != oauth; add expiry check before upload.

title: Outside-file approval staging with telemetry
text: stageWithOutsideFileApproval() builds file map, collects left-out references, prompts for approval (unless --yes/--include-outside-files), tracks via telemetry. Returns staged fileMap + outsideFiles list for notice.
how: Integrate into render pipeline before upload: stage project, prompt in Telegram for outside files, log left-out references to brain.jsonl.

title: Lint preflight with strict/non-strict modes and verbose toggle
text: runRenderLint aborts on errors unless --strict-all; prints one-line summary by default, full findings with --lint-verbose. Default-entry mismatch shows fixHint even in non-verbose.
how: Adopt in preflight.py: add --strict/--strict-all/--lint-verbose flags. Show fixHint for blank_root_with_standalone_composition always. Integrate with Telegram approval.

title: CPU telemetry sampler with auto-stop on render complete/error
text: Start a CPU sampler at render start; on completion or error, stop it and attach cpuBusyAvgPct/cpuBusyPeakPct to telemetry. Sampler must be stopped exactly once per render.
how: In renderLocal wrapper (or doctor.py), wrap producer execution with startRenderCpuSampler(); in finally block call stop() and push metrics to stats.py / Telegram report.

title: Audio-lowered warning with exact dB value in render result
text: When loudness normalization lowers the mix, emit a warning with the precise dB reduction (e.g., 7.3 dB) and include code 'audio_lowered' in render warnings array.
how: In mix.py after EBU R128 normalization, if gain < 0, push {code:'audio_lowered', message:`Audio lowered ${Math.abs(gain).toFixed(1)} dB`} to render warnings; surface in review.py and Telegram approval card.

title: Diagnostic JSON line only for piped non-TTY stdout
text: Emit @hf-diagnostic {json} line only when stdout is not a TTY and not in quiet mode. Strip private fields (ids, details) from diagnostic payload.
how: In publish.py/stats.py, check process.stdout.isTTY; if false and not quiet, print structured diagnostic line. Sanitize with allowlist before emit.

title: Quiet mode restricts producer logger to warn level
text: When --quiet, pass logger level 'warn' to producer; default is 'info'; --debug forces 'debug'. Ensures CI logs stay clean.
how: In renderLocal wrapper, map quiet/debug flags to loggerLevel; pass to producer config. Apply in compose.py render call and Cloudflare worker.

title: Browser GPU mode resolution: CLI flag > env > default auto
text: resolveBrowserGpuForCli(docker, cliFlag, env) returns: docker→software; cliFlag explicit→that; env→that; else 'auto'. Hardware only when explicitly allowed.
how: Add resolveBrowserGpuForCli() in compose_lab.py; use in render config. Set PRODUCER_BROWSER_GPU_MODE=software in CI; allow --browser-gpu hardware for local high-quality renders.

title: Telemetry event forwarding for render lifecycle phases
text: Producer emits [Render:trace] logs with phase (capture_streaming), status (start/end), framesCompleted, totalFrames, durationMs. Forward these to telemetry as structured observations.
how: In producer config, add logger that captures [Render:trace] and pushes to trackingState.renderObservations; in stats.py, aggregate phase timings for dashboard.

title: Format-specific encoder validation before producer load
text: For MP4 with force-sdr: require libx264 encoder; reject early if missing. For HLS: refuse VideoToolbox fallback (needs forced keyframes). WebM/MOV/PNG/GIF skip H.264 check.
how: In preflight.py, add detectH264EncoderModeForRender(); if format=mp4&hdr=force-sdr and no libx264, abort with clear error. If format=hls and only videotoolbox, abort.

title: Circuit breaker for feature rollout with explicit env override
text: Feature flag (DE parallel router) defaults ON. Breaker trips after 2 reverted renders; writes explicit false to config. User env var (HF_DE_PARALLEL_ROUTER) always wins over breaker.
how: Implement in brain.jsonl: track feature health per render; after N failures, write featureFlag=false to config. Respect OS env override. Use for new transitions, avatar, etc.

title: Structured render telemetry with machine-readable result line
text: Emit @hf-result JSON line on stdout with version, operation, reference_background, motion_blur tier/movers/failed_frames. Suppressed in quiet mode or Docker. Enables automated QA dashboards.
how: In review.py, after render, print JSON line to stdout (not stderr). Parse in stats.py for dashboard. Add motion_blur summary from producer perf. 10 lines.

title: Segmented capture resume for long renders
text: With HF_SEGMENTED_CAPTURE=true, reuse validated segments from renders/.hf-segments/<hash>/segments.json on re-run. Each segment re-validated before skip. --keep-segments retains cache for debugging.
how: In compose.py render loop, implement segment hashing (composition hash + settings). Write segments.json with frame ranges and checksums. On resume, verify each segment file exists and matches checksum. 60 lines.

title: Content-addressed frame cache with relocation
text: Extracted frames cached in <tmpdir>/hyperframes-extract-cache-<uid> keyed by SHA256. --frames-cache-dir moves cache off system drive (critical for Windows C:). Disable with 'off'/'none'/'false'.
how: In compose.py frame extraction, add cache dir config. Hash source video + seek time + format. Store as .jpg/.png with .sha256 sidecar. Cleanup on render end unless --keep-segments. 50 lines.

title: Quality preset to encoder mapping
text: Quality aliases map to concrete encoder settings: 'looks' -> CRF 16 (standard), 'delivery' -> high tier (no CRF), 'draft'/'standard'/'high' map to quality tiers. Explicit --crf or --video-bitrate overrides preset; MOV/ProRes ignores CRF.
how: In mix.py and publish.py, define QUALITY_PRESETS = {'looks': {'crf': 16}, 'delivery': {'preset': 'high'}, 'standard': {'crf': 20}}. Validate that --crf/--bitrate not used with MOV. Apply preset when no explicit override.

title: Page/workflow attribution via skill
text: Each render plan captures authoringSkill from explicit --skill flag or project's hyperframes.json (authoringSkill). Source tracked as 'flag' or 'project-config'. Invalid skill slugs recorded for telemetry but don't override project config.
how: Add page_id (kaise-tech, puran-katha, aage-suno) to brain.jsonl and hyperframes.json. In plan.py, resolve page from flag or project config. Include in stats.py reports to correlate retention with page.

title: Operator env var snapshot for debugging
text: At plan time, snapshot HF_/HYPERFRAMES_-prefixed env var names (never values), sorted, capped at 20. Excludes CLI-internal keys (HF_SHADER_WORKER_ENTRY). Provides reproducible context for telemetry without leaking secrets.
how: In plan.py, capture STUDIO_-prefixed env var names (e.g., STUDIO_GEMINI_KEY, STUDIO_MUSE_ACCOUNT). Store in plan.studioEnvOverrides. Log in doctor.py and stats.py for debugging production issues.

title: Specific video source failure hints
text: sourceFailureHint walks error cause chain (max 5 levels) for VIDEO_SOURCE_UNRENDERABLE code. Maps failure kinds to actionable hints: invalid_media -> check ffprobe/file completeness; source_missing -> check local path; download_not_found -> check URL 404. Deduplicates hints.
how: In review.py, when vision review fails due to missing/corrupt media, catch exception and call a similar hint function. Output actionable message to Telegram approval with exact check command (ffprobe, ls, curl -I).

title: Immutable frozen render plan
text: createRenderPlan resolves all flags, defaults, and project config into a deeply frozen RenderPlan object (Object.freeze on plan and plan.environment) before any execution. This prevents accidental mutation during render and ensures reproducibility.
how: In our pipeline, make plan.py output a frozen dataclass (or Pydantic model with frozen=True) containing all render settings (fps, quality, resolution, env vars). Pass this immutable plan to compose.py, mix.py, and review.py.

title: Aspect-agnostic resolution aliases
text: The CLI accepts aliases like '1080p', '4k', '1440p' and maps them to landscape/portrait/square based on composition. The plan stores outputResolutionAspectAgnostic=true and the raw alias for telemetry.
how: Extend thumb.py and compose.py to accept --resolution 1080p|4k|square etc. Map to our standard resolutions (1920x1080, 1080x1920, 1080x1080) based on page default orientation. Store raw alias in brain.jsonl for analytics.

title: Range rendering for quick previews
text: --start/--end flags render only a time range (seconds). Only supported for MP4 with whole-number FPS in {24,25,30,50,60} and SDR. Returns error with clear message for unsupported combos.
how: Add --start/--end to plan.py and pass to HyperFrames render. Use in preflight.py to render just the hook (first 2s) for quick vision review. In review.py, render only problematic segments for re-check.

title: Declarative environment variables in plan
text: Environment changes (low-memory-mode, fast-capture, frames-cache-dir, max-concurrent-renders) are collected into plan.environment (frozen) and only applied via applyRenderEnvironment() at execution start. Keeps plan pure and auditable.
how: In plan.py, collect all env vars into plan.env dict. In doctor.py and render entry point, call apply_env(plan.env) once before spawning render workers. Ensures consistent env across retries.

title: Catalog usage tracking per render
text: summarizeCatalogUsage scans project manifest and render entry to list installed blocks vs used blocks. Reports manifestUnreadable. Runs once per plan (shared across batch rows).
how: In plan.py, after resolving entry HTML, scan for data-composition-src references. Compare with components/ directory. Store used_components in plan. In stats.py, track which lab/classic components are actually used per page.

title: Targeted Dependency Updates
text: Instead of full-set re-installs, use a manifest-driven 'update' that only fetches missing or 'outdated' modules. Use `GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1` and `GIT_CLONE_PROTECTION_ACTIVE=0` to speed up git-based asset/code fetches.
how: Modify `doctor.py` to check a local `brain.jsonl` version against the repo manifest and only pull specific updated playbooks/scripts rather than a full `git pull` every time.

title: Private Media Isolation
text: When downloading remote assets for processing, use a private directory with restricted permissions (0o700 on Unix) to prevent cross-user access. Validate URLs against a blocklist of private/internal IP ranges (SSRF protection).
how: In `research.py` (yt-dlp) and `compose.py` (Muse downloads), ensure temp folders are created with restricted modes and validate that URLs aren't pointing to 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.x.x.

title: Composite recapture order
text: Recapture snapshot composite only after video frame injection and visibility sync, before final screenshot. Requires __hf_page_composite_resolve on window; skipped if resolver absent.
how: Document in compose_lab.py: any custom composite effects (blur, transitions) must register resolver before snapshot capture. Ensures review frames match final render.

title: Tail-frame timing for snapshot sampling
text: Back off 3% of composition duration (capped at 250 ms, floor 50 ms) to capture the last readable frame instead of the blank exact-end frame. Default frame sets always include this tail; explicit --at times append it unless already covered.
how: Adopt in review.py and preflight.py when selecting frames for vision review or contact sheets. Replace any fixed-end sampling with computeSnapshotTimes logic (tailFrameTime + computeSnapshotTimes).

title: Self-closed media detection
text: Warn when <audio> or <video> tags are self-closing (e.g., <audio src="x.mp3" />) because they produce blank stills; require closing tags even with fallback content. Returns null when all media tags are properly closed.
how: Add to preflight.py HTML audit: scan composition HTML for self-closed media tags, emit warning with element IDs and frame impact. Reuse selfClosedMediaWarning logic.

title: SVG ID isolation across scenes
text: When multiple scenes reuse the same SVG symbol/gradient/clipPath IDs, each scene's snapshot must resolve its own definitions. Test proves corner gradient from page-level defs works while scene-local portrait renders correctly per scene.
how: In compose_lab.py, ensure scene-scoped SVG defs are namespaced or cloned per scene before render. Add snapshot test to verify no ID bleed across scene boundaries.

title: Displayed-size frame extraction
text: Extract video frames at their displayed pixel dimensions (never larger than source). Downscale if requested displayedPixels < source; upscale requests are clamped to source size.
how: Modify extractVideoFrameToBuffer calls in review.py and thumb.py to pass displayedPixels from layout (data-width/height). Prevents upscaling artifacts in contact sheets and thumbnails.

title: Comprehensive video format handling
text: Robust extraction across fragmented MP4, MPEG-TS, HEVC, open-GOP, stream-copy trims with edit lists, negative timestamps, VFR, B-frames, and A/V sync offsets (audio lead/lag). Retags SDR as sRGB.
how: Add test matrix in our CI covering these formats. Ensure frame extractor uses ffprobe for presentation timestamps, handles edit lists, and applies color-space retagging (bt709 → sRGB) for consistent review frames.

title: HDR tone mapping for snapshot color consistency
text: If source video is HDR (BT.2020 + HLG/PQ), apply FFmpeg zscale tonemap filter to extracted frames so they match the SDR export. Without libzimg, frames stay HDR-tagged and browser maps them darker. Probe metadata via ffprobe first.
how: In preflight.py frame extraction, call extractMediaMetadata via ffprobe. If isHdrColorSpace, apply hdrToSdrToneMapFilter in FFmpeg -vf chain. Fallback gracefully if filter missing. Ensures Gemini sees same colors as final render.

title: Composition range sampling for targeted checks
text: Support sampling frames within a specific sub-composition (--composition stat) by resolving its start/end from timeline data. Also supports --range start,end for arbitrary windows. Useful for focused QA on a single scene or transition.
how: In preflight.py, add --composition and --range flags. Use resolveSnapshotCompositionRange and sampleSnapshotRange to get times. Pass to existing capture loop. Enables per-scene preflight without full composition capture.

title: Batch frame decoding via frame bank
text: Group frames from the same video that share a keyframe decode into a single FFmpeg pass (groupOverlappingDecodes). The frame bank plans all needed frames upfront, decodes once per keyframe group, and serves repeated requests from cache. Cuts FFmpeg invocations dramatically for multi-frame review.
how: Add snapshotFrameBank.ts logic to preflight.py/review.py. When extracting N frames from a video, call frameBank.plan(videoPath, wants) then frameBank.take() per frame. Set VIDEO_FRAME_EXTRACT_CONCURRENCY=4.

title: Orthogonal camera for 3D depth verification
text: Apply CSS 3D transform to composition root (rotateX/Y) with a single perspective on its parent, preserving 3D through ancestor chain. Captures occlusion and depth that head-on screenshots miss. Works on any composition shape, no #stage assumption.
how: In preflight.py, add optional --angle iso|custom flag. Before each seek, inject orbitStageSource() via page.evaluate with pitch/yaw. Capture extra still for 3D QA. Use for lab look panels, HUD, terminal elements.

title: Artifact recording with metadata
text: Each captured frame gets a UUID, absolute path, timestamp, and metadata (composition, camera angle, zoom, review role). Stored in project history (artifactDirectory) with manifest. Enables reproducibility, audit trail, and later diff against render output.
how: Integrate captureArtifactRevision and recordArtifacts into preflight.py and review.py. Write artifact JSONL alongside frames. Use in doctor.py to verify frame-to-render consistency (frame-accurate video diff).

title: Composition range resolution with nested offset clamping
text: Resolves a sub-composition's visible time window by walking up ancestor tree, applying each ancestor's data-start/data-duration, and clamping to ancestor bounds. Handles relative offsets like 'parent + 1'. Returns [start, end] clamped to root duration. Validates unique composition ID match.
how: Use in plan.py/compose.py when calculating scene windows for nested compositions (e.g., lab look panels inside a scene). Replace manual timing math with this resolver using our scene tree and registered durations.

title: Content-addressed template pulls with atomic staging and abandonment cleanup
text: Downloads pinned template bundles (SHA256 + byte size verified), unpacks in .hyperframes/template-pulls/<slug>.part-<pid>-<rand>/, writes .hyperframes-pull.json marker with owner/pid, verifies file manifest against cached hashes, then atomically renames into templates/<slug>/. On restart, removes part folders whose pid is dead. Blocks symlinks, hardlinks, path traversal.
how: Adopt for our asset packs (Muse/FLUX prompt packs, SFX libraries, font bundles). Store manifests in cache-dir, stage in .studio/asset-pulls/, verify on each pull, auto-clean stale partials. Prevents corrupted assets and Windows rename locks.

title: Telemetry status with override precedence and persistence safety
text: Effective telemetry status checks: config flag > HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY > DO_NOT_TRACK > dev_mode > telemetry_disabled_build. Write uses fresh config read (bypasses module cache), fails loudly on EACCES with stderr details, never claims success on write failure. JSON output only for status subcommand.
how: Apply to our doctor.py/telemetry: read config fresh before writing, define clear override hierarchy (env > config > build), error with exact reason on disk failure, restrict JSON to status command.

title: Timeline mutation commands with plan/apply/undo receipts
text: CLI verbs: move, trim, split, delete, set, duplicate, ids, apply, undo. Each reads only fields relevant to verb (FIELDS_READ_BY_VERB). --plan shows diff without writing. --json outputs machine-readable receipt. apply consumes atomic plan file. undo restores from receipt. Runtime queries via inspector service on HF_INSPECT_URL.
how: Add to our timeline editing (plan.py/compose.py): implement move/trim/split/delete with --plan preview, emit JSON receipts, store for undo. Later expose via CLI for manual fixes.

title: Standardized 16kHz WAV Pre-processing
text: Before transcription, downsample all audio to 16kHz mono WAV. This is the standard input for Whisper and Parakeet, reducing processing time and memory overhead.
how: In `research.py` and `voice gate`, use ffmpeg to create a temporary 16kHz WAV file before calling the transcription engine, then delete it after the JSON is produced.

title: Regex-based Project Pinning & Upgrade
text: Automatically find and update versioned strings (e.g., `npx hyperframes@0.7.48`) in `package.json` scripts and shell wrappers using regex-based replacement.
how: Add an `upgrade.py` utility to our stack that scans our script directory and `ideas.py` for hardcoded model versions or API tags, allowing us to bump the 'shared brain' versions globally.

title: Extract lint findings for missing/empty sub-compositions as validate errors
text: HyperFrames bundler silently skips broken data-composition-src files. Validate pulls 'missing_or_empty_sub_composition' lint findings (severity error) and surfaces them as console errors, turning silent failures into hard validation failures.
how: In preflight.py, after linting project, check for missing_or_empty_sub_composition findings and treat as blocking errors (not warnings). Ensures all referenced scene files exist and are non-empty before render.

title: Media fit analysis handles rate lanes, canonical trim, loop
text: analyzeClipMediaFit computes playable media seconds from slotSeconds, mediaSeconds, loop, and automation rate lanes (piecewise constant or linear). Canonical trim (data-playback-start + data-media-start) overrides legacy offsets. Returns null if slot fits, else fit object with shortfall.
how: Port analyzeClipMediaFit logic to Python for preflight. Input: slotSeconds, mediaSeconds, loop, automation JSON. Output: fit or None. Use in audio validation (item 2).

title: Race media metadata load with deadline instead of fixed wait
text: When checking media durations, wait for loadedmetadata or error event per element up to a deadline (Date.now() + maxWaitMs), not a single fixed sleep. Elements with existing duration resolve immediately. Prevents false 'could not read duration' on slow remote sources.
how: Modify review.py's blank-stretch scan or preflight's media checks: for each media asset, spawn a probe (Audio/Video element), await loadedmetadata/error with Promise.race against deadline. Use Node's EventTarget duck-typing for testability.

title: Per-process hang watchdog (60s silence -> diagnostic report)
text: Wrap stdout/stderr write; if no write for 60s, write a JSON diagnostic (excluding env vars) to HYPERFRAMES_HANG_REPORT dir. One report per process, unref timer. Useful for stuck renders, browser launches, or API calls.
how: Add to doctor.py or a new hangwatch.py: monkey-patch sys.stdout/stderr write, arm 60s timer, on timeout write process.report.getReport({excludeEnv:true}) to file. Set HYPERFRAMES_HANG_REPORT=/var/log/hyperframes/hangs in render workers.

title: Safe version guard before shell exec (isSafeVersion)
text: Reject any version string not matching strict semver (no shell metacharacters) before passing to execFileSync with shell:false. Prevents injection from poisoned registry responses. Shared with update notice.
how: Add isSafeVersion(version) regex check in doctor.py before any git/npm/bun version exec. Use in upgrade logic if studio ever auto-updates dependencies. Validate VERSION from package.json before using in commands.

title: Aspect ratio correction: crop center, never stretch
text: If a generator returns 1344x768 for a 16:9 request (1.75:1 vs 1.777:1), crop to 1344x756 centered rather than stretching. Tolerance: 0.2% aspect difference. Log note: "HeyGen returned WxH for 16:9; cropped to WxH (centre), not stretched".
how: In `review.py` or `compose.py` after download, probe video dimensions. Compute target from requested aspect. If `abs(actual/target - 1) > 0.002`, crop with `ffmpeg -vf crop=w:h` centered, re-encode CRF 12 slow. Add note to manifest.

title: Voice catalog with language-code mapping and idempotent pick
text: Map language codes (en, en-US, zh-CN, cmn) to provider's language names (English, Chinese). Pick first public voice for that language. Reject multilingual fallback unless explicitly requested. Cache pick per project+request+account scope with idempotency key to survive catalog reorder on retry.
how: In `voice.py`/`plan.py`: use `Intl.DisplayNames` to map code->name. Query provider voices (Gemini TTS voices). Store picked voice_id in `.hyperframes/voice-picks.json` keyed by `hash(request+scope)`. On re-run, reuse same voice_id.

title: Per-run credit budget with 10% headroom for vendor-priced models
text: Store a credit limit in `.hyperframes/credit-limit.json` per project run. Before any generation, estimate cost; if vendor-priced (charged on provider's bill), add 10% headroom and refuse if `estimate * 1.1 > limit`. Track actual charges in a job ledger keyed by idempotency key.
how: Add `credit-limit.json` write in `plan.py`/`ideas.py` when a run starts. In `generate.py` (or equivalent), compute cost via pricing table, apply headroom for Gemini/Muse/FLUX if they bill externally, call `checkLimit()` before API call. Record actual credits in `.media/manifest.jsonl` and a local ledger.

title: Enhanced media manifest with full provenance
text: Extend `.media/manifest.jsonl` to include: provider, route, model, job ID, prompt, references (relative paths), first_frame, avatar, audio, video, motion, masks (box + time window), voice, cuts_inside, charged_credits. Regenerate index on every write.
how: Modify `recordInPlace` in `media-use/lib/manifest.mjs` (or our equivalent) to accept all fields. Update `generate.py`, `compose.py`, `mix.py`, `thumb.py` to pass provenance dict. Add `regenerateIndex` call after each write.

title: Reference image preprocessing: max 2048px, JPEG, EXIF orientation
text: Before sending images to any model, load with sharp (auto-rotate via EXIF), resize to fit 2048px on long side, encode JPEG q90. Fallback to ffmpeg if sharp unavailable. Ensures consistent input, avoids orientation bugs from phone photos.
how: Create `preprocess_refs.py` used by `generate.py` (images), `compose.py` (clips), `thumb.py`. Use `sharp` with `.rotate().resize(2048,2048,{fit:'inside',withoutEnlargement:true}).jpeg({quality:90})`. Fallback to `ffmpeg -vf scale='min(2048,iw)':'min(2048,ih)':force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease -q:v 3`.

title: Pre-generation pricing and validation (--plan mode)
text: Every generation type has a `priceOf(request)` function returning USD, credits, basis string, and vendor-priced flag. `checkRequest()` validates required flags, conflicts, aspect/model compatibility, reference counts before any API call. `--plan` runs pricing + validation only.
how: Create `pricing.py` with tables for Gemini TTS, Muse, FLUX, Pollinations. Add `checkRequest()` in `generate.py`/`compose.py` that validates: required fields, file existence, aspect support, reference limits. Expose via CLI `--plan` flag that prints price and exits.

title: Motion guide cut detection and masked-region blanking
text: If using a motion guide clip (for future video-to-video), detect cuts via frame signatures. Refuse multi-shot guides unless `--allow-cuts`. For masked regions (text overlays), blank them before sending: temporal median filter (radius=fps) for moving areas, frame-color shrink for static text. Verify result with structure ratio (inside edges > 1.5x ring).
how: When we add motion-guide support in `compose.py`/`generate.py`: add `checkGuide()` using `findCuts`. Add `fillMasks()` using ffmpeg `tmedian` and `scale=3:3,scale=w:h`. Add `structured()` check post-generation. Store masks in manifest as `[x,y,w,h,start,end]`.

title: Vendor-Priced Credit Headroom
text: When using APIs that charge based on variable vendor rates (like image generation models with different aspect ratio costs), enforce a 10% headroom (1.1x multiplier) on the estimate during pre-flight checks. This prevents jobs from failing mid-render if the final bill is slightly higher than the initial estimate.
how: In preflight.py, when calculating the 'cost' of a video plan, multiply the estimated credit usage by 1.1 before comparing it against the studio's remaining budget.

title: Refusal-to-Fix Mapping
text: Map specific API error codes to human-readable 'Fixes'. For example, 'hf_usage_exhausted' should trigger a specific 'Buy Credits' link, while 'content_policy_violation' should suggest a specific 'Reword Prompt' action. This allows the automated 'doctor' to provide actionable feedback to the operator.
how: In doctor.py, implement a lookup table that parses API error bodies and returns the 'fix' string to the Telegram Studio360 channel.

title: Request-Derived Idempotency Keys
text: Generate a unique key for every API request by hashing the route and the request body (e.g., hf-sha256(route + body)). This ensures that if a network error occurs or a script is re-run, the external provider (like HeyGen or ElevenLabs) recognizes it as the same job and doesn't charge twice.
how: Update doctor.py and the API calling functions in research.py/compose.py to generate a hash of the prompt/parameters before calling external services, passing it as an Idempotency-Key header.

title: Sticky Voice Selection
text: Store the specific voice ID used for a project in a local ledger (e.g., .studio/voice-picks.jsonl). On re-runs, the system must check this ledger first before picking a 'random' or 'best' voice for a language. This ensures character consistency across edits of the same video.
how: Add a check in plan.py to look for an existing voice entry in the project folder before calling the TTS engine.

title: Project-Level Job Ledger
text: Maintain a heygen-jobs.jsonl (or studio-jobs.jsonl) inside each project's hidden directory. Record every API call's status (reserved, pending, completed, failed), the idempotency key, and the actual credits charged. This allows for precise 'resume' logic and audit trails for spending.
how: Create a new utility projectRecords.py to append JSON lines to a hidden project file whenever an external API is called in the pipeline.

title: Cell-based SSIM catches localized errors
text: Whole-frame SSIM >0.99 can hide 80x60 cell failures (e.g., missing label, wrong color box). Compute per-cell SSIM (8x6 grid on 64x36 signature); report 5th percentile (cell_p05). If cell_p05 < 0.8 while mean >0.92, flag and extract worst-cell ROI for vision review.
how: In review.py vision review, after whole-frame SSIM pass, compute cell SSIM via OpenCV. If cell_p05 < 0.8, crop worst cell region from full-res frames and send to Gemini for targeted inspection ("Is the title missing?").

title: Missing Content 'Flatness' Check
text: Detect AI generation failures by identifying cells where the original/intended scene had high luma spread (detail) but the render is 'flat' (low standard deviation). If a cell's luma spread is <4 and the original was >8, the content is missing or blurred. This catches 'blobby' AI subjects.
how: Add to 'preflight.py'. Sample the 'lab' look UI panels; if the 'terminal typing' area is detected as 'flat' during an animation, it indicates a rendering stall.

title: Onset-Based Audio Alignment
text: Align audio by creating an 'onset curve' (RMS loudness change every 10ms). Correlate the curves of two audio tracks to find the exact millisecond offset. This is more robust than simple peak detection for aligning voiceovers with background SFX cues.
how: Use in 'mix.py' to verify that Charon's voice starts exactly when the 'kinetic title' appears, accounting for any TTS generation silence.

title: Least-Squares Face Alignment
text: When replacing a subject (e.g., in mythology stories), use a transform (scale, x, y) that minimizes the residual distance between face boxes in the clip vs. the original composition. This ensures the character stays centered and at the correct scale across different generated clips.
how: In 'compose.py', after Muse generates a character clip, use this fitting logic to automatically calculate the GSAP 'scale' and 'translate' values to keep the face consistent.

title: Face size grading thresholds
text: Grade presenter face height as share of frame: ≥0.25 passes (holds), 0.15–0.25 warns (slides), <0.06 fails (floor). For cast-in-crowd shots use 0.15 as fail threshold. Sample 4 faces/sec, require ≥3 faces over ≥1s to judge a shot.
how: Add to preflight.py when avatar/talking-head videos arrive: run faceBoxes on rendered clips, compute faceSummary, reject if verdict != 'pass'. Thresholds are constants in face.ts.

title: Ink measurement for text region detection
text: Given RGB crop, compute per-pixel ink (via drawn.contrast), find bounding box of all ink pixels, share = ink_pixels / total_pixels, group consecutive ink rows into lines (y, height). Returns null if no ink. Works on 3-channel RGB, 8-bit.
how: Integrate into preflight.py caption check: crop caption box from rendered frame, run measureInk, verify share > 0.01 and line count matches expected. Reject if ink bounds exceed safe zone or lines missing.

title: SumOf nesting for ffmpeg select expressions >50 terms
text: ffmpeg 8 rejects deeply nested expressions. sumOf() joins terms with '+' up to 50; beyond that it recursively nests halves: '(first_half)+(second_half)'. Keeps all terms, avoids 'Error while parsing expression'. Used for frame selection and snapshot timing.
how: Replace current select expression builder in media.py/plan.py with sumOf logic. Ensures reliable frame picking for preflight stills (100+ frames) and snapshot commands (100+ times).

title: Hand landmark tracking via MediaPipe in headless Chrome
text: Download pinned MediaPipe WASM (11.5 MB) and hand_landmarker.task (7.8 MB) once. Run HandLandmarker in Chrome with software WebGL, CPU delegate, VIDEO mode. Extract palm (mean of wrist+4 knuckles), index tip, pinch (thumb+index mid) per frame at up to 30 fps, 15s max. Pick largest hand or specific side.
how: Add hands.ts logic to a new measure/hands.py: spawn Chrome via existing browser manager, serve pinned files via local HTTP intercept, decode frames to JPEG, get 21 landmarks per frame. Use for gesture detection in generated clips or UI interaction demos.

title: Audio kind inference from filename keywords
text: Classify audio files by path tokens: 'bgm'/'music'/'soundtrack' → bgm; 'sfx'/'fx'/'sound' (not soundtrack) → sfx; 'voice'/'narrat' → voice; default bgm. Enables automatic provider routing and manifest typing.
how: Apply in adoptExistingAssets when scanning assets/; use in mix.py to auto-duck bgm under voice, boost sfx at cues.

title: Transcript-driven cut list compiler
text: Parse word-level transcript (start/end timestamps) to generate cut ranges: keep explicit ranges, remove filler words (configurable list), remove silence gaps > threshold (default 0.15s pad), remove specific word indices or time ranges. Enforce minimum segment duration (0.2s) and merge adjacent ranges. Output ffmpeg-ready start/end pairs rounded to 6 decimal places.
how: Add cutlist.mjs as a new step after voice gate in plan.py/compose.py; feed Gemini TTS transcript (or Parakeet output) to compileCutList with --remove-fillums, --cut-silence 0.3; pass resulting ranges to render chunking.

title: Parametric 3D LUT generation from intent keywords
text: Build .cube LUT (default 33^3, max 65^3) from params: exposure (-2..2), contrast (-1..1), temperature (-1..1), tint, saturation, vibrance, lift/gamma/gain (blacks/shadows/highlights/whites), split-tone. Map intent words: 'warm cinematic' → temperature 0.18, contrast 0.08, saturation 0.04; 'punchy' → contrast 0.22; 'dark moody' → exposure -0.12, contrast 0.12.
how: Add cube-build.mjs to compose_lab.py grade step; let plan.py emit grade intent per scene; generate LUT at render start, apply via ffmpeg lut3d filter. Validate with cube-validate.mjs in preflight.

title: Reuse candidate ranking with lexical overlap
text: List project + global assets for a type, rank by token overlap with intent (icon↔image adjacency), cap 8 per scope, preserve recency for ties. Return handles: project uses manifest path, global uses SHA prefix (--reuse <sha16>). Report truncated flag and total counts. Zero-overlap candidates still listed (no hard filter).
how: Call listCandidates in ideas.py/research.py when searching for B-roll/music/SFX; show formatted list in dashboard; pass chosen handle to resolve step.

title: Bundled SFX library with health check and recovery
text: Manifest.json maps keys to {file, description, duration}. inspectBundledSfxAssets() verifies every file exists; throws typed BundledSfxAssetsError with fix command 'npx hyperframes skills update media-use'. Provider ranks manifest entries via token overlap, returns localPath. Symlink-safe path resolution via realpath.
how: Adopt bundled-sfx-provider.mjs for mix.py SFX cues; run health check at doctor.py interval; add recovery command to setup docs.

title: Structured segment markdown for quality gates
text: Segment file format: `## S01 · 0.00–2.40 s · title` headings with optional `Pixels: rebuilt|reused|regenerated`, `Regenerated: x,y,w,h` (pixels or 0-1 shares), `Drawn: x,y,w,h [a–b s]`, `Copy:` (has drawn text). Parse into Segment[] with id, start, end, title, pixels, regenerated region, drawn boxes, copy flag.
how: Emit segments.md from plan.py; feed to preflight.py for per-segment still audit; use in review.py to verify regenerated regions match spec.

title: Atomic config file locking with stale detection
text: Lock file at ~/.hyperframes/config.json.lock using open(wx) + write token (pid-timestamp-random). Wait 25ms via Atomics.wait; if lock older than 5s or wait >10s, throw HF_SETTINGS_LOCKED with path. Never auto-delete another's lock; only human can remove. Release in finally block.
how: Wrap config writes in doctor.py, publish.py, and any concurrent CLI commands with withFileLock; prevents corruption during auto-update.

title: Codex CLI image generation provider pattern
text: Use `codex exec --enable image_generation` (or legacy imagegenext) with project_root_markers=[] to isolate runs. Save to private temp folder (media-use-codex-<pid>-<ts>.png); verify file exists post-run, else fetch freshest file from $CODEX_HOME/generated_images/ newer than start time (2s skew). Auth via ~/.codex/auth.json presence, not TTY command.
how: Add as fallback provider in media-use ladder after mflux.local; gate with --local-only flag. Requires user ChatGPT subscription (paid), so keep optional.

title: Frame-precise cut boundaries prevent one-frame drift
text: When converting transcript times to ffmpeg -ss/-to, keep full float precision (e.g., 12.866666666666667 → 12.866667). Rounding to milliseconds (12.867) pushes start past the intended frame at 30fps, causing one-frame late start.
how: In pace.py or cutlist integration, use round3(n) = Math.round(n*1000)/1000 (3 decimal places) not millisecond rounding. Pass exact values to ffmpeg.

title: Duck lane interpolation preserves gain at arbitrary clip start
text: duckLane() computes initial volume at clipStart by interpolating between keyframes before and after. If clip starts during attack, gain is mid-ramp; during speech, ducked; during release, rising; after, base. Ensures seamless music bed regardless of edit offset.
how: When placing music bed under voice, compute duck keyframes once for full composition, then for each music clip segment call duckLane(clipStart) to get correct local envelope.

title: Error diffusion pointSize >1 fills blocks from center sample
text: With pointSize=2, each 2×2 block uses the center pixel (offset 1,1) for luminance decision, then fills entire block with palette color. Error diffuses to neighboring blocks. Preserves alpha channel unchanged.
how: For lab-look HUD elements, use pointSize=2 or 3 to create blocky, retro-terminal dither without per-pixel noise. Combine with palette ['#000000', '#00ff00', '#008800'] for green-on-black depth.

title: Grade analysis clamps adjustments to safe limits per parameter
text: Exposure ±2, contrast ±1, whites/blacks ±1, temperature/tint ±1. Suggestions derived from YAVG, percentile spread (YHIGH-YLOW), chroma averages. Shadow clip risk = avg(YLOW≤16), highlight clip risk = avg(YHIGH≥235). HDR transfer (smpte2084) triggers warning.
how: In review.py, after grade analysis, only auto-apply if all adjusts are within ±0.5. Larger suggestions → human flag. Log measured note for trend tracking.

title: Media index generation for .media folder with aligned columns
text: generateIndexContent() reads manifest records, computes column widths (id, type, dur, dims, path, desc), outputs markdown table. regenerateIndex() writes to .media/index.md. Handles missing duration (—), icons (svg), transparent flag.
how: In doctor.py or post-render, call regenerateIndex(projectDir). Use in dashboard to show asset inventory. Extend manifest.mjs to track our downloaded/generated assets.

title: HeyGen CLI error classification with actionable remediation
text: classifyHeygenError() distinguishes not_found (ENOENT/command not found), not_authenticated (401/unauthorized), outdated (<v0.3.0 or unknown flag --headers), rate_limited (429/quota/throttle). Returns user-facing message with install/login/update command. reportHeygenFailure() tracks telemetry, stashes remediation for one-time display.
how: If we integrate HeyGen for avatar/video, wrap all CLI calls with this. In doctor.py, check heygen version on startup. Show remediation once via consumeHeygenRemediation().

title: Parakeet-TDT 0.6B via MLX beats Whisper on accuracy and speed
text: NVIDIA Parakeet-TDT 0.6B (parakeet-mlx) achieves 6.05% avg WER vs Whisper-large-v3 7.44% (~19% better), 4.73% vs 5.96% on noisy audio, and 5-10x faster. Verified on 24GB Mac: 8s audio transcribed in ~3s with native word timestamps (sub-word tokens merged to words). WhisperX (CPU-only) is the fallback. Cohere Transcribe 2B tops leaderboard but MLX quants produced multilingual garbage and ran 40-70x slower (live-tested 2026-07).
how: Replace whisper.cpp in transcribe step with parakeet-mlx for transcript-driven cut lists (transcript-cut). Install: uv venv ~/.venvs/parakeet && uv pip install parakeet-mlx. Use --output-format json for word timestamps. Falls back to whisperx on CPU-only machines.

title: FLUX --low-ram streams components to avoid swap (20s vs 90min on 24GB)
text: FLUX.1 schnell int4 (flux-schnell-mflux-q4) on 24GB Mac: without --low-ram, T5-XXL + transformer blow past 24GB into swap (768x512 took 90min). With --low-ram (streams components from disk), 512x512 in ~20s at 7.6GB free. --low-ram is MANDATORY at this tier. Official FLUX repos are HF-gated; use community 4-bit re-upload (dhairyashil/FLUX.1-schnell-mflux-4bit) that includes VAE. Runner resolves repo to local snapshot before --path; bare repo id breaks mlx unflatten.
how: If ever running FLUX locally (e.g., offline fallback), enforce --low-ram flag and point --path at non-gated community 4-bit repo. Add to imagegen provider: verify model_path resolves to local snapshot, not bare HF id. Cache snapshot to avoid re-download.

title: Pinned CDN manifest for reproducible asset resolution
text: theSVG manifest pinned to glincker/thesvg@e5957fa742c1ebf6da07ac40665bdd01d8add35f via jsDelivr CDN. Manifest ~3.3MB, capped at 20MB download. Single fetch per process (memoized). On network failure, manifest reset to null so next call retries. Redirects to private hosts (127.0.0.1) rejected via redirect: 'manual' and location check. Entry selection: normalized slug > title > alias, ties broken by collection rank (brands > community > aws > azure > gcp > k8s > auth-badges).
how: Apply to any external asset catalog (Muse templates, FLUX model index, SFX library): pin commit hash, fetch manifest once per run, cap download size, reject private redirects. In compose_lab.py, use for template gallery: fetch pinned manifest, match by normalized slug/title, prefer 'brands' collection. Cache in memory with reset hook for tests.

title: Model selection by available RAM with explicit quality rank and demotion ladder
text: selectModel() gates on specs.availableRamMB (not total RAM), GPU presence, and VRAM. Models declare explicit `rank` when quality ≠ size (Parakeet rank 0 beats Whisper rank 1 despite smaller footprint). selectModelLadder() returns every fitting model best-first; callers walk it so a missing binary, gated weights, or OOM demotes to next tier instead of killing the local path. Apple Silicon unified memory counts as VRAM.
how: Adopt in doctor.py/preflight.py: probe available RAM/VRAM before each render, pick best local model (or cloud fallback) per capability. Wrap external API calls (Gemini, Muse, Cloudflare) in same ladder: try primary, demote on 429/5xx/timeout. Store specs in brain.jsonl for reuse.

title: Multi-tier logo resolver with license gating and placeholder rejection
text: Three tiers tried in order: 1) theSVG (pinned CDN manifest glincker/thesvg@e5957fa, only 10 accepted SPDX licenses: CC0, MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-3, ISC, CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY-SA-4.0, CC-BY-ND-4.0, MPL-2.0, Unlicense). Brand mark preferred over auth badges via collection rank. 2) GitHub org avatar (known orgs only, no guessing). 3) DuckDuckGo favicon (size >500 bytes to reject DDG globe placeholder). Single manifest fetch per process. Variant support (mono, wordmark) with miss if brand lacks it.
how: Replace ad-hoc logo fetch in thumb.py/cover generation with this cascade. Add theSVG manifest pin to deps. Filter by accepted licenses. For favicon, download to temp, verify >500 bytes, then copy to .media/images. Cache manifest in memory per run. Expose variant param for mono/wordmark needs.

title: LTX video generation ladder with partial discard and home-dir execution
text: ltxVideoGenerate() walks selectModelLadder("videogen") (LTX 2.3 int4 q4 on 16GB+, int8 q8 on 32GB+). Each tier: check binary on PATH, build argv via tokenized template (spaced prompt stays single arg), run in $HOME (avoids project folder named like model id being read as model), 30min timeout. On failure (missing binary, non-zero exit, no output file), discard partial MP4 (unlink + discardPrivateOutput) before demoting. Errors logged per tier. preferTier pins to one tier. Verified: 512x320x33 frames in ~19min cold on 24GB Mac.
how: Add as local video gen fallback in visuals pipeline (when Muse/Cloudflare unavailable). Install ltx-2-mlx in CI. In compose_lab.py, add provider that calls ltxVideoGenerate for B-roll clips. Use width/height multiples of 64. Set frames=33 (1.375s at 24fps) for short inserts. Capture stderr for doctor.py diagnostics.

title: Favicon size filter rejects DuckDuckGo placeholder (500 bytes)
text: faviconSearch() downloads from icons.duckduckgo.com/ip3/{domain}.ico, checks body.byteLength >= 500 (DDG placeholder is ~120 bytes). Verified bytes written to temp file, then handed as localPath (freeze step copies instead of re-downloading). Single network round-trip. Returns low_res: true in provenance.
how: Add to thumb.py/asset fetch: after any favicon/ICO download, verify size >500 bytes before accepting. Log rejection with bytes count. Applies to brand/logo fallback in cover generation. Prevents placeholder images polluting thumbnails.

title: Two-Tier Preference Promotion
text: Store preferences (aspect ratio, voice, style) at project level first. Promote a value to 'user-tier' (global default) only after it's been confirmed in 2+ distinct projects (PROMOTE_AT=2).
how: Update `brain.jsonl` logic. When a user confirms a style in `Studio360` (Telegram) for a new video, check if that style has been used in other projects before setting it as the studio-wide default.

title: Secure Media Fetching
text: Validate every redirect target against a BlockList of private/internal IP ranges (127.0.0.1, 192.168.x.x, etc.) and enforce a strict byte cap on streams to prevent 'lying' content-length headers.
how: Add `isPublicMediaUrl` check to `scout.py` and `research.py` before downloading any external tech news assets or thumbnails to protect the internal network.

title: Openverse SFX Integration
text: Search and pick CC0/CC-BY sound effects from Openverse API. Includes a penalty-based ranking system (prefers shorter clips and CC0) and an automated CREDITS.md generator for CC-BY attribution.
how: Integrate into `mix.py`. Use the `searchOpenverseSfx` logic to find cues based on Gemini's scene plan, then use `writeSfxCredit` to maintain the attribution file automatically.

title: TF-IDF Media Ranking
text: Rank local assets using tokenization, singularization (plural to singular), and TF-IDF scoring. Weights 'strong' fields like IDs/Titles 3x higher than descriptions or tags.
how: Apply to our 'shared brain' search. Instead of simple keyword matching in `research.py`, use this ranking to find the most relevant previous 'lessons' or assets.

title: Model Demotion Ladder
text: A 'ladder' pattern for AI generation: attempt the highest quality model first (e.g., FLUX-schnell), and if it fails (OOM, missing binary), demote to the next tier rather than failing the job.
how: In our image generation scripts, implement a fallback chain: if Cloudflare FLUX is down or hits a limit, automatically fall back to Pollinations or a local model if available.

title: Token-to-Word Timestamp Merging
text: Merge sub-word tokens (from models like Parakeet-MLX) into word-level timestamps by joining tokens that don't start with a space to the previous word.
how: If we move from Gemini TTS to local models for transcription or alignment, use `mergeTokensToWords` to ensure our 'word light-up' captions remain frame-accurate.

title: Search Miss Logging
text: Record 'misses' (failed searches) in a JSONL file including the intent and type. This provides a data-driven list of what assets (BGM, SFX, clips) the studio needs to acquire.
how: Add `recordMiss` to our asset search functions. Periodically review `misses.jsonl` to identify gaps in our 'mythology' or 'tech' asset libraries.

title: Shell-Safe ffprobe Metadata Extraction
text: Use `execFileSync` with literal arguments instead of `exec` to prevent shell injection via malicious filenames. Specifically selects video streams while ignoring attached covers/thumbnails.
how: Update `review.py` and `preflight.py`. Replace any shell-based `ffprobe` calls with this literal array approach to safely handle user-uploaded or scraped filenames.

title: Recipe freeze for recurring formats
text: Freeze an approved run as a named recipe: frame.md (design spec), storyboard-skeleton.md (structure with content blanked to '<fill in: this video's content for the "Hook" beat...>'), brief-skeleton.md (reusable frontmatter keys only), and recipe.json (version, workflow, style_preset, destination, aspect, language, voice). Re-freezing bumps version and archives old folder as <name>@v<N>.
how: Add a freeze step after Telegram approval in publish.py: serialize the run's frame.md, STORYBOARD.md, BRIEF.md into .media/recipes/<slug>/ with skeletonization. Use for Kaise Tech, Puraan Ki Katha, Aage Suno templates.

title: Two-tier storage: project recipes + global recipes
text: Recipes live in project .media/recipes/<name>/ (committed) and user ~/.media/recipes/<name>/ (global). Freeze writes to project tier, then copies to user tier (promotes immediately). useRecipe() imports from user tier into project if missing, copies frame.md to project root, returns skeleton paths. Project tier wins on conflict.
how: Mirror for our templates: project-level .media/recipes/ for page-specific formats, global ~/.studio/recipes/ for shared formats (e.g., common hook structures). doctor.py can sync or validate.

title: 30 ms fade at concat boundaries
text: When concatenating voice segments, apply 30 ms fade-in/out at each splice (scaled down for short segments, skipped if degenerate). Prevents clicks. fadeFilterFor(duration, {fadeIn, fadeOut}) returns ffmpeg afade filter chain or null.
how: In mix.py, when stitching TTS segments (or voice + SFX), compute fade flags per segment (first: fadeOut only, middle: both, last: fadeIn only) and inject into ffmpeg filter graph before loudness mastering.

title: Search over manifest for quick asset lookup
text: searchRecords(records, query, {page, pageSize}) does case-insensitive substring match on id, description, entity, type. Returns paginated results with total, pages, page. Used for CLI search commands.
how: Add search to our dashboard (or CLI) over .media/manifest.jsonl to find assets by description, type, or entity. Integrate into thumb.py for quick thumbnail asset selection.

title: Stats with time window and cross-project reuse
text: buildStats({projectDir, days}) reads manifest.jsonl and misses.jsonl, filters by timestamp (--days window), aggregates resolves by type, source, provider, via; computes hit_rate = resolves/(resolves+misses); top 5 missed intents per type; global cache assets, disk bytes, cross-project reuse count (records with provenance.reused_by).
how: Extend stats.py to compute pipeline stats: render success rate, provider usage, common failures, asset reuse across pages. Add --days flag. Feed into 09:00 report and dashboard.

title: Windows binary shadowing protection
text: On Windows runners, set 'process.env.NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath = "1"'. This prevents the system from looking in the current working directory for executables before searching the PATH, mitigating security risks and accidental binary shadowing.
how: Add this environment variable assignment to the entry point of our runner or doctor.py script.

title: Four-tier media resolution cascade
text: Resolve media needs using a strict priority: 1. Project manifest (exact match), 2. Entity match (reusing specific brand assets), 3. Global cache (cross-project reuse), 4. External providers (Search first, then Generate).
how: Refine research.py and scout.py to check our 'shared brain' and local asset folders before hitting Cloudflare or Muse APIs.

title: Candidate reuse prompts
text: Before generating new media, list 'similar' existing assets from the global cache to the operator or agent. This encourages reuse of existing high-quality assets and saves generation credits.
how: In the Telegram approval flow (Studio360), show thumbnails of 2-3 similar existing assets when asking to approve a new generation.

title: Orphan asset detection via substring matching
text: Identify unused media by performing a substring match of asset filenames against all project HTML/composition files. This 'ponytail' approach avoids complex HTML parsing while effectively flagging files safe for pruning.
how: Add to doctor.py or a new prune.py; scan the .media folder and check if filenames appear in any compose_lab.py generated HTML strings.

title: System dependency doctor
text: Implement a --doctor command that verifies the environment: FFmpeg/FFprobe presence, Node version (>=18), and API authentication status. It should provide specific 'fix' strings for the user (e.g., 'brew install ffmpeg').
how: Expand preflight.py to include system-level binary checks and credential validation with actionable error messages.

title: Provider tier telemetry for cost tracking
text: Classify every media resolve by provider_tier: local (bundled), network_free (Openverse), network_paid (HeyGen). Non-Heygen providers carry tier only; Heygen adds auth_method (oauth|api_key). Enables per-video cost estimation and budget alerts.
how: In resolve.py, capture telemetry event media_use_resolve with provider_tier. Log to brain.jsonl. Add cost estimate in plan.py based on tier and duration.

title: Concurrent resolve credit race protection
text: When multiple SFX resolves run in parallel, each must append its own credit line atomically. Test uses a barrier directory + SharedArrayBuffer wait until both processes have read CREDITS.md, then writes. Prevents interleaved or lost credit lines.
how: In resolve.py, if running parallel resolves, use a file-based lock (fcntl) around CREDITS.md append, or serialize resolves. Simpler: run resolves sequentially in our single-worker pipeline.

title: Safe registry installer with edit preservation
text: Install registry items (blocks/components) to project folders while blocking unsafe targets (symlinks escaping project, node_modules, .git, .claude, config files). Preserves local edits via SHA256 lockfile (hyperframes.lock.json). Force flag overwrites. Records every file for multi-item dependency installs.
how: Use hyperframes add <item> --project <dir> for template blocks. In compose.py, before rendering, run hyperframes add for required components. Lockfile prevents re-download of edited files.

title: Bounded file reading for cache safety
text: readBoundedRegistryFile(path, maxBytes) opens fd, fstats to verify regular file and size <= maxBytes, then reads in 64KB chunks up to maxBytes+1. Throws if exceeded. Prevents OOM from corrupted/huge cache entries.
how: In cache.py (if any), replace open().read() with bounded read for manifest/index files. Set maxBytes=10MB for JSON manifests.

title: Compound-word expansion for Hinglish queries
text: Split query tokens when both halves exist in catalog vocabulary (countdown → count + down); join adjacent tokens when compound exists. Inferred tokens weighted 0.35× so exact match still wins. Prevents disjoint result sets from spelling differences.
how: In scout.py/research.py keyword extraction, apply expandCompounds before matching against brain.jsonl tags. Use existing vocabulary from brain to gate splits/joins.

title: Plural folding without aggressive stemming
text: Fold only regular plurals (ies→y, es→e, s→'' guarded for press/status/axis). Porter stemmer merges distinct concepts (counter→count). Keeps query precision: adding detail (counts, pulses) doesn't degrade results.
how: Add singularize() to research.py tokenization before matching against brain tags. Use the same PLURAL_RULES list; skip words ≤3 chars.

title: Consent-gated local model downloads with pinned revision
text: Model download (33 MB) only after explicit user consent; never auto. Revision pinned (ea104dacec62c0de699686887e3f920caeb4f3e3) with SHA256 per file. Status states: ready/declined/not-asked/unavailable. Agent/CI gets non-interactive message with --yes flag.
how: Apply to any future local model (e.g., background removal, Parakeet ASR): wrap download in ensureLocalModel(), gate behind config flag, pin revision+SHA256, expose status command.

title: Tiered search strategy: word → local semantic → hosted
text: Word ranker (free, offline) runs first; if matches < threshold, local semantic (33 MB model, opted-in); finally hosted API. Each tier returns ranked names with scores. Caller decides cutoff.
how: In compose.py block selection: try rankByWords against local registry index; if top score < 0.3, call localSemanticRanking; if unavailable, fall back to Gemini-hosted embedding. Log tier used.

title: Safe path validation for asset writes
text: Installer rejects absolute paths, '..' segments, Windows drive letters, hidden folders, node_modules, tool config files (lockfiles, agent instructions), and paths outside allowed dirs (compositions, assets, models, lib). Validates at install time, not just schema.
how: Add assertSafeTarget() to mix.py/thumb.py/compose.py before writing any generated asset. Define STANDARD_INSTALL_DIRS for project. Reject writes to .git, .env, package.json, etc.

title: ResizeObserver for container-relative smear updates
text: Motion-blur copies re-read perspective and transform when the element's box changes (cqw units, responsive layouts). ResizeObserver callbacks fire on resize; live count tracked to avoid detached subtree leaks.
how: In compose_lab.py, after attaching motion blur to a responsive panel, register a ResizeObserver that re-samples the element's computed perspective and transform on layout shift. Clean up observers on scene unmount.

title: Declarative blur attribute with polling and warnings
text: Elements with data-hf-motion-blur='{"samplesPerFrame":4}' auto-attach when their composition's timeline registers on window.__timelines. Polling budget 250×32ms; warns once for unclaimed targets, malformed JSON, unknown keys, nested targets, duplicate timelines, or mismatched frame rates. Strips attribute from clones to prevent double-blur.
how: Adopt a similar declarative pattern in our scene JSON: mark elements with "motionBlur": {"samplesPerFrame": 8}. In compose_lab.py, when a composition mounts, scan for marked elements and attach blur once. Emit structured warnings to brain.jsonl for review.

title: Registry fetcher with stale-while-revalidate and byte budget
text: 24h TTL cache keyed by URL hash; on network failure serves stale entry instead of failing. skipCache forces revalidation but still falls back to stale. Item downloads share a 512 MB budget, cancel streams on overflow. Retries 3× for transient errors (ECONNRESET, DNS), not for TLS failures. Cache isolated per registry URL to prevent poisoning.
how: Wrap our Muse/Cloudflare/Pollinations asset fetches in a fetch_with_budget(url, budget) that enforces byte limits, cancels streams, retries transient errors, and caches manifests with stale fallback. Add per-vendor budget in doctor.py preflight.

title: Shared library byte-consistency check
text: Test ensures every block that installs compositions/lib/shaders.iife.js ships identical bytes. Divergence would downgrade other blocks. Also verifies each shader block names a shader present in the bundle and includes THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt.
how: Add a CI step (or doctor.py check) that hashes our shared assets (GSAP plugins, shader chunks, font subsets) across all pages and fails if same target path has different content. Enforce license sidecar for third-party code.

title: Quiet/Burst Debounce Strategy
text: Use a dual-timer debounce for file system events: a 'Quiet' window (30ms) to wait for a single write to finish, and a 'Burst' window (300ms) to group multiple file changes (like a git checkout or bulk asset move) into a single rebuild trigger.
how: Apply these constants to our `doctor.py` or any future auto-render triggers to prevent 'flapping' where one change triggers five redundant render attempts.

title: Zero-Dependency WordPiece Tokenizer
text: Implement BERT-style WordPiece tokenization locally for text analysis. Includes normalization (lowercase, strip accents, isolate CJK characters), pre-tokenization (punctuation isolation), and greedy longest-match-first subword splitting. Avoids 300MB+ ONNX dependencies.
how: Add this logic to `research.py` to perform local keyword ranking or TF-IDF on script drafts without sending every intermediate string to Gemini.

title: Tiered CPU Priority Management
text: Use `os.setPriority` to manage system resources: `PRIORITY_LOW` for background tasks (scouting, stats), `PRIORITY_NORMAL` for renders, and `PRIORITY_ABOVE_NORMAL` for critical setup like browser installs. This prevents background lints or news-gathering from starving the main render process.
how: Update `scout.py` and `stats.py` to set themselves to low priority on startup. Add a priority boost in `doctor.py` when it performs system-level repairs or installs.

title: Linux Inode-Safe File Watching
text: On Linux, recursive file watches fail when files are replaced atomically (renamed), as the watch is tied to the inode. Instead, watch every directory in the tree individually. When a directory is 'renamed' or replaced, re-arm the watch on the new inode to maintain continuity.
how: If we build a local 'Live Preview' for the lab look, implement the `watchProjectTree` logic in a new `watcher.py` to ensure the preview doesn't break after an atomic save from an editor.

title: Topological Dependency Resolver
text: Resolve asset/component dependencies using a Depth-First Search (DFS) to produce a flat, ordered list. This ensures prerequisites are always installed/loaded before the items that depend on them, while detecting circular dependencies (A->B->A) and preventing duplicate loads in diamond graphs.
how: Use this in our 'shared brain' logic if we start creating complex 'Lab' props that depend on shared CSS themes or JS utility blocks.

title: Lazy Schema Compilation
text: Compile AJV/JSON schemas only on first use rather than at module import. This significantly reduces startup time for CLI tools that may only use a fraction of their available commands in a single run.
how: Wrap our schema validators in `plan.py` or `preflight.py` in a 'compiledOnFirstUse' getter pattern.

title: Share Freshness Detection
text: Detect if a published video is 'stale' by comparing the current local project content fingerprint against the checksum of the uploaded file. This identifies edits made to voiceovers or scripts after the last successful export/upload.
how: In publish.py, before showing the 'Published' status, compare the local SHA256 of the render with the metadata stored in the results.md or the remote API to flag if a re-upload is needed.

title: Loopback Security Boundary
text: Enforce a 'local-only' boundary for studio APIs by checking if the socket peer is a loopback address (::1 or 127.0.0.1) and validating the 'sec-fetch-site: same-origin' header. This prevents LAN-based attacks on the studio's file-system endpoints.
how: Add a middleware to our local asset/preview server that rejects any request where the remote IP is not loopback, protecting our project files from other devices on the same network.

title: Sequential Multi-Host Port Probe
text: Test port availability across 127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0, ::1, and :: sequentially rather than in parallel. Parallel binding races the socket close callback, causing spurious EADDRINUSE errors that block server startup, especially on Linux/Crostini.
how: Update the port selection logic in our server startup scripts to use a serial for-loop for host probes, ensuring each probe's 'close' event settles before the next host is tested.

title: Local GSAP Vendoring
text: Resolve GSAP and plugins (CustomEase, MotionPath) from a local 'vendor' directory or node_modules instead of a CDN. Use a tiered resolution: built-in artifact -> installed package -> CDN fallback.
how: In compose_lab.py, modify the HTML template to point to a local /vendor/gsap path served by our local asset server, ensuring the 'lab' look renders without internet dependency.

title: Race-Safe Bundle Reading
text: Use openSync with O_NONBLOCK followed by fstatSync to read internal artifacts. This prevents the process from hanging on named pipes or sockets and ensures that even if a file is replaced/renamed during the read (common in dev/build cycles), the file descriptor remains valid.
how: Implement a readBundleFile utility in our asset loader to wrap all internal JS/CSS reads, specifically for the HyperFrames runtime and GSAP plugins.

title: Tiered Runtime Resolution
text: Load the animation runtime using a priority ladder: 1. Live build (for development), 2. Inlined string (for production speed), 3. Pre-built IIFE artifact (fallback). This ensures the studio always has a working renderer regardless of the environment.
how: In the render engine, implement a loader that first checks for a local source file, then falls back to a hardcoded string in the script if the file is missing.

title: Preserve asset URLs with base-href in preview
text: Preview HTML keeps src="assets/pic.png" (not base64) and injects <base href="/api/projects/film/preview/"> so relative URLs resolve via the asset route. Nested compositions resolve ../assets correctly.
how: In compose_lab.py and thumb.py, when generating preview HTML for Telegram approval, set a base href to our asset CDN endpoint and keep relative URLs intact.

title: File-race-safe static asset serving
text: When serving bundle assets, read the file after existence check but before send; if the file is replaced mid-read, the already-checked bytes are still served (tested via rename during read). File descriptors closed on error or success.
how: Wrap our thumb.py and compose.py asset reads in a helper that snapshots file content after stat, serves that snapshot, and ensures fd cleanup via try/finally.

title: Atomic project folder swap with preview refresh
text: Replacing the entire project directory via renameSync triggers a watcher event (path:".", affectsPreview:true) that invalidates cached preview ETAGs; subsequent preview requests serve new content with new ETAG.
how: In publish.py and our Telegram approval flow, when a new version is approved, atomically rename the render output folder into the project root and emit a watcher event to refresh any open Studio previews.

title: Off-main-thread linting via subprocess
text: Project and page lint run in a separate process; in-process lint throws an error. The server spawns a worker, avoiding event-loop blockage for large projects.
how: Move our preflight.py HyperFrames layout audit and Gemini vision review into a subprocess (Node or Python) invoked via asyncio.create_subprocess_exec, with timeout and structured JSON output.

title: Path containment for static routes
text: Static handlers resolve request paths against bundle root; percent-encoded traversal (..%5c..%5c) is rejected with 404 before filesystem access. Tested on Windows and POSIX.
how: Add a middleware in our HTTP server (Cloudflare Workers or local preview) that normalizes and validates asset paths against an allowlist root before serving.

title: HEIC conversion gated by received-files record
text: Outside-project HEIC images are converted to .hyperframes/prepared-assets/heif/ only for developer-owned projects. Received projects (with received-files.json) skip conversion and warn; inside-project HEICs still convert.
how: In our image fetch pipeline (Muse, Pollinations), add a check for received-files.json before converting HEIC; if present and file not listed, serve original with warning and skip conversion.

title: Route-based cache policy
text: /assets/* (content-hashed) → public, max-age=31536000, immutable. /icons/*, /favicon.svg, HTML shell → no-store (icons) or no-cache (HTML) to allow revalidation without bfcache eviction. Bundles served uncompressed on loopback.
how: Configure Cloudflare Workers / Cloudflare Pages headers: immutable for hashed assets in /static/, no-cache for index.html, no-store for dynamic previews. Disable compression for small JS bundles.

title: CSP framing protection on all HTML responses
text: Every HTML response (including 500 error page) includes Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self' and X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, preventing clickjacking of Studio shell.
how: Add a global middleware in our preview and dashboard servers that injects these headers on all text/html responses.

title: Project history retry with exponential backoff and host-app isolation
text: History open retries on busy/closed errors: first request waits undefined, subsequent waits 0ms; never opens history if HYPERFRAMES_DESKTOP_PROJECT env set (host app owns it). Prevents lock contention across processes.
how: In doctor.py or a new history manager, wrap project-state loads with retry (max 3, 0ms then 100ms) and skip if DESKTOP_PROJECT env present. Add to brain.jsonl as resilience pattern.

title: Remote GIF download with magic-byte validation and path filter
text: Downloads only if URL path ends with .gif (not query/fragment); writes body to temp, checks GIF89a/GIF87a header, discards non-GIF bodies, cleans temp dir. Prevents SSRF and corrupt asset injection.
how: In compose_lab.py asset fetch: before downloading, verify url.path.endswith('.gif'); after download, read first 6 bytes == b'GIF89a' or b'GIF87a'; else delete and log. Apply to Muse/Cloudflare asset pulls.

title: Render cancellation cleans partial GIF output and sidecar
text: On cancel, waits for render to settle (late completion flag), then deletes both .gif and .meta.json. Handles race where executor writes files after abort signal. More thorough than current doctor.py sweep.
how: In review.py cancel path: after task.cancel(), await task with timeout, then unlink output_path and output_path.with_suffix('.meta.json') in try/finally. Add late_completion test.

title: Thumbnail browser reuse with origin isolation and CDP fetch enable
