text: Reuses browser per origin (not per request URL), passes server's own origin to acquireBrowser, enables CDP Fetch domain before navigation, clears element isolation after screenshot. Prevents cross-origin leaks and proxy refusals.
how: In thumb.py generate_thumbnail(): cache browser by origin, pass origin to Chrome launch, add CDP session.send('Fetch.enable') before page.goto(), evaluate clearElementScreenshotIsolation after screenshot. Reuse for Kaise Tech/Puraan Ki Katha thumbnails.

title: File-change SSE with affectsPreview flag and projectId labeling
text: SSE emits {path, affectsPreview, affectedCompositions[], projectId, version, writeToken?}. affectsPreview=true only after preview loaded asset; studio writes carry token for undo labeling; external writes get version for dedupe. Enables instant preview reload without full refresh.
how: Extend stats.py dashboard SSE: track loaded assets per preview session, compute affectsPreview on fs events, include projectId (channel slug), encode version via hash. Hook into publish.py for live thumbnail updates.

title: Strict host-header guard with allowed-hosts env and loopback allowlist
text: All routes return 403 if Host not in {localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1]} ∪ HYPERFRAMES_PREVIEW_ALLOWED_HOSTS; ignores X-Forwarded-Host. Tunnel writes require env var. Prevents DNS rebinding and unauthorized preview access.
how: Add middleware in publish.py/server (if any) or Cloudflare Worker: validate Host header against allowlist, reject with 403 and error naming missing env. Set HYPERFRAMES_PREVIEW_ALLOWED_HOSTS for ngrok/Cloudflare tunnels.

title: Project signature caching for thumbnail generation
text: createProjectSignature() walks project once; subsequent thumbnails reuse cached signature. Invalidated only on project folder rename. Avoids repeated fs scans per thumbnail.
how: In thumb.py: compute project_signature = hash(tuple(sorted(file_mtimes))) on first call, store in memory keyed by project_dir; invalidate on folder rename (watchdog event). Reuse for batch thumbnails.

title: DNS rebinding guard for local HTTP endpoints
text: Validate Host header against loopback names (localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1]) and optionally machine's LAN IPs when explicitly opted in. Rejects attacker-controlled hostnames resolving to 127.0.0.1.
how: In publish.py (Instagram webhook) and any local server, add middleware checking request.host against allowed list. Use same logic for Telegram webhook endpoint if exposed.

title: Viewport rewrite for installed fragments
text: When writing fragment HTML files, rewrite viewport meta and inline width/height to match host composition's data-width/data-height. Applies to all .html files written, not just requested block.
how: In compose.py after writing fragment HTML, call a rewrite function that reads host index.html for dimensions and updates viewport meta and CSS width/height in all written .html files.

title: Cross-process config refresh on request boundaries
text: Long-running server refreshes telemetry/config cache on every render start and SPA document serve. Clears both config memoization and derived boolean cache together to avoid stale mid-refresh state.
how: In doctor.py and any long-running process (publish.py scheduler), add a refreshConfig() call at start of each job iteration. Clear both raw config cache and derived settings cache atomically.

title: Thumbnail page pooling with versioned reuse
text: Reuse a single loaded preview page for multiple thumbnail captures at increasing timestamps; reload only when project version changes or seek goes backward. Idle pages close after 1s. Max 2 pages per URL. Avoids full navigation per thumbnail.
how: In thumb.py, replace per-thumbnail browser launch with a pool keyed by (previewUrl, projectSignature). Seek forward on same page; new page for backward seeks or version change. Close idle pages after 1s.

title: Shared Chrome process pool for thumbnails and renders
text: Thumbnail browser and render workers share one Chrome process via engine's browser pool. Launched with screenshot-optimized args and page-server origin pinning. Reused across captures until GPU mode or origin changes.
how: In doctor.py or a new browserPool.py, initialize a single Chrome instance at startup. Pass its CDP endpoint to both thumbnail capture (thumb.py) and video render (compose.py). Ensure same GPU mode and page-server origin.

title: Manual edits overlay for thumbnails and renders
text: Studio manual edits stored in .hyperframes/studio-manual-edits.json. Injected as script into thumbnail page and render body. Re-applied after seek. Allows post-render tweaks without re-authoring.
how: Add manual_edits.json support in compose.py. In thumb.py, inject edits script after page load and after seek. In compose_lab.py, pass edits as renderBodyScripts to producer. Editor UI writes JSON.

title: 60-day compatibility window for breaking changes
text: Define a transition timestamp (null = unscheduled). For 60 days after, allow both old and new workflows with clear notices. After window, default to new workflow but keep legacy updates for existing projects. Fail fast on invalid timestamp.
how: In doctor.py/config, add TRANSITION_NOTICE_RELEASE env. When rolling out YouTube upload or new caption format, set timestamp. In publish.py, check phase: unscheduled/compatibility/share. Show notice via logger. Keep legacy IG/FB paths for existing channels.

title: Share service state machine with async recovery
text: States: not_shared, rendering, uploading_source, uploading_video, checking, processing, ready, link_off, failed. On status, reconcile pending uploads before reading local state. Recovery: if pending upload exists, refresh it; if completed, mark ready. Never re-render on status check.
how: In publish.py/Telegram approval flow, model states explicitly. In stats.py, add reconcile_pending() before reading insights. For stuck uploads, implement refreshReviewExport equivalent: poll Meta API for reel status. Store pending_upload_id in brain.jsonl.

title: Plan-gated source sharing with video-only fallback
text: Source attachment (project files) requires paid plan. Free tier gets video-only. Explicit --video-only flag skips source prep entirely. On source failure (network, changed assets), error with 'Retry or use --video-only'. Default to video-only even when source sharing available.
how: In publish.py, add --video-only flag. Check Gemini free tier quota; if exceeded, force video_only. In thumb.py/cover generation, skip source upload. Error message: 'Source upload needs paid plan. Use --video-only for video only.'

title: Consent-gated first publish with explicit audience
text: First share requires explicit audience flag (--public/--team/--private). Unattended runs fail with audience_required. Existing links can be retrieved without re-consent. Audience change requires explicit manage action, not implicit on share.
how: In publish.py, for new channels (no channel_id in brain.jsonl), require --audience flag. In Telegram approval, add audience buttons. Store audience in channel record. Reject auto-approve if audience missing.

title: Project vs content fingerprint separation
text: Project fingerprint = code/structure (HTML, config). Content fingerprint = media assets (voice, images, edits). They change independently. Render reuse needs both. Content fingerprint computed via shareSourceFingerprint (media files). Project fingerprint via projectFingerprint (all source).
how: In brain.jsonl, store both per render. In ideas.py/research.py, when checking 'freshness', compare content fingerprint to last render. If only project changed (e.g., caption style), can reuse visuals. If content changed, full re-render.

title: Privacy-first telemetry with opt-out refresh
text: Telemetry events only include declared fields (no URLs, project paths). Read opt-out config fresh at each event; reset posture cache. Honor DO_NOT_TRACK and custom env. Errors in telemetry never block main flow. Use attempt_id for mutation tracking.
how: In stats.py/dashboard, wrap trackEvent with readConfigFresh()/resetTelemetryPostureCache(). Define ALLOWED_FIELDS per event. In doctor.py, add telemetry_opt_out check. Send only: client_surface, action, reason (from allowlist), attempt_id. Drop unknown reasons to 'other'.

title: Upload origin allowlist with fail-closed
text: Maintain hardcoded production S3 origins. Only trust them when all env vars match production (API URL, token URL, client ID). Custom deployments must set explicit HYPERFRAMES_REVIEW_UPLOAD_ORIGINS with valid HTTPS origins (no wildcards, userinfo, accelerated hosts). Empty override = fail closed.
how: In publish.py/upload_to_meta.py, define PRODUCTION_UPLOAD_ORIGINS. Before upload, validate destination URL against cliReviewUploadOrigins(). In doctor.py, add preflight check: if origins empty and not production env, error 'configure upload origins'.

title: Identity pinning during render
text: Capture auth token/owner at share start. If token or owner changes during render (e.g., another CLI login), abort with LOGIN_CHANGED. Prevents uploading to wrong account. Verified in test: mock token change mid-render -> reject.
how: In publish.py, before render, store auth_token_hash and owner_id. In render.py callback, re-verify; if mismatch, raise RuntimeError('Account changed during render'). Applies to IG/FB token refresh mid-upload.

title: Discovery hints for unknown agents prevent blind spots
text: When no vendor rule matches, detectAgentHints() emits agent_hint (from AI_AGENT/AGENT), term_program, and up to 16 sorted agent-ish env keys (keys only, never values). Credential-shaped values (sk-, AKIA, 16+ alnum) are dropped. Enables clustering unknown agents in analytics for later rule promotion.
how: Add runtime_detect.detect_hints() returning dict. In stats.py, include hints in run metadata. Monthly review of agent_env_hints frequency to identify new agents needing VENDOR_RULES. No code change in render path.

title: CI exclusion from percentage enrolment prevents metric noise
text: CI runs (detected via getSystemMeta().is_ci) are excluded from percentage bucketing (reason=excluded) but explicit HF_CANARY_* overrides still apply. Prevents ephemeral CI IDs from hopping cohorts and diluting rollout signal.
how: In doctor.py / GitHub Actions workflow, set STUDIO_CI=true. Canary resolver checks this flag; if true and no override, returns enabled=false, reason=excluded. Allows manual HF_CANARY_FEATURE=on in workflow for testing.

title: Never read secret values — only check env-var existence
text: All agent detection rules use `typeof env[KEY] === 'string'` or `env[KEY] === '1'` — never read the value. API keys (CODEX_API_KEY, BOBSHELL_API_KEY) explicitly ignored. Credential-shaped hints (sk-, AKIA, 16+ alnum) sanitized to null. Prevents accidental secret leakage in telemetry.
how: Audit studio code for any env var value reads (os.getenv). Replace with existence checks. In runtime_detect.py, use `key in os.environ` not `os.environ[key]`. Add sanitize_hint() for any user-facing hint values.

title: Agent/sandbox detection for environment-aware defaults
text: Detect 30+ coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, etc.) and sandboxes (gVisor, Docker, Firecracker, WSL) via env-var existence only — never read values. Rules ordered: specific (BOBSHELL_CLI) before generic (AI_AGENT). Gemini managed agent detected via /.agents/ directory + gVisor kernel. Returns agent_runtime and sandbox_runtime strings for logging and conditional behavior.
how: Create studio/ops/runtime_detect.py mirroring agent_runtime.ts logic. Use in doctor.py to tag runs (local vs CI vs managed). In compose_lab.py, auto-enable low-resource mode (FLUX --low-ram) when sandbox_runtime in {gvisor, docker}. In scout.py, suppress noisy GitHub Actions runs when agent_runtime=github_actions.

title: Stable bucket seed for consistent A/B cohorts across config wipes
text: Bucket seed (UUID) stored in install-state file survives config.json re-mint (telemetry ID roll). Both files in ~/.studio; deleting directory clears cohort. Fallback to anonymousId only on failed backfill. evaluateCanary(unitId=bucketSeed) ensures same install stays in same cohort for hook/thumbnail A/B tests.
how: In ideas.py A/B hook selector, use bucket_seed from ~/.studio/install_state.json (create on first run). Pass seed to canary evaluator for hook_variant_A vs B. Seed persists across git pulls and config resets.

title: Memoized canary decisions per render process
text: Decisions cached in Map keyed by canary name; cache invalidated only when telemetry posture changes (opt-in/out). Guarantees a render that starts enrolled finishes enrolled; telemetry events match actual code path. HF_CANARY_* overrides win over percentage but are marked forced=true for Studio to honour despite its own opt-out.
how: In compose.py render entry, call resolve_canary() once per feature; store in render context. Pass decisions to Studio via --canary-decisions JSON. Studio adopts wholesale (canaryDecisionsForStudio pattern) avoiding divergence.

title: PostHog-style flag properties with reasons for cohort analysis
text: canaryEventProperties() emits $feature/canary-<name>=true|false plus canary_reason_<name> (in_cohort, out_of_cohort, forced_on, forced_off, excluded, no_unit_id, telemetry_opt_out). Reason distinguishes developer override from genuine bucket flip — critical for accurate metric breakdown.
how: In stats.py render_complete event, include canary_flags dict with both enabled and reason. Dashboard cohort filter uses reason to separate forced vs organic. Enables clean retention comparison for A/B hook tests.

title: Identity persistence classification: durable / unknown / process_only
text: Each run classifies its anonymous ID persistence: 'durable' (loaded from pre-existing config), 'unknown' (minted this run and write succeeded — ephemeral HOME indistinguishable from genuine first run), 'process_only' (minted but write failed). This classification is emitted with every telemetry event, enabling accurate churn metrics.
how: Add a persistence_classification field to our render job metadata (in results.md or dashboard). Classify each run's project_id: 'durable' if project dir existed with valid brain.jsonl, 'unknown' if fresh scaffold with successful write, 'process_only' if disk full/permission error. Log classification in doctor.py's 10-min report.

title: DNS reachability check before sending; queue events when offline
text: Before each flush, a hostAnswers() probe checks DNS resolution. If DNS fails, events stay queued and flush() returns immediately without HTTP attempt. Next flush retries the probe. Prevents spurious network errors and log spam in air-gapped/CI environments.
how: In stats.py upload_stats(), before POSTing to Meta API or our dashboard endpoint, do a quick socket.getaddrinfo('graph.facebook.com', 443) with 2s timeout. If it fails, skip upload and log 'offline, queued'. Retry on next render completion or doctor.py run.

title: First-run telemetry notice before any tracking, written to stderr not stdout
text: showTelemetryNotice() runs before any trackEvent(). It persists telemetryNoticeShown=true in config first, then prints a disclosure banner to stderr (via diag.notice) so it never corrupts JSON stdout (--json). Users see the notice before any data leaves the machine.
how: Add a first-run check in cli entrypoint (or ideas.py first invocation): if ~/.studio/notice_shown not set, write it, then print a Hinglish/English banner to stderr explaining what data is collected (render metrics, no content), how to disable (studio telemetry off). Do this before any network call.

title: System metadata enrichment on every event (OS, CPU, memory, CI, Docker, agent runtime)
text: trackEvent() automatically adds: os, arch, node_version, os_release, cpu_count, cpu_model, cpu_speed, memory_total_mb, is_docker, is_ci, ci_name, is_wsl, is_tty, sandbox_runtime, agent_runtime, execution_harness_hint, agent_hint, term_program. Enables segmenting failures by environment (e.g., 'all OOMs on 8GB RAM CI runners').
how: Create a get_system_meta() in utils/sysinfo.py returning a dict with the above fields (use psutil, platform, os). Call it once per render in plan.py and attach to the render context. Include in stats.py events and doctor.py reports. Especially valuable: memory_total_mb, is_ci, is_docker for debugging FLUX --low-ram vs full.

title: Install-state file separate from config for monotonic breaker latches
text: A second JSON file (install-state.json) lives beside config.json and holds only markerAt, bucketSeed, and tripped breaker flags (e.g., deParallelRouterTrialFired). It survives config wipe/corruption, so a once-tripped breaker never re-enrolls the machine. The tripped bit is salvageable even when markerAt and bucketSeed are corrupt.
how: Create ~/.hyperframes/install-state.json for our pipeline breakers (e.g., 'router_trial_fired', 'flux_oom_demoted'). On config load, merge breaker flags from install-state into config (install-state wins). Never clear a true breaker flag unless explicit release command runs.

title: FlushSync via detached child process reading payload from file
text: flushSync() spawns a detached Node child (process.execPath, -e <script>) passing the event queue as a JSON file path. The child reads the file, sends the batch, and exits. Parent returns immediately. Handles Windows 32k command-line limit by keeping payload off the command line. Survives parent crash/SIGKILL.
how: Refactor stats.py's IG insights upload and dashboard report to use a similar pattern: on render completion, write a small JSON payload to /tmp/hf-stats-<uuid>.json, spawn a detached python -m studio.upload_stats <path>. Parent exits; child handles retries, backoff, and Meta API rate limits. Ensures stats upload even if main process is killed.

title: Beginframe no-damage reuse counters for render efficiency
text: Track beginFrameNoDamageFrames vs beginFrameHasDamageFrames in render telemetry. High no-damage ratio indicates effective frame reuse (static scenes, talking heads). Use to optimize capture strategy.
how: In HyperFrames render (compose_lab.py), expose beginframe damage stats via CDP. In review.py, parse and log ratio. Alert if no-damage < 20% for static-content videos.

title: Power-state sampling only when telemetry enabled
text: pmset subprocess spawn for battery/low-power mode runs at call site before trackEvent's shouldTrack guard. Must check telemetry opt-out first to avoid two blocking spawns per render on opted-out machines.
how: In review.py/render pipeline, wrap any system metric collection (battery, thermal, CPU freq) behind telemetry-enabled check. Move psutil/pmset calls inside telemetry-enabled branch.

title: Error redaction: paths → [path], query strings truncated
text: All error messages and stack traces in telemetry replace absolute paths with [path] and truncate URL query strings to '…'. Prevents PII leakage while preserving error structure.
how: Add redact_error() utility used in review.py, doctor.py, and any telemetry emit. Regex replace /home/user/... → [path], C:\Users\... → [path], and ?token=... → ?… in URLs.

title: Deduplicate error reporting across wrapper layers
text: trackCommandFailure deduplicates by error cause chain: same underlying Error reported once even if wrapped in multiple CliRuntimeError layers. Uses a Set of error messages per process.
how: In doctor.py and review.py, maintain a process-local set of error signatures (type + message). Before logging/telemetry, check set; skip if seen. Clear on new render job.

title: Structured skill/command telemetry with run_id correlation
text: cli_command and cli_command_result include run_id when available. skill_invoked and skill_command_ran separate skill invocation from CLI command retries. Skills_installed/outdated attached to commands after first check.
how: In publish.py and scout.py, generate run_id per job. Emit command_start/command_end with run_id. Track skill usage (e.g., 'mythology', 'tech') per render. Attach installed skill versions to command telemetry.

title: Run-ID correlation across pipeline stages
text: Generate a UUID (HYPERFRAMES_RUN_ID) at pipeline start (scout.py → ideas.py → plan.py → compose.py → review.py → publish.py) and pass via env. All telemetry events include run_id, enabling end-to-end tracing from topic selection to published Reel.
how: Modify doctor.py to generate run_id at 00:00 daily run; export to all child processes. Add run_id column to dashboard (Today, Runs, Approvals).

title: Worker auto-sizing telemetry
text: Log why N workers were chosen: cpu_based, memory_based, heap_based, frame_based, heap_limit_mb, exceed_heap_advisory. HyperFrames caps workers by per-worker heap budget (e.g., 6 workers on 24 GB / 4 GB heap). Prevents OOM and explains render speed variance.
how: In compose.py/compose_lab.py, compute worker count with same factors; write workers_bound_by, workers_heap_limit_mb to results.md. Add to dashboard Server view.

title: Lint streak tracking for recurring preflight issues
text: Track how many edits a preflight/lint finding survives before clearing. HyperFrames emits lint_rule_streak at 3 surviving edits (unresolved) and on clear. Surfaces rules agents repeatedly fail to fix (e.g., media_missing_data_start).
how: In preflight.py, persist finding fingerprints (file hash + rule code) in brain.jsonl. On each run, compare; increment streak. Log streak events to results.md. Add 'stuck findings' panel to dashboard.

title: Automated feedback prompt after N successful renders
text: Prompt owner for 0–10 rating + comment every 15 successful renders (configurable). Skip in CI/agent mode; auto-resolve after 10 s. HyperFrames logs rating, render_duration_ms, doctor_summary, and recent_render_ids for correlation.
how: In publish.py after successful upload, increment renderSuccessCount in brain.jsonl. If count % 15 == 0 and not CI, send Telegram poll with rating buttons + comment field. Store feedback in brain.jsonl.

title: Snapshot run telemetry by stage & keyframe distance
text: For each preflight snapshot, log frames, video_frames, decode_passes, shared_frames, longest_decode_seconds bucket (≤2s, ≤10s, ≤60s, >60s), and slow_stage (open|seek|video|capture). Pinpoints why some stills are slow (keyframe distance vs decode).
how: In preflight.py snapshot loop, wrap each stage with timers; compute keyframe distance via ffprobe. Log to results.md. Alert if slow_stage=seek and keyframe_distance>10s.

title: PII-Safe Telemetry Slugs
text: Avoid sending raw paths or filenames in telemetry. Use 'skill slugs' (e.g., `mythology-story-v1`) and count-based summaries for excluded files (e.g., `blocklisted_count: 3`) to maintain privacy while tracking pipeline health.
how: Update `stats.py` to aggregate file-level errors into counts per category rather than logging specific local file paths.

title: Sub-composition In-Point Shifting
text: When nesting a composition (like a recurring character scene), use `data-playback-start` to define which part of the sub-composition is visible. Nested clips must be shifted and clipped based on this in-point to ensure A/V sync.
how: Modify `compose.py` to support a `playback_start` attribute. When rendering, calculate `absStart` and `mediaStart` by subtracting the host's in-point from the child's authored start time.

title: Deterministic ID Minting (ensureHfIds)
text: Every animatable element needs a unique ID for GSAP targeting. If IDs are missing or duplicated during a 'split' operation, the timeline breaks. Use a dedicated pass to mint IDs (e.g., `hf-1`, `hf-2`) if they aren't present.
how: Add an `ensure_ids` function to our HTML generation pipeline. Before passing HTML to the renderer, scan for elements with the `.clip` class and assign unique IDs if the `id` attribute is missing.

title: Render Observability Counters
text: Track browser-level diagnostics during render: `consoleErrors`, `pageErrors`, `requestFailed`, and `memoryExhaustionDetected`. This distinguishes between a code bug and a resource/OOM failure.
how: In `review.py`, parse the Chrome/Muse browser logs for 'OOM' or 'Failed to load resource' strings. Map these to specific error codes in our `brain.jsonl` for automated repair by `doctor.py`.

title: Undo Receipt System
text: Save a 'receipt' after every automated edit (mutation). The receipt contains the filename, the previous content version hash, and a path to a backup file, allowing for safe multi-step rollbacks.
how: When `doctor.py` or a manual Telegram command edits a project, save a `.hf-receipt.json`. Implement a `rollback` command that uses this JSON to restore the exact previous state.

title: Parent-Child Visibility Guard
text: Logic to detect 'never visible' clips: a nested element whose absolute timing (e.g., 6-8s) falls entirely outside its parent container's window (e.g., 0-5s).
how: Integrate into `preflight.py` layout audit. If a UI panel in 'lab look' is scheduled to appear after its parent container has exited, flag the scene for an automated Gemini rewrite.

title: ASCII Timeline Debugger
text: Generate a terminal-based ASCII timeline using block characters (█) to visualize every track (video, audio, graphics) and their absolute start/end times. Includes labels for 'duration=media' or 'pending'.
how: Add to `preflight.py`. Before the final render, print a visual timeline to the logs. This helps the operator catch gaps in 'Kaise Tech' explainers or overlapping audio in 'Puraan Ki Katha' before wasting render credits.

title: Anchor-based Relative Timing
text: Support relative time expressions like 'after:#hook', 'start-of:#scene1', or '+0.5s' in HTML metadata. Includes frame-based offsets (e.g., '30f') converted via project FPS.
how: Implement in `compose.py` and `compose_lab.py`. Instead of Gemini hardcoding every second, the script can define scenes relative to the 'hook', allowing the intro to expand or shrink without breaking the rest of the video.

title: A/V Sync Drift Detection
text: Calculate `syncOffsetFrames` between video and audio clips sharing a `data-sync-origin`. Reports signed frame differences (e.g., +12f for late audio).
how: Add to `review.py`. For 'Puraan Ki Katha' stories where we use separate background clips and voiceovers, this ensures the visual 'clues' align perfectly with the Charon TTS voice.

title: Ponytail Concurrency Semaphore
text: A lightweight 4-line async gate (`createProbeGate`) to limit concurrent external process spawns (like ffprobe or yt-dlp) without heavy library dependencies.
how: Apply in `scout.py` and `research.py`. When the AI/tech radar scans 20+ trending GitHub repos or HF papers, this prevents CPU spikes and OS process-limit crashes.

title: Voice-to-Locale Auto-Inference
text: Standardize voice naming conventions where the first letter indicates the language (e.g., 'h' for Hindi, 'a' for US English). This allows the pipeline to automatically set the correct phonemizer/language code.
how: Adopt the 'hf_name' (Hindi) and 'af_name' (US) prefixing in our voice catalog. Update 'plan.py' to infer the 'lang' parameter from the chosen voice ID.

title: Diagnostic Routing to Stderr
text: Route all progress notices, warnings, and non-fatal logs to 'stderr'. Reserve 'stdout' strictly for machine-readable JSON payloads or the final video path to prevent log noise from corrupting automated pipes.
how: Audit all .py files; replace 'print()' for status updates with 'sys.stderr.write()'. Ensure only the final result is printed to 'stdout'.

title: Recursive TTS Token Overflow Splitting
text: Kokoro has a 510-token limit. If synthesis fails with an 'index out of bounds' error, the text should be split at the nearest sentence boundary (。！？!?\n) or space, synthesized in chunks, and concatenated.
how: Update our TTS logic to catch IndexError. Implement the 'split_for_retry' logic to recursively break down long scripts before sending them to the engine.

title: Python Runtime Path Isolation
text: Prevent local scripts from accidentally importing malicious or conflicting files in the working directory by removing the empty string (current dir) from 'sys.path' before execution.
how: In any subprocess calls to Python (like our research or scout scripts), prepend the code with: 'import sys; if sys.path and sys.path[0] == "": del sys.path[0]'.

title: Espeak-ng Mandarin Mapping Fix
text: If using espeak-ng for Mandarin (zh), the language code must be translated to 'cmn' (ISO 639-3) at the engine boundary, even if the public-facing API uses 'zh'.
how: In our TTS engine wrapper, add a mapping dictionary to translate 'zh' to 'cmn' specifically for the synthesis subprocess call.

title: Render Summary Clarity
text: Explicitly label 'Video Duration' vs 'Render Time' in completion summaries. Users often confuse wall-clock render time with the actual media duration. For directory outputs (PNG sequences), report frame counts instead of duration.
how: Apply this to our `review.py` logs. Ensure the final report clearly states 'X.Xs video rendered in Y.Ys' to help us track rendering efficiency vs. content length.

title: macOS Developer Tool Stub Detection
text: Before executing system commands like `git` or `cc` on macOS, verify they aren't 'stubs' (which trigger a GUI install dialog). Check if the command is in `/usr/bin` and if valid Command Line Tools or Xcode paths exist.
how: Add a preflight check in `doctor.py` specifically for Mac-based dev environments to prevent the studio server from hanging on a 'Developer Tools' popup.

title: Unattended Prompt Gate
text: Enforce a strict wrapper around CLI prompts (confirm, select, text) that throws a 'prompt_unavailable' error if the environment is unattended (CI, coding agent, or non-TTY). This prevents automated scripts from hanging indefinitely on a hidden question.
how: Update our CLI entry points to check `process.stdin.isTTY` and environment flags. Wrap any interactive prompts in a utility that fails-fast with a hint to use CLI flags instead.

title: Process-Aware Background Update
text: A background installer script that polls a 'running' directory for active PIDs. It waits for all CLI processes to exit before applying updates, ensuring the binary isn't replaced mid-render. It uses file-based locks to prevent concurrent update attempts.
how: In `doctor.py`, implement a check that registers the current PID in a temp folder. Our update script must verify this folder is empty before running `git pull` or `npm install`.

title: Detached Background Maintenance
text: Run maintenance tasks (like update checks or asset cleanup) in a detached child process using 'node -e' with 'unref()'. This allows the main pipeline to finish without waiting for 'housekeeping' tasks to complete.
how: Modify 'doctor.py' to launch its periodic disk cleanup and git syncs as detached processes, so the 'publish.py' flow isn't delayed by maintenance overhead.

title: Network change resilient asset validation
text: Re-request failed assets after network changes (simulated by referer header); only keep failures that persist (404). Drop transient cuts that load again (206). Also filters aborted images that reload successfully.
how: In doctor.py or preflight, retry failed asset URLs once with a brief delay; only flag if still failing. Use referer header for same-site proxy validation.

title: Proxy failure deduplication
text: Suppress repeated http_error (502) for same proxy URL when media_proxy_failed already reported. Keeps original missing (404) and unrelated proxy errors. Prevents noise from preview retries.
how: In review.py finding deduplication: if media_proxy_failed exists for a source, drop subsequent http_error with hf-proxy query for same source.

title: Seek clock collection for A/V sync verification
text: Extract GSAP timeline clocks at seek points (root and nested timelines) to verify timeline synchronization. Skips custom clocks returning null. Used to align media time with composition time.
how: In review.py, after render, run a seek pass collecting __timelines clocks; compare with expected timestamps from plan.json to detect drift.

title: Media proxy pre-resolution at composition size
text: Before render, scan for browser-hostile codecs (HEVC, VP9, etc.), transcode to H.264/VP8 at the exact composition box size (quantized to 2048x1218). Proxies are cached per project and box, avoiding runtime fallback.
how: Add to preflight.py: run `hyperframes check --pre-resolve-proxies` or integrate proxy transcode step using ffmpeg with composition dimensions from plan.json.

title: Runtime console error harvesting
text: Capture console.error/warn/info during headless seek; classify into media_proxy_fallback, webgpu_runtime_error, web_audio_bypass, media_proxy_unavailable. Deduplicate WebGPU validation warnings with repeat count.
how: Add a headless check pass in review.py using puppeteer/playwright; collect console messages, map to finding codes, merge into review report.

title: Multi-browser parallel sampling
text: Spawn second Chrome instance when >1 CPU core and >250MB free RAM per browser; split samples across browsers. Survives helper crashes/hangs; merges findings by time, deduplicates load messages.
how: Modify doctor.py or check script to use samplingBrowserCount logic; launch multiple browser contexts, distribute seek samples, merge drafts via mergeHelperDrafts.

title: Finding frame selection for visual evidence
text: For each error/warning finding with a real bbox (width>0,height>0), pick the middle sample of the longest contiguous hold (heldMs gap rule). Limit to 60 distinct times total (MAX_FINDING_FRAME_TIMES), preferring errors over warnings. Emit frame requests with filenames like 'finding-frame-01-at-2.345s.png'. Optionally attach inspector targets (by data-hf-id or selector) for DOM/animation snippets.
how: In review.py, after collecting findings, run selectFindingFrames(report) to get a plan. Then capture frames at those times via HyperFrames' captureFindingFrames. Attach frame paths and inspection data back to findings for the dashboard.

title: Budgeted video copy windows (trim to played seconds)
text: When making browser-playable proxies, don't transcode the whole source. Compute the composition's played window per asset via mediaUsedSeconds(html) (returns Map<pathname, secondsPlayed>). Pass limitSeconds to proxy transcode so only the needed segment (+small padding) is encoded. Saves massive time on long source clips.
how: In preResolveHostileMediaProxies, call copyWindows(projectDir, html, pathnames) which uses mediaUsedSeconds to get played seconds, then proxyWindowSeconds(sourcePath, seconds) to get the trim window. Pass limitSeconds to resolveProxies. Integrate into preflight.py's media prep.

title: Ambiguous Selector Enforcement
text: Ensures that any element targeted for audit or automated fix is unique. If a CSS selector (like '.caption') matches multiple elements, the audit is marked as 'ambiguous_selector' and failed to prevent incorrect automated repairs.
how: Strictly enforce in 'preflight.py'. Every element generated by our 'compose.py' scripts must have a unique 'hf-id' or data-attribute to ensure the 'review.py' vision feedback is applied to the correct object.

title: Rotation Pivot Drift Detection
text: Identifies 'wobbly' rotations by tracking the AABB (axis-aligned bounding box) center of a spinning element. If the center drifts significantly while the element's dimensions remain stable (not scaling), it indicates a 'transform-origin' error.
how: Add to 'preflight.py'. During the layout audit, sample 3-5 frames of any element with a GSAP rotation. If the center moves more than 1% of canvas width without a corresponding scale change, flag for repair.

title: Off-Pivot Rotation Guard
text: Specifically for 'Kaise Tech' explainers (gauges, clock hands). It recovers the mathematical center-of-rotation from material points and compares it to detected 'hubs' (concentric circles). Fires if the needle orbits a point far from the visual hub.
how: Apply in 'compose_lab.py' for UI components like dials or needles. Use the geometric solver to ensure 'transform-origin' matches the center of the background 'hub' graphic.

title: Analysis Progress Watchdog
text: Prevents the pipeline from hanging during heavy visual analysis (like face detection or SSIM). It uses a 'CheckDeadline' that must be 'poked' by progress events (like frame seeks); otherwise, it throws a named timeout error.
how: Implement in 'doctor.py'. Wrap the Gemini vision calls and the 'HyperFrames' render process in a watchdog that kills the job if no new frames are processed within 30 seconds.

title: Trusted executable verification for CLI tools
text: Never run yt-dlp, ffmpeg, ffprobe by bare name. Use a pinned allowlist (findTrustedExecutable) that resolves absolute path once, validates signature/hash, caches. Spawn with stdio=[pipe,ignore,ignore], timeout=5s, windowsHide=true. Fail fast if missing.
how: Create utils/trusted_bin.py with allowlist {yt-dlp, ffmpeg, ffprobe, espeak-ng}. On first use, resolve via which/shim, verify file hash against known good (store in brain.jsonl). Replace all subprocess.run calls to use trusted path.

title: Shared snapshot lease for concurrent renders
text: Reference-counted snapshot directory: beginCheckSnapshots increments counter, finishCheckSnapshots decrements; only last release triggers cleanup. Multiple concurrent checks share same capture artifacts, avoiding duplicate browser renders.
how: In render pipeline, when multiple scenes need same composition preview, call beginCheckSnapshots(project_dir) per worker. Share snapshot dir via env var. Last worker calls finishCheckSnapshots. Integrate with existing content-addressed asset deduplication.

title: Windows-Safe Directory Copy
text: Node's `fs.cpSync` can crash (0xC0000409) when copying into existing folders under a drive root. A manual recursive copy using `readdirSync` and `copyFileSync` avoids this system-level failure.
how: Update any Node-based asset management scripts or the `doctor.py` self-repair logic if we ever move the studio runner to a Windows-based environment.

title: Ambient Tween Threshold
text: Define 'ambient' motion as any animation lasting >= 4 seconds, repeating, or having an infinite ancestor. These are treated as background effects rather than active content changes.
how: Use this 4-second rule in `research.py` when Gemini analyzes Shorts to distinguish between a 'hook' transition and a 'background' Ken Burns effect.

title: Ordered Concurrency Limiter
text: Run async workers over an array of inputs with a strict concurrency limit while preserving input order. Rejects immediately on the first failure but allows in-flight work to settle.
how: Apply in `thumb.py` and `images` generation. When hitting Muse or Cloudflare FLUX for multiple assets, use this to stay within rate limits without sacrificing the speed of parallel requests.

title: Frame 0 Content Guard
text: Ensure Frame 0 is not empty or covered by a background-only layer. Since social players use the first frame as a default thumbnail, it must contain the hook title or key visual immediately.
how: In `thumb.py`, add a pre-render check to verify that the 'hook' element has `opacity: 1` and is not occluded at `time: 0`.

title: Silent Film Safety Gate
text: Any video longer than 15s with zero audio sources (music or voice) is a failure. Automated renders can sometimes lose audio tracks due to muxing errors; this gate prevents publishing 'dead' files.
how: In `preflight.py`, check the generated HyperFrames HTML for `<audio>` tags or `mix.py` logs for audio streams. If duration >15s and audio is missing, abort the render.

title: Daily Notice Throttling
text: Prevent 'telemetry/update' spam by recording a timestamped 'claim' file per project. Only show specific CLI notices or prompts once every 24 hours to keep logs clean for the R&D head.
how: Implement a `daily_notice.py` utility to gate non-critical AI news or 'playbook' updates in `scout.py` so they only appear once per day per studio project.

title: Docker Build Timeout Recovery
text: Docker image builds for renderers should have a 10-minute timeout. If it fails due to `ETIMEDOUT`, the system should suggest an immediate rerun, as Docker caches layers and will likely succeed on the second pass.
how: In `doctor.py`, if a render fails due to a Docker timeout, automatically trigger one retry before marking the job as failed.

title: Rational FPS serialization for exact NTSC
text: Serialize fps as '30000/1001' string (not 29.97) when passing to renderer, so the rational survives host→container hop and ffmpeg gets exact NTSC rate.
how: In plan.py or render config, when fps is 30000/1001, pass as string '30000/1001' to HyperFrames CLI. Avoids drift in long videos.

title: DOMParser polyfill for server-side HTML parsing
text: Polyfill globalThis.DOMParser with linkedom's implementation for Node.js, safe to call multiple times.
how: Call ensureDOMParser() at startup if any step (e.g., scout.py parsing HN/GitHub HTML, or preflight.py analyzing composition HTML) uses DOMParser in Node.

title: Redirect handling for all common codes (301,302,303,307,308)
text: Treat 307/308 as redirects (not just 301/302); resolve relative Location headers against the request URL; close each redirect response before next request; limit to 10 hops; strip signed query params from error logs.
how: Ensure our asset downloaders (Muse, FLUX, Pollinations) follow 307/308 and resolve relative redirects. Log redirect chains without secrets for debugging CDN issues.

title: Native arm64 Docker platform resolution
text: Resolve Docker --platform to linux/arm64 on arm64 hosts (Apple Silicon, Graviton) instead of defaulting to linux/amd64, avoiding qemu emulation that causes Chrome segfaults. Honor HYPERFRAMES_DOCKER_PLATFORM override for Rosetta Node or remote daemons.
how: In our render pipeline (compose.py/compose_lab.py), when spawning Docker renders, use resolveDockerPlatform(process.arch, process.env) to pick native platform. Add env var override for CI parity.

title: Bounded stderr tail with error-line extraction
text: Keep last 2000 chars of container stderr; on failure, return the last error-looking line (matching error|fail|exception|cannot|not found|denied|killed|no space) skipping stack frames, else last non-empty line, capped at 160 chars.
how: Wrap our docker render calls (in render.py or doctor.py) with createStderrTail(); on non-zero exit, raise DockerRenderExitError with extracted message for alerting and retry logic.

title: Error normalization with page-crash detection and step annotation
text: Normalize any error to string; if pageCrashed flag set and message matches 'Target closed|detached Frame|Session closed', prefix with OOM hint. atStep(step, fn) wraps promises to append '(while step)' to error message, stripping protocol-timeout advice.
how: In preflight.py, review.py, voice gate, and render steps, wrap each stage with atStep('stage-name', asyncFn). Call notePageCrash() in browser capture on crash detection. Improves post-mortem in doctor.py and Telegram alerts.

title: Dev-mode detection via import.meta.url
text: Check if import.meta.url ends with '.ts' to detect tsx dev mode vs bundled production. Fail-safe to false (production) on parse error.
how: Add isDevMode() to our CLI entry (main.py) to gate telemetry, debug logging, and local asset serving. Keeps production builds clean.

title: HTML escaping utility for dynamic composition
text: Escape &, <, >, ", ' for safe interpolation into HTML templates used by HyperFrames compositions.
how: Use escapeHtml() in thumb.py, compose.py when injecting titles, captions, or user-provided text into HTML templates. Prevents XSS and layout breaks.

title: Forward audio delivery options only when set
text: Pass --keyframe-interval, --max-bitrate, --buffer-size to renderer only when explicitly provided; omit otherwise to let encoder defaults apply.
how: In render.py when building ffmpeg/renderer args for music bed + SFX mix (mix.py), conditionally add these flags only if config specifies them. Avoids overriding encoder sweet spots.

title: Structured GitHub issue generation with truncation guards
text: Builds pre-filled GitHub issue URLs with title (max 80 chars), body (max 4000 chars), bug label, rating, repro URL, environment, CLI version. Truncates at boundaries preserving whole emojis (replaces trailing surrogate with …). Strips .git from repo URL. Notes when repro publishing failed.
how: Adopt for doctor.py error reporting: when self-repair fails, auto-generate issue URL with run context (scene, asset, error). Operator clicks to file. Use same truncation logic in our Telegram error reports.

title: Structured feedback lint with required markers
text: Validates feedback comments for actionable bug reports: requires non-empty REPRO COMMAND: block for ratings < 10; for ratings ≤ 7 with visual-defect keywords (black, flicker, corrupt, wrong frame, blank, visual), requires COMPOSITION_STRUCTURE: block. Case-insensitive, word-bounded keyword matching avoids false positives (blackboard, visualize). Soft warnings only, never blocks submission.
how: Integrate into review.py and doctor.py: after render, if vision review flags visual defects, prompt operator for structured feedback with required markers. Use same keyword list for auto-detecting visual defects in our preflight vision checks.

title: HDR auto-promotion detection
text: Inspects local media files (not remote) for HDR color space (smpte2084/bt2020) that would auto-promote render output to HDR. Skips probe if grading keeps SDR. Returns triggering asset and output spec (BT.2020, HEVC Main10). Lists remote HDR sources not inspected.
how: Add to preflight.py before render: run inspectHdrAutoPromotion on all local assets from compose plan. If promotion detected, either warn operator or force SDR grading. Prevents unexpected HDR output from Muse/FLUX assets.

title: Quick DNS reachability probe
text: Before making fetch requests, probes DNS with 1-second timeout, 1 try per nameserver (A and AAAA). Returns true if any family resolves without timeout. Skips probe if fetch goes through env proxy (HTTPS_PROXY + NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY).
how: Add to scout.py, image downloaders, and asset fetchers: call hostAnswers(host) before HTTP requests. Fail fast on unreachable hosts instead of hanging on system lookup. Use in Muse/FLUX/Pollinations download paths.

title: Conservative auto-update installer detection
text: When unsure of install method (pip, uv, brew, cargo, etc.), return 'skip' and let user handle update manually. Never guess — clobbering Homebrew with pip is worse than no auto-update. Classify by resolved entry path signatures.
how: If we add self-update to studio CLI, implement detect_installer(resolved_path) checking for /lib/python3.x/site-packages/ (pip), ~/.local/share/uv/ (uv), /Cellar/ (brew), etc. On unknown, log reason and skip. User runs manual update command.

title: Held-duration floor for issue promotion (500 ms)
text: Require contiguous held duration ≥500 ms to promote transient warning to error. Sample count alone is insufficient: at 8 fps, 2 samples = 250 ms. Use wall-clock span (lastSeen - firstSeen) of contiguous run (gap ≤1 s).
how: In preflight.py persistence tiering, compute held_ms = (last_seen - first_seen) * 1000 for each contiguous run. Promote content_overlap only if held_ms ≥ 500. Applies to any temporal quality check (audio sync, caption drift).

title: JSON config flag supporting file, stdin, inline with PowerShell fixes
text: Accept --config file.json, --config -, or inline JSON. Detect PowerShell quote stripping (value lacks braces but contains colon) and suggest file/stdin. Decode UTF-8/UTF-16LE BOM. Throw actionable error on missing file or empty stdin.
how: Add read_json_flag(flag, value) to cli_utils.py. In compose.py/plan.py, use for --style, --grading, --plan flags. Handle Windows: if value looks like stripped inline JSON, hint 'PowerShell strips quotes; use --flag file.json or --flag -'.

title: Structured findings formatting with control-char escaping
text: Format findings with visible escapes for ANSI/control chars (\x1b, \x07, \x9b). Support --verbose (include info), --summary (one-line counts), --errors-first (group errors before warnings). Include fix hint indented. File label only when multi-file.
how: Create format_findings(findings, opts) in review_utils.py. Use in preflight.py and review.py. Escape control chars via regex. Add CLI flags --verbose, --summary, --errors-first. Output to stderr for human, stdout for --json.

title: User-friendly network failure explanations
text: explainNetworkFailure() wraps fetch errors, extracts cause chain (DNS, timeout, refused, reset, cert), maps to human reason ("address could not be looked up (DNS); this machine looks offline"), and adds actionable hint (check HTTPS_PROXY). Returns original error if not a transport failure.
how: Wrap all external API calls in publish.py, ideas.py (yt-dlp), research.py (Gemini) with fetchExplained() or try/catch + explainNetworkFailure to surface actionable errors in Telegram reports instead of raw 'fetch failed'.

title: Missing npm package detection with install hints
text: isMissingPackageError() distinguishes 'package itself missing' (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND with "Cannot find package 'pkg'") from 'dependency of installed package missing'. missingPackageMessage() returns formatted string with both global and local install commands.
how: In doctor.py or CLI entrypoint, catch ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, call isMissingPackageError for known optional packages (@hyperframes/aws-lambda, etc.), and print missingPackageMessage so operators can fix with one copy-paste.

title: Recursive mounted-composition discovery
text: projectCompositionFiles() walks data-composition-src mounts recursively, handles template-wrapped scenes, deduplicates cycles, ignores commented/scripted mounts, and stays inside project root. Returns ordered list of project-relative paths.
how: Replace any ad-hoc composition scanning in scout.py, preflight.py, or doctor.py with this function to reliably enumerate all sub-compositions for linting, rendering, or asset auditing.

title: First-use optional package install with version pinning and cache isolation
text: Packages (onnxruntime-node, @google/genai, sharp) install on first use into per-version directories under a private cache. Concurrent callers share one install; failures are cached so retries don't hammer npm. Env var HYPERFRAMES_NO_OPTIONAL_INSTALL=1 or comma list disables installs for air-gapped runs.
how: Adopt for our Whisper/ONNX/GenAI dependencies: wrap model loads in loadOptionalPackage() that installs pinned versions to ~/.cache/hyperframes/optional/<pkg>@<version>/, uses background install for sharp, and respects HYPERFRAMES_NO_OPTIONAL_INSTALL. Replace ad-hoc pip/npm calls in doctor.py and compose_lab.py.

title: Pinned file download with SHA256 verification and atomic replace
text: ensurePinnedFile() checks cached file against size+SHA256 pin; if mismatch, downloads to .part, verifies, then atomic rename. Failed downloads are discarded and error message includes manual npm install command. Progress callback reports re-download reason.
how: Use for our model assets (Whisper, FLUX weights, ONNX models) in download.py. Replace current unchecked downloads. Store pins in knowledge/brain.jsonl or a pins.json. Adds integrity guarantee for 1-2GB model files on flaky connections.

title: Credential and tool-state upload blocklist
text: Block composition/asset uploads for env, Git, credential and agent/editor state paths, matched case-insensitively at any depth: .env*, .envrc, .git/*, .npmrc, .yarnrc.yml, _netrc, pip.ini, .git-credentials, .ssh/config, .aws/credentials, .config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json, .config/gh/hosts.yml, keys/*.pub, *.PEM, .claude/settings.json, .mcp.json, .idea/workspace.xml. Resolve symlinks to the real target first; keep ordinary names (monkey.png, id.png, claude/logo.svg, scenes/mcp.json) allowed.
how: Add one shared blocklist module used by thumb.py, publish.py and any upload/serve path: resolve each asset's realpath, test the relative path against the patterns, and refuse with a JSON error naming the path. Also skip any dotfile segment (hidden project files) before upload.

title: Received-file ledger matched by hash and inode
text: A received-files ledger should recognise a file by three signals: exact relative path, SHA-256 content hash, and dev:ino identity. Renamed or copied files stay "received" via hash/identity; if the ledger or its content-hash sidecar cannot be parsed, fail closed and treat every file as received. Directory walks are budgeted; exceeding the budget returns "unchecked" rather than a partial answer.
how: Extend our received-files ledger with a SHA-256 sidecar and inode identity, and make publish.py/thumb.py treat an unreadable or unchecked ledger as do-not-publish. Cap the scan at a fixed file/folder budget and log when the cap trips.

title: In-place JSON config patch that preserves the file
text: When a tool must add one key to an existing JSON config, patch the parsed object in place instead of rebuilding it from a whitelist: keep unknown keys, reuse the file's own indentation, preserve a leading UTF-8 BOM, and skip the write entirely when the value is unchanged. Never clobber a corrupt config; treat "missing" and "unreadable" as different states.
how: Use a patch_json(path, key, value) helper for our per-page config and brain metadata: read, patch, compare, and atomically replace only when changed, preserving indentation and unknown keys; leave corrupt files untouched and report them instead of overwriting.

title: Lock file with stale and clock-skew thresholds
text: Guard shared-file writes with an exclusive-create lock file: poll every 25 ms for up to 2 s; steal the lock if it is older than 10 s or dated more than 1 s in the future (clock skew); otherwise fail loudly with "another program is changing <file>" instead of writing past a held lock. Release the lock in a finally block.
how: Use this in the shared-brain writer and any file both doctor.py and publish.py touch: lock file next to the target, 2 s wait, 10 s stale, 1 s future skew, then raise a JSON error naming the file so the run retries instead of corrupting state.

title: Closed JSON schema with test-time validation
text: Enforce `additionalProperties: false` at all schema levels and write a test that validates a config exercising every key the system can write (including nested objects). This catches missing schema entries at test time, not in editors or CI.
how: Add a test in our pipeline (e.g., `test_schema_sync.py`) that loads our video project schema, asserts `additionalProperties: false` at root and nested levels, and validates a config containing every field our `plan.py`/`compose.py` can produce.

title: External asset allowlist by file extension for publish/upload
text: Only copy outside-project files with extensions in `{.png,.avif,.svg,.bmp,.tif,.mp4,.mov,.webm,.avi,.ogv,.mp3,.wav,.aiff,.woff,.woff2,.ttf,.otf,.css}`. Reject scripts, JSON, HTML, PDF, etc. with warning. Follow symlinks to check target type, not link name.
how: In `publish.py` and `scout.py` (when fetching assets), filter downloaded files by this allowlist before adding to project. Log rejected files with reason `file_type`.

title: Deterministic archive byte-identity
text: ZIP timestamps cause byte differences across second boundaries. Fix by setting fixed mtime (e.g., 0) on all entries during zip creation, ensuring identical buffers for same content.
how: In thumb.py/archive creation (if any), pass fixed timestamp to zip library (adm-zip or equivalent). Add test that two archives created 3s apart are byte-equal.

title: Comprehensive credential file blocklist
text: Always exclude .env*, .npmrc, .yarnrc*, .pypirc, .netrc, .git-credentials, .ssh/*, .aws/credentials, .docker/config.json, .kube/config, .azure/*, .gcloud/*, .claude/*, .codex/*, .cursor/*, .agents/*, .gemini/*, .vscode/*, .idea/*, keys/*, scenes/_netrc, etc., even if .hyperframesignore tries to include them.
how: In preflight.py, extend private file patterns with this list. Enforce before any archive/upload. Keep .hyperframes/received-files.json excluded but allow .hyperframes/shared/ via explicit ignore rule.

title: Upload timeout scaling with file size
text: Minimum 120s timeout. Above 64MB, scale linearly: timeout = 120s + (size - 64MB) * (1ms/MB). Return integer milliseconds.
how: In publish.py, implement uploadTimeoutMs(bytes) function. Use for all HTTP uploads (Meta, YouTube, S3). Set request timeout accordingly.

title: Proactive OAuth token refresh before upload
text: Before any authenticated upload, check token expiry. If expired and refresh_token exists, refresh automatically. If refresh fails or no refresh token, abort with clear 'run auth login' message. Never send expired token.
how: In publish.py, add pre-upload credential check. Use stored refresh_token (if any) to get new access_token. Update stored creds. If API key or host token rejected, name the env var (HEYGEN_API_KEY, HEYGEN_ACCESS_TOKEN).

title: Srcset asset localization with descriptor preservation
text: Parse srcset attributes, localize each candidate URL (skip data:, https:, //). Preserve descriptors (1x, 2x, 640w). Handle commas in URLs, percent-encoded filenames. Rewrite HTML in archive only, leave source unchanged.
how: In compose.py, add srcset parser for , , . For each local candidate, copy to _ext/, rewrite URL. Keep descriptors intact. Test with mixed data URLs, remote, local.

title: Rewrite only <video src>, never <audio src>, when sharing hostile source
text: AAC audio demuxes fine from HEVC container in HEVC-less browsers. Proxy bake must rewrite <video src> to proxy but leave <audio src> pointing at original hostile file.
how: In bakeMediaProxies, pass selector 'video[src]' and attrs ['src'] to rewriteHtmlAttributes. Ensure audio elements are untouched.

title: Case-insensitive path normalization for cross-platform received-files
text: When tracking received files across renames/moves, compare paths case-folded on case-insensitive volumes (detected via swapCase existence check). Store NFC-normalized keys; resolve on-disk spelling via readdirSync match.
how: Apply in receivedRecordFollow logic for our brain.jsonl asset index. Use onDiskPath() before writing manifest entries.

title: Deterministic ZIP timestamps for content-addressable archives
text: Force every ZIP entry to 1980-01-01 00:00:00 so identical file maps produce byte-identical archives regardless of when/where they're built. Uses adm-zip header.time override after adding all files.
how: In zipPublishFileMap (or our equivalent), after archive.addFile() loop, set entry.header.time = new Date(1980,0,1,0,0,0,0) for all entries before toBuffer().

title: Structured proxy-bake manifest with fail-fast on required transcodes
text: Return {proxied:[], skippedAlpha:[], failed:[{path,error}]}. Sort arrays for determinism. Throw ProxyBakeError with manifest if any failed entry exists — aborts publish before shipping unplayable assets.
how: Add manifest check in publish.py after bake step; surface failed paths in Telegram approval message with retry option.

title: Browser navigation timeout validation (reject sub-ms, cap 24h)
text: Parse --browser-timeout as seconds float. Reject non-numeric, ≤0, >86400 (24h). After ms = round(sec*1000), reject if ms < 1 (Puppeteer treats 0 as 'no timeout'). Prevents silent hang from 0.0004s rounding to 0ms.
how: In our render config (compose.py), validate any page.goto timeout or navigation budget with same rules. Set default 180s.

title: GIF loop count (0–65535) and HLS segment (1–60s integer) validation
text: GIF loop: absent → undefined (default infinite), else integer 0–65535. HLS segment: absent → undefined, else whole seconds 1–60 (ffmpeg's #EXT-X-TARGETDURATION must be integer). Reject fractional, zero, negative, >60.
how: Add to thumb.py (if we ever output GIF) and any future HLS exporter. Validate CLI flags early.

title: Screenshot retry on transient Chrome 'dropped mid-paint' error
text: Chrome's Page.captureScreenshot sometimes fails with 'Unable to capture screenshot' mid-paint. Retry exactly once; if the second attempt fails with a different error, rethrow the first. Do not retry persistent errors (e.g., zero width).
how: Wrap the screenshot call in preflight.py (and thumb.py) with screenshotOnceMore(). Catch the specific transient error string.

title: Cross-platform shell argument escaping
text: POSIX: plain words (letters, digits, _./@:+,=-) unquoted; else double-quote if no "$`\!; else single-quote with '\'' escaping. Windows: plain words without @ , or splat; else double-quote with trailing backslashes doubled; reject any string containing "$`!"“” or %VAR% (returns null).
how: Use in mix.py, publish.py, and any ffmpeg/yt-dlp command building. Replace naive shlex.quote with this for Windows compatibility.

title: Canonical source verification via git ls-remote
text: Fetch manifest from GitHub raw URL pinned to git ls-remote HEAD SHA (not branch URL) to avoid CDN staleness. Disable credential helpers, askpass, GCM_INTERACTIVE. Timeout 4s. Fallback to branch URL only if SHA fetch fails.
how: In scout.py playbook.md fetch, use git ls-remote to pin playbook version. In publish.py for thumbnail templates, verify against canonical repo before using local cached copy.

title: Retired template notices with knowledge migration map
text: Maintain RETIRED_TEMPLATES list with retiredSkillNotice() mapping each to where its knowledge moved (e.g., 'hyperframes-audio → media-use/references/mixing.md'). Show notice when user requests retired template instead of failing.
how: In plan.py template resolver, check RETIRED_TEMPLATES. If matched, log notice to Telegram with migration path. Keep retired templates in brain.jsonl for reference.

title: Version-stamped cache invalidation on reconcile
text: Cache freshness: 2-hour TTL, but only valid for same CLI version (skillsCheckedVersion). On template update (skills update), call invalidateSkillsCache() to drop timestamp AND counts, forcing re-check. Prevents stale verdict resurrection after offline failure.
how: In publish.py after template update, delete brain.jsonl template_cache_* keys. In doctor.py, check cache age + version before trusting cached template status.

title: Unattended mode: suppress outdated-only, show missing
text: In unattended/agent runs (no TTY), suppress notices for templates that are only outdated. Still alert on missing core templates. Prevents noise in automated pipelines while catching breaking absences.
how: In stats.py 09:00 report, if running in cron (no TTY), filter outdated-only templates from alert. Only alert if coreMissing>0. Add is_unattended() check using sys.stdin.isatty().

title: Two-tier template system: core vs on-demand
text: Classify templates as core (entry router + shared domain skills every workflow needs) or on-demand (decks, ports, optional integrations). Core templates install eagerly with init/update; on-demand install only when named. Missing on-demand ≠ update available.
how: In ideas.py/research.py, tag templates: core = lab look, classic look, caption styles; on-demand = map animations, 3D scenes, avatar heads. Modify plan.py to pull on-demand templates only when script references them.

title: Manifest-based freshness diff with coreMissing tracking
text: Diff installed vs latest manifest per template: current/outdated/missing. Update available only if outdated>0 OR coreMissing>0. Missing on-demand templates don't trigger update. Summary includes coreMissing count for alerting.
how: Add templates_manifest.json to repo root. In doctor.py, run diff against local installed templates. Set updateAvailable flag for dashboard. Only alert on core template staleness.

title: Daily throttled update notices per project
text: Print stale-template notice at most once per day per project directory. Cache last notice timestamp in config. Suppress in attended interactive runs; show in unattended/agent runs. Include actionable command: 'npx hyperframes skills update'.
how: Add to dashboard.py 09:00 report: if core templates outdated, send daily Telegram alert with 'Run: python -m studio templates update'. Track last_alert_date per channel in brain.jsonl.

title: Foreign asset protection via lock attribution
text: Read vercel-labs/skills lock file (.skill-lock.json) to attribute each installed template to its source. Never compare, refresh, or overwrite templates attributed to another publisher. Templates with no lock entry = provenance unknown, not foreign.
how: In compose.py template loader, check .template-lock.json (new) before overwriting user-modified templates. Only update templates our studio owns. Preserve user customizations in project/overrides/.

title: Cross-environment template mirroring with symlink safety
text: Mirror global template store (~/.studio/templates) into per-agent/project dirs via relative symlinks (Unix) or copies (Windows). Skip agents that natively read universal store. Fail closed if target aliases install-owned store (same inode or path overlap). Idempotent refresh.
how: Add mirror_templates() to doctor.py. Run on startup. Mirror core templates to each channel's project dir (Kaise Tech/, Puraan Ki Katha/, Aage Suno/). Use relative symlinks for instant updates.

title: Bounded open-ended media ranges prevent Chrome connection starvation
text: Chrome limits 6 HTTP/1.1 connections per host. An open-ended Range (bytes=N-) served to EOF holds the connection until buffer full. Bounding each response to MAX_OPEN_MEDIA_RANGE_BYTES (e.g., 1MB) lets Chrome release connections, allowing concurrent requests (like probe.txt) to succeed.
how: In our media serving (review.py validation), ensure any video/audio Range response caps at 1MB. Already partially done in Cloudflare Workers; verify local preview server does the same.

title: Strip SDR PNG colour tags (cICP) before serving for consistent snapshots
text: serveUntaggedPng reads PNG, strips colour tags via stripSdrPngColourTags, serves untagged bytes. Ensures vision review and pixel diff see raw pixel values, not colour-managed display values. Only applied to image/png.
how: In preflight.py's vision review step, ensure reference frames are compared without colour tags. Add strip step when saving snapshots for SSIM comparison.

title: Stoppable exec with process-tree termination on abort
text: stoppableExecFile runs child off event loop; on AbortSignal, kills entire process tree (terminateProcessTree) and rejects with caller's reason. Without signal, falls back to execFileSync. Handles maxBuffer, timeout, ENOBUFS/ETIMEDOUT mapping to execFileSync-compatible errors.
how: Replace subprocess calls in render.py, mix.py, thumb.py with a wrapper using this pattern. Critical for doctor.py to kill stuck ffmpeg/Chrome trees on timeout. Add AbortSignal from a per-job controller.

title: Inert 404 for stray requests with OAuth parameter guard
text: refuseStrayRequestsInertly registers first middleware: returns 404 with sandbox CSP, COOP, XFO=DENY, no-sniff, no-store. Silently drops requests carrying OAuth code/state params. Clears any prior response headers before writing inert refusal.
how: Apply to any local HTTP server we run (preview, webhook receiver). Add to the server in publish.py (Meta webhook) and compose_lab.py preview. Prevents credential leakage and framing attacks.

title: Transparent media proxy with range support and origin check
text: serveProxyRequest transcodes hostile codecs (HEVC, ProRes) to H.264/VP8 on demand, serves with Range support, returns 502 on transcode failure (never silent black frame), 503 on queue full with Retry-After:1. Blocks ?hf-proxy from cross-site/same-site/no-fetch-metadata requests (requires same-origin Sec-Fetch-Site or Referer).
how: Integrate into our Cloudflare FLUX / Muse pipeline: when compose.py detects hostile codec via probeAssetCodec, auto-transcode via ffmpeg and serve proxied version to browser during preflight validation. Reuse decideMediaProxyEligibility logic.

title: In-process server fallback when sandbox refuses listen()
text: If listen(127.0.0.1:0) fails with EPERM/EACCES, creates an in-process answer function using socket pairs; browser requests to a generated localhost URL are answered via HTTP over in-memory duplex streams. Port=0 signals in-process mode. Cleanly closes on server.close().
how: Add to the local server started by preflight.py for Gemini vision review. If running in restricted CI/sandbox (GitHub Actions), fall back to in-process serving so headless Chrome can still fetch assets.

title: UTM source tagging for CLI-generated links
text: cliSourced adds ?utm_source=cli to hyperframes.studio, hyperframes.heygen.com, heygen.com URLs unless a utm_source already exists. Leaves other hosts, non-URLs, and look-alike domains untouched. Pure function, fully tested.
how: Apply in publish.py and thumb.py when generating share links (Telegram approval, dashboard). Ensures analytics attribute traffic to our CLI automation.

title: Studio preview server discovery with IPv6 fallback and port disambiguation
text: findPreviewServerForProject scans active servers (port 3002), matches by projectDir, falls back to Vite Studio on 5190 (trying 127.0.0.1 then [::1]). Rejects ambiguous duplicates unless preferredPort specified. Returns proven server with host/port for API calls.
how: If we run multiple HyperFrames preview servers (per project), add a discovery utility in doctor.py to find the right one for lint/selection. Use preferredPort from config to disambiguate.

title: Timeout parsing with units and floor
text: Parses --timeout values like '45s', '2m', '45000ms', or bare numbers (treated as ms). Warns if bare value <1000ms (likely meant seconds). Enforces floorMs minimum. Returns milliseconds as int. Used for CLI commands that need bounded waits (e.g., detector ready, network probes).
how: Adopt in our Python CLI wrappers (e.g., render.py, scout.py) for any --timeout/--wait flags. Replace ad-hoc parsing with a shared function that accepts '30s', '5m', '1000ms' and warns on ambiguous bare numbers. Set floorMs to 1000 for network operations.

title: Deprecation notice only on stderr, once per invocation
text: printDeprecationNotice writes a single line to stderr (never stdout) so --json output stays pure. Called by deprecated commands (validate, inspect, layout) via withMeta({deprecated:true}). The _meta.deprecated key appears only when explicitly set true; omitted otherwise (not even false).
how: For our deprecated scripts (e.g., old compose.py, legacy research.py), print deprecation warnings to stderr only. In JSON output (stats.py, dashboard), add _meta.deprecated only when the command is actually deprecated. Never include deprecated:false.

title: Best-effort feedback submission with field caps
text: Submits feedback (rating 1-10, comment, env, source, email) to backend with hard truncation limits (comment 2000, cli_version 100, env 500, email 254). Omits rating fields if absent. Uses 5s timeout, never throws (catches all errors). Also submits catalog search misses (query, wanted, tier) with same guarantees. Includes heygen_route: canary header for misses.
how: Wrap our Telegram feedback handler (owner feedback -> lessons) in a similar fire-and-forget function. Cap fields before sending to our brain.jsonl or external analytics. Add a catalog miss endpoint for when ideas.py or research.py finds no suitable assets/templates. Ensure 5s timeout and silent failure.

title: Git-style unified diff for composition changes
text: Produces unified diff with 3 lines context, Myers O(ND) algorithm, capped at 4000 changed lines (beyond that shows whole middle as replace). Handles missing final newline marker. Matches git diff --no-index output. Used for --json envelope diffs and composition rewrite previews.
how: Add to plan.py or compose.py when showing scene-by-scene plan diffs after Gemini rewrite. Use for preflight.py to show visual diff between expected and actual frame layouts. Implement in Python (difflib.unified_diff with context=3) or port the TypeScript logic for exact git compatibility.

title: Face rect mapping through object-fit transforms
text: faceRectOnCanvas converts face coordinates (normalized to video frame) to canvas pixels, accounting for object-fit cover/contain (frame vs box), flipX/flipY, and crops faces to the visible box area. Drops faces where visible area <50% of original. Uses intersect and area calculations.
how: Use in our text-over-face detection (item 1) and also for caption placement in compose_lab.py: when positioning kinetic titles or HUD panels, query face rects on canvas to auto-avoid faces. Requires passing video layout (box, frame, flip) from compose to detection.

title: Usage budget parser for multi-provider quota tracking
text: usageBudget.ts normalizes Claude (5h/7d windows + spend), Codex (primary/secondary windows by duration), and Grok (weekly credits) into a common HarnessUsage type with usedPercent, remainingPercent, resetsAt. Validates with AJV JTD schemas, caps spend at 100%, falls back to extra_usage when spend disabled.
how: Create `quota.py` that calls each provider's usage endpoint (Gemini, Pollinations, Muse, FLUX) and maps responses through a similar parser. Store in `brain.jsonl` with `resetsAt`. In `ideas.py` and `scout.py`, check remainingPercent before scheduling expensive generations; skip or downscale when <10% remains.

title: Filesystem walk budget prevents asset-scan hangs
text: walkBudget.ts returns a predicate that allows at most 20,000 entries and 2,000 ms. The walker calls it with each batch; once it returns false, the walk stops unfinished. Zero dependencies, trivial to embed.
how: Wrap `scout.py`'s GitHub/HN scraping and `thumb.py`'s asset search with a similar budget. In `compose.py` when scanning `.media` for placeholders, pass a budget callback. If exceeded, log a warning and use fallback assets instead of blocking the render.

title: Windows PATH sanitization for subprocess safety
text: windowsExeSearch.ts strips PATH to only absolute folders outside the project root, removes `.` and `node_modules/.bin`, sets `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1`. Runs on every CLI entry point that spawns children. Prevents execution of project-local binaries or CWD implants.
how: In `compose.py` and `mix.py` where ffmpeg/Chrome are spawned, sanitize `os.environ['PATH']` on Windows: keep only system folders and known tool directories (ffmpeg, Chrome). Set `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1`. Do this once at process start in a new `utils/subprocess_safety.py`.

title: Language-aware model selection
text: Auto-swap English-only (.en) models for multilingual variants when target language isn't English (e.g., Hinglish -> small instead of small.en). Base language code from first subtag (en, hi, etc.).
how: In plan.py or caption step, call initialModelForLanguage(selectedModel, detectedLanguage) before ensureModel(). Detect language from script or user input.

title: Whisper error classification: unavailable vs transcription failure
text: Distinguish WhisperUnavailableError (code WHISPER_UNAVAILABLE) — missing binary, no brew, no compiler — from actual transcription crashes. Treat former as optional dependency skip; latter as real command failure.
how: In doctor.py or caption step, catch errors and use isWhisperUnavailable(err) to decide: if unavailable, skip captions gracefully; if transcription failure, retry or alert.

title: Multi-format transcript parser with unified Word[] output
text: Parse whisper-cpp JSON (transcription[].tokens), OpenAI verbose_json (words[]), SRT, VTT, and pre-normalized word arrays into consistent Word[] (id, text, start, end). Assigns w{index} IDs, repairs empty IDs, strips HTML tags, decodes VTT entities.
how: Use loadTranscript() from normalize.ts as single entry point for any caption source (Whisper output, uploaded SRT/VTT, manual JSON). Returns {words, format}.

title: Word-level cue grouping with maxChars/maxGap and CJK/Thai support
text: Group Word[] into cues: max 42 chars, max 0.8s gap, flush at sentence end. Auto-detect phrase-level input (internal whitespace for space-separated scripts; median token length ≥4 for CJK/Thai/Lao/Myanmar/Khmer). Joins tokens without space across CJK boundaries.
how: Use wordsToCues() from normalize.ts when exporting SRT/VTT for thumbnails or caption files. Pass preGrouped=true for phrase-level sources (SRT/VTT import).

title: Caption HTML patching for live preview
text: Atomically replace `const script = []` or `const TRANSCRIPT = []` in HTML preview files with normalized Word[] (JSON stringified, escaped for HTML). Preserves surrounding code, handles array terminators, skips empty arrays.
how: Call patchCaptionHtml(dir, words) in compose.py after generating preview HTML. Enables real-time caption preview in lab look with word light-up.

title: Warm-check protocol for render worker health
text: Fast liveness check via Unix socket/named pipe with HMAC proof-of-possession handshake (2s timeout). Forwards stdout/stderr/exit frames, handles signals. Private runtime dir (0o700) with token file (0o600), rejects symlinks/world-writable.
how: Adapt warmCheckClient.ts logic in doctor.py for render worker monitoring: spawn warm-check server per worker, client does handshake, verifies env digest matches, streams logs. Replaces generic ping.

title: Build-from-source with pinned commit verification
text: When building dependencies (whisper.cpp), clone specific tag (v1.9.5), verify HEAD commit matches reviewed hash (d1be6fde), clean stale builds, seal cache dir against foreign writes. Fail fast on mismatch.
how: Apply in any dependency installer (e.g., FFmpeg, custom GSAP): use assertPinnedCheckout(git) after clone, sealCacheInstall() before build, assertPrivateCachePath() after. Prevents supply-chain drift.

title: Model-aware timeout scaling with discoverable error hints
text: Timeout = min(12h, max(5min, duration × 10s × modelFactor)) where factors: tiny/base=0.5, small=1, medium=2, large=4. On timeout, error message names --timeout flag, HYPERFRAMES_TRANSCRIBE_TIMEOUT_MS env, effective seconds, and model.
how: Apply same formula to render/ffmpeg timeouts; wrap errors with wrapWhisperTimeoutError pattern so users see exact knob to adjust.

title: Voice-to-locale auto-inference from language code
text: parakeetSpeaks(language) extracts base language (pt-BR → pt) and checks against supported list; returns true if unspecific or supported. Used to pick engine without explicit locale.
how: In plan.py, infer TTS voice locale from script language tag (Hinglish → hi-IN, English → en-US) using same base-code extraction; fallback to default if unsupported.

title: Dropped speech gap detection via energy threshold
text: After decoding a window, find gaps ≥1s without tokens where RMS energy exceeds 30% of window average — indicates missed speech. Returns gap [from, to] seconds.
how: Add droppedSpeechGaps check in voice-gate after TTS; if gaps found, trigger re-voice before visual render.

title: Silence-aware window cuts for long audio
text: Split audio into ~60s windows at quietest 100ms block within ±5s of each boundary, preventing cuts inside words. Returns sample indices.
how: Use silenceCuts in any long-audio processing (podcasts, compilations) to feed decoder in safe chunks.

title: Progress streaming with 16KB line limit and download coalescing
