how: In our lab-look templates, drive animated grading via CSS custom properties set by GSAP. Use the same property names (--hf-color-grading-*) so HyperFrames picks them up automatically. No extra JS needed.

title: CORS-safe image grading via anonymous fetch
text: In opaque origins (file://, null), HyperFrames creates a crossOrigin='anonymous' copy of the image for WebGL sampling. If CORS fails, falls back to grading the original image (tainted canvas). Handles load/error events to swap seamlessly.
how: When using external images in Puraan Ki Katha or Aage Suno, ensure they're served with CORS headers. If not, HyperFrames will still grade but canvas becomes tainted (no toDataURL). Prefer local assets or CORS-enabled CDN.

title: Visibility-aware grading lifecycle (hidden ancestors pause grading)
text: Grading pauses when the media element or any ancestor has visibility:hidden or display:none. Canvas visibility follows source. When shown again, grading resumes without re-creating WebGL resources. Prevents wasted GPU work on off-screen clips.
how: In our scene system, use visibility:hidden (not display:none) for inactive scenes to preserve grading state. HyperFrames' setSourceVisibility() is called automatically by the runtime's MutationObserver.

title: LUT loading with GPU texture-size fallback and caching
text: When a .cube LUT's packed texture width exceeds GPU MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE, HyperFrames automatically shrinks it (e.g., 27^3 → 4×2). LUTs are fetched once and cached; concurrent preview requests serialize until the LUT loads.
how: In compose_lab.py, add a LUT preset registry that references .cube files. Ensure the render pipeline calls HyperFrames' renderPreviews for thumbnail generation so LUT caching benefits apply. No code change in HyperFrames needed.

title: Producer render-frame integration for capture
text: When a producer injects a render frame (__render_frame_<id>__), HyperFrames detects it, hides the source video, grades the render frame instead, and moves the grading canvas above the frame before capture. Handles staged scene clones without canvas thrashing.
how: In our capture step (preflight.py/review.py), ensure the producer's render frame gets the expected ID and class. No HyperFrames changes needed; just verify the DOM structure matches the test expectations.

title: Before-after compare grading for tutorials
text: setCompare() enables a split-view compare with position (0-1), lineWidth, and enabled uniforms, without modifying the source grading attribute. Useful for 'before/after' tech demos or color grading tutorials.
how: In compose_lab.py, add a 'compare' scene type that calls runtime.setCompare() on the target clip. Expose position/lineWidth via scene plan. Use for Kaise Tech 'before/after' segments.

title: Advanced grain/vignette with size, roughness, seed
text: Grain: bayer4 dither + hash noise, u_grain (0–1), u_grainSize (1–5× scale), u_grainRoughness (0–1), u_grainSeed (per-frame). Vignette: u_vignette (0–1), u_vignetteMidpoint (0–1), u_vignetteRoundness (0–1), u_vignetteFeather (0–1). Applied after primary grade, before LUT.
how: Upgrade lab look grain/vignette params in compose_lab.py to match these uniforms. Add grainSeed animation (increment per frame) for temporal noise. Set default vignetteMidpoint=0.5, roundness=0.3, feather=0.5 for subtle cinematic look.

title: Loop-inflated timeline detection (7200s threshold)
text: If timeline duration ≥7200s (2 hours), treat as infinite loop (repeat:-1) and ignore it for length calculation. Instead use floor (sub-composition ends) or fallback. Only use timeline length if no floor/fallback exists.
how: In compose.py, when parsing HyperFrames JSON, detect timeline duration >7200s; log warning 'loop-inflated timeline, using floor'; set scene duration from floor. Prevents 2-hour renders from accidental repeat:-1.

title: Authored composition floor from direct sub-compositions
text: Only direct children of root with data-composition-id and data-start count. For each, floor = start + duration (from its own declared/timeline/floor). Root's own data-duration also a candidate. Max of all = authored floor. Nested sub-compositions ignored (handled by their own floor).
how: In plan.py, when building scene hierarchy, compute floor for each composition recursively. Pass floor up to parent. Use for multi-scene videos (Aage Suno stories) to auto-determine total length without manual timing.

title: External Script Load Diagnostics
text: Implements an 8-second timeout for external script loads with diagnostic reporting for 'timeout', 'error', or 'load' status. Helps identify why specific scenes fail to render in automated pipelines.
how: Add a diagnostic listener to `review.py` that catches `external_composition_script_load_issue` events and flags them in the Telegram Studio360 report.

title: Runtime Asset Path Rewriting
text: Rewrites relative paths (e.g., ../assets/logo.png) in sub-compositions to absolute URLs based on the component's source URL. This prevents 404 errors in Studio previews where the base URI differs from the final render path.
how: Update our HTML renderer in `compose_lab.py` to include a path-rewrite utility that scans `[src]`, `[href]`, and CSS `url()` patterns when mounting external templates.

title: SVG ID Namespacing for Collisions
text: Detects and namespaces colliding SVG IDs across multiple mounted components. It rewrites both the ID attributes and the corresponding CSS `url(#id)` or `fill='url(#id)'` references to ensure unique rendering.
how: Implement a post-mount pass in our UI panel logic that appends a unique suffix to SVG IDs and updates all internal references within that component's DOM tree.

title: Font-Gated Script Execution
text: Delays the execution of component scripts until `document.fonts.ready` resolves. This is critical for scripts that measure text width for kinetic titles or auto-sizing chat bubbles.
how: Wrap our component initialization logic in an `await document.fonts.ready` block to ensure 'lab look' UI panels calculate their dimensions correctly on the first frame.

title: Safe Swallow Pattern
text: A 'swallow(label, err)' function for intentional silences (e.g., failed postMessage or media.play). It logs to console.debug only if a debug flag is set, preventing lint errors and keeping production logs clean.
how: Standardize all try/catch blocks in our runtime JS to use a swallow() helper. This keeps our inlined IIFE small and prevents 'no-empty' lint warnings.

title: Authored-Frame Stack Normalization
text: Captures runtime errors and normalizes the stack trace to show only the top 3 library frames plus the first 'authored' frame (matching the composition URL). Strips noise and replaces newlines with ' <- ' for single-line logging.
how: Add recordStartupError to our runtime IIFE. In review.py, check window.__hfStartupError after a failed render to get a clean, actionable reason why a script crashed.

title: Crop Lift Style Override
text: Temporarily 'lifts' a crop by injecting a style rule: '[data-hf-id=...] {clip-path: none !important}'. This allows an editor to see the full asset while adjusting boundaries without losing the original clip-path data.
how: Add to our Telegram approval flow (Studio360). When a user requests a crop adjustment, the preview can 'lift' the crop for easier visual alignment.

title: Audio Grouping and Metering
text: Uses '<hf-audio-group>' elements to logically group audio tags. Implements a 'level tap' to read real-time stereo levels (master and per-group) for visual meters.
how: Update mix.py to output these group tags. In the dashboard, we can now show real-time volume levels for 'Voice' vs 'Music' during the review phase.

title: Motion path home with transform and perspective awareness
text: Compute element center (x,y), size (w,h), and growth shares (ax,ay) by walking offsetParents, adding ancestor transforms (not own), handling CSS translate (percent/px), GSAP-parsed xPercent/yPercent (folded translate), and perspective scaling (1/m44 from matrix3d). Growth shares: 0.5 from left/top, -0.5 from right/bottom, plus percent offset.
how: Use in compose_lab.py when building motion paths for panels, charts, HUD elements. Replace manual center calculations with elementHome logic. Apply transformWDivisor for 3D-transformed containers.

title: Tween patch validation rules
text: Only finite numeric values allowed for SET_CHANNELS (x,y,rotation,rotationX,rotationY,rotationZ,z,transformPerspective,scaleX,scaleY,scale,opacity) plus width,height. Reject strings (GSAP relative expressions), non-finite, empty props, unknown channels. Keyframe steps must be static numeric objects. Max 64 patches, 64 keyframe steps, 2000 char selector.
how: Enforce in our animation parameter schema (plan.py, compose_lab.py). Add validation before sending patches to preview. Use finiteNumericProps and keyframesAreStatic patterns.

title: Soft reload timing plan application
text: Before script re-run, apply saved timing attributes (data-start, data-end, data-duration, data-track-index, data-media-start, data-playback-start, data-playback-rate) to live elements via applyAuthoredTiming. Plan per element, skip rewritten roots (data-hf-inner-root). Fail if any timed element missing or duplicate key.
how: In preflight.py, when timing edits occur, compute timing plan and apply before soft reload. Use planSavedTiming and applyTimingPlan. Ensures clip windows and film length correct at rebind.

title: Geometry event schema with strict validation
text: Each push: {v: version, event: 'geometry', at: timestamp, elements: [{rect:{x,y,width,height}, angle, clipPath, corners:{ne,nw,se,sw}, members:[rect], source:{width,height,declaredWidth,declaredHeight}, visible}]}. Null for missing elements. Validate all fields, drop extra. Max 32 elements.
how: Adopt in our preview-to-studio protocol. Use geometryEvent parser in dashboard for real-time layout metrics. Feed into preflight.py layout audit.

title: Authored style restoration with GSAP clearProps
text: When resetting target styles: save cssText, gsap.set(targets, {clearProps: 'all'}), restore cssText, then reapply authored styles (transform, translate, rotate, scale) and authored opacity (from stamped attribute or readStampedAuthoredOpacity). Skip opacity in tweened props. Prevents stale from() values.
how: Use in soft reload and preflight style reset. Implement restoreAuthoredStyle in our GSAP utilities. Call before timeline rebind. Ensures clean slate for from() tweens.

title: Safe in-place attribute restoration for undo/redo
text: Restore full attribute sets (class, style, data-*) on identified elements (data-hf-id or id). Reject handlers (onclick), URLs (href, src), sandbox, data-composition-src. Handle sub-composition copies. Rebind timeline at target time via __hfForceTimelineRebind and seek.
how: Implement in our Telegram approval flow: when editor undoes, send restoreAttributes params to preview. Use planRestore to validate safety. Add to review.py for post-render attribute fixes without re-render.

title: Live audio group parameter updates
text: Set attributes on <hf-audio-group> elements (data-volume, data-hidden, data-label, data-fx-chain, data-automation) directly; the audio graph follows. Validate attr against allowlist, value length ≤200k. Returns {applied: boolean}.
how: Extend mix.py to send setAudioGroupAttribute via editing port for real-time fader/FX changes during preview. Add to our audio automation UI. Validate with parseSetAudioGroupAttribute.

title: Stable Element Handles with FinalizationRegistry
text: Map DOM elements to unique, session-stable string handles (e.g., 'loadId:count') using a WeakMap and FinalizationRegistry. This allows the studio to refer to specific elements across different pipeline stages without holding onto dead nodes or losing references during scene 'parking' or re-renders.
how: Implement in a new 'runtime/handles.js' for HyperFrames. Use it to identify elements in Telegram feedback loops, allowing the 'doctor.py' or manual edits to target specific UI panels or text blocks by a persistent ID.

title: Rotated Corner Point Calculation
text: Calculate the exact viewport coordinates (NW, NE, SE, SW) of rotated elements by applying a DOMMatrix transform to the border-box corners. This is essential for placing 'mono HUD' lines or 'kinetic titles' that must perfectly align with the edges of rotated panels.
how: Integrate into 'compose_lab.py'. Use the corner coordinates to draw GSAP-animated connecting lines or 'panel shine' effects that follow the perspective of rotated UI elements.

title: CSS Draft Restoration Pattern
text: Store original inline styles (translate, width, height, box-sizing) in a WeakMap before applying temporary 'draft' edits. This allows for a 'restore' command that perfectly resets an element to its authored state without needing a full page reload.
how: Update 'compose.py' and 'compose_lab.py' to support a 'preview-edit' mode where Telegram-based layout adjustments can be toggled on/off instantly during the approval phase.

title: GSAP Property Ownership Detection
text: Check if GSAP 'owns' an element's position by inspecting the '_gsap' object and active tweens for 'x', 'y', or 'motionPath' properties. Use 'gsap.getProperty' to read the current value, which correctly handles the folding of CSS translates into the GSAP transform cache.
how: Modify 'review.py'. Use this to verify that 'kinetic titles' or 'stat counters' actually moved as intended by comparing the GSAP-reported position against the scene plan.

title: Automated Snap Candidate Discovery
text: Identify nearby 'snap candidates' by walking the DOM and filtering for rendered elements that aren't part of the currently active/pressed group. Limits the search to a fixed number (e.g., 60-80) to maintain performance in complex 'lab look' layouts.
how: Apply in 'compose_lab.py' to automatically align 'chat bubbles' or 'UI panels' to the edges of existing elements, ensuring a clean, grid-based aesthetic without manual coordinate math.

title: Content-Aware Element Labeling
text: Generate human-readable labels for elements: use the first 56 characters of text for paragraphs/spans, or generic roles like 'Image', 'Video', or 'Shape' for media tags.
how: Integrate buildElementLabel() into review.py and the Telegram approval logs so the owner sees 'Edited: [Mythology Hook...]' instead of 'Edited: div#caption-1'.

title: Layer Kind Classification
text: Categorize DOM elements into 'image', 'video', 'audio', 'vector', 'group', 'text', or 'shape'. Text is identified if an element has only formatting children (b, i, span) and non-empty text content.
how: Implement layerKindOf() in compose_lab.py to automatically label UI components in the 'lab' look, allowing the engine to apply specific logic (like kinetic titles) only to 'text' kinds.

title: Full-Bleed Hit-Testing Logic
text: When identifying elements at a point, ignore 'backdrop' elements that cover >95% of the composition unless they are specific media tags (img, video, canvas). This ensures clicks/picks target content, not backgrounds.
how: In the Studio360 preview, use a 0.95 ratio check against the viewport to filter out background divs when the owner is selecting elements to edit or highlight.

title: MessagePort Editing Bridge
text: Establish a secure, asynchronous channel between the video preview iframe and the host studio using MessageChannel. This allows the host to request 'computed-styles' or 'geometry' without origin conflicts.
how: Implement createEditingPortClient in the Studio dashboard to query the preview frame for real-time stats like audio-meter levels or console errors during a test run.

title: Far-Scene Content Visibility
text: Apply 'content-visibility: hidden' to scene containers that are more than one neighbor away from the current playhead. Use 'ResizeObserver' to capture and apply 'contain-intrinsic-size' so the scrollbar and layout don't collapse when scenes are hidden.
how: In 'compose_lab.py', tag scene containers with 'data-hf-scene'. Add a runtime observer that toggles a 'data-hf-far-scene' attribute based on playhead position, with a CSS rule mapping that attribute to 'content-visibility: hidden'.

title: Decode-Gated Seek
text: Prevent 'flashes' of old frames during jumps by holding the seek resolution until the target image decodes ('img.decode()') or video reaches 'HAVE_CURRENT_DATA'. Implement a 1s safety cap ('seekHoldCap') to force the jump if assets are slow.
how: Modify the player's seek function to return a Promise. Use 'Promise.all' for all images/videos in the target frame, resolving only when they are ready or the 1000ms timeout hits.

title: Iframe Film Bridge
text: Run untrusted or isolated composition scripts in a sandboxed iframe ('allow-scripts' without 'allow-same-origin'). Communicate via 'postMessage' with a sequence-numbered protocol to request specific frames.
how: If we scale to multi-user templates, use 'filmBridge.ts' logic to isolate the rendering of user-provided HTML/JS from the main studio control logic.

title: Define-if-Absent CSS Variable Pattern
text: When injecting variables into templates, use a 'define-if-absent' strategy. Check if a CSS variable is already defined via inline styles or stylesheets before applying the default from the variable schema. Overrides from the engine always win.
how: Apply this in 'compose_lab.py' when generating the 'lab look'. It allows us to hardcode specific 'hero' colors in the HTML while still having a fallback system for generic UI elements.

title: Data-Driven Template Variables
text: Implement a schema-based variable system using 'data-composition-variables' for defaults and a global '__hfVariables' for overrides. Supports strings, numbers, booleans, and enums with validation warnings. Injects these as CSS variables (e.g., --figma-brand-primary) for real-time theme swapping.
how: Update 'compose_lab.py' to output a JSON schema in the HTML root. Modify our GSAP templates to use CSS variables for accent colors and UI panels, allowing Gemini to 're-skin' a video by just passing a new JSON object to the render command.

title: Late-Start Audio Protection
text: Prevent the 'catch-up' effect where audio is sped up if it starts a few milliseconds late. The runtime should ensure that if an audio element has a start lag (common in browser-based TTS), the film clock waits or maintains 1x speed rather than accelerating to sync.
how: In our HyperFrames runtime, implement the logic from 'init.audioStart.test.ts' to detect 'movesFromMs' lag. Ensure 'playbackRate' is never automatically adjusted above 1x during the first 500ms of a voice clip.

title: Sublinear Media Seek Indexing
text: Optimize seeking in long timelines by only visiting media clips whose 'window' (start/end) was crossed by the playhead since the last frame. This prevents performance degradation as the number of clips increases (O(1) or O(crossed) instead of O(total)).
how: Integrate the 'media clip index' logic into our HyperFrames runtime. This is critical for 'Aage Suno' story videos which may eventually exceed 60 seconds and contain dozens of small SFX/clip layers.

title: 8-Second Asset Starvation Timeout
text: If a video or audio clip fails to provide data (buffering) for more than 8 seconds, the runtime should stop holding the film and play on without it. This prevents a single failing CDN asset from hanging the entire automated render pipeline.
how: Add a 'buffering' state watcher to our render process. If 'readyState < 3' persists for 8s, flag the asset as 'stuck' in 'doctor.py' and allow the render to proceed (perhaps with a placeholder) to avoid stuck jobs.

title: Preview Health Choppiness Detection
text: Monitor 'waitingShare' (percentage of time spent buffering) and 'heldBy' (the specific element causing the lag). Report this as a 'choppy' flag to the parent process.
how: Add a 'preview-health' message to our Telegram Studio360 previewer. If a video is choppy due to Muse/Cloudflare asset lag, the bot can warn the editor before they approve a potentially broken render.

title: Long-File Source Deferral (WebKit)
text: For long source files on WebKit/iOS, defer setting the 'src' attribute until the playhead is near the clip's start. This prevents the browser from trying to buffer multiple segments of the same large file simultaneously, which crashes the media stack.
how: Implement 'deferMediaUntilDue' in our previewer. If a story uses the same 5-minute background loop multiple times, only the active segment will have a 'src' assigned, saving memory and bandwidth.

title: Preview Seek Hold State
text: Implement a 'hold' attribute (e.g., PREVIEW_SEEK_HOLD_ATTR) that keeps the current frame's visual state (via canvas snapshots) visible until the destination video has fully decoded ('landed'). This prevents black-frame flickering during timeline scrubbing.
how: Modify compose.py and the HyperFrames JS runtime to detect seek starts, draw the current frame to a temporary overlay canvas, and only remove it when the 'seeked' event fires for all active videos.

title: Isolated Media Reloading
text: When a video source is updated or reloaded (e.g., proxy to high-res swap), restore the playhead position immediately without re-triggering the start-time resolution logic for the entire project. This prevents UI freezes in long videos.
how: In the runtime's media handler, catch 'loadedmetadata' events. If the element was already part of a timeline, use a cached mediaElementTime(currentPlayhead) to reset its currentTime without re-running the full startResolver.

title: Attribute Read Caching
text: Cache DOM attributes like 'data-start' and 'data-duration' once during the initial warm-up or first play pass. Reading these from the DOM on every requestAnimationFrame (especially with 300+ elements) causes significant layout thrashing.
how: In the JS runtime, create a Map of element IDs to their timing metadata during the first pass of initSandboxRuntimeModular. Reference this Map during playback instead of calling getAttribute.

title: Audio-Only Video Detection
text: Skip video-frame decoding gates for video elements that have a videoWidth of 0 (audio-only MP4s). This prevents the renderer from stalling while waiting for a frame that will never arrive.
how: Add a check in the render-ready gate: if (video.videoWidth === 0 && video.readyState >= 1), treat the video as 'landed' immediately for visual purposes.

title: Timeline-Gated Visibility Rule
text: Clips should be forced to `visibility: hidden` whenever the playhead is outside their authored `data-start` and `data-duration` window, even if a GSAP tween (like `autoAlpha`) tries to make them visible.
how: Enforce this in the `HyperFrames` CSS: elements with `data-start` should have a default state of `visibility: hidden` unless the runtime explicitly toggles them based on the global clock.

title: Partial Scene Swapping (Hot Reload)
text: Implement a scene-swapping mechanism that replaces only the edited scene's DOM, styles, and GSAP timelines while preserving the playhead and other scenes. It must validate that no 'outside' animations are targeting the scene and that no new media assets are introduced that haven't been pre-loaded.
how: In our preview server, add a `swapScene` endpoint. When a script or style changes, send the new HTML fragment. The runtime should kill the specific scene's GSAP timeline, replace its DOM node, and re-run only that scene's script to register a new timeline.

title: Lazy AudioContext Initialization
text: Delay the creation of the `AudioContext` until the first audio clip actually needs to play. This avoids unnecessary resource allocation and potential 7+ second initialization hangs on Windows systems for videos that might be silent or still loading.
how: In `mix.py` or the browser runtime, wrap the `AudioContext` creation in a getter that is only invoked when the transport starts playing a composition containing audio elements.

title: Stereo Peak Level Tapping
text: Use a side-chain `AnalyserNode` with a 2048-sample window to read real-time stereo peaks (L/R) from any AudioNode. This allows for visual meters or automated loudness validation without affecting the main output mix.
how: Add `createLevelTap` to our audio pipeline. Use it in `review.py` to verify that 'Puraan Ki Katha' narrations actually have signal and aren't hitting 0 (silence) or clipping during the render process.

title: GSAP Animation Stack Inspection
text: Hook into GSAP methods (`to`, `from`, `set`) to record the call stack whenever a tween is created. This allows the system to identify exactly which line of code created an animation targeting a specific DOM element.
how: In `preflight.py`, use a proxy to wrap `gsap.to`. Store the `new Error().stack` in a `WeakMap` keyed by the tween. If a visual audit fails, Gemini can look at the stack trace to tell us which part of the script is misbehaving.

title: MutationObserver Gesture Tracking
text: Use an attribute-filtered `MutationObserver` to track 'manual-edit' gestures instead of querying the whole document every frame. This reduces the paused main-thread budget usage by up to 6% in media-heavy projects.
how: If we implement manual adjustments in Studio360, use this to detect when an element is being dragged. The observer should only watch for a specific attribute (e.g., `data-dragging`) to wake/park the transport.

title: Timing Resolver Scoping
text: Cache timing resolutions (calculating absolute start times from relative offsets like `lead + 0`) within a single seek/frame pass. Building a new resolver per element leads to O(N^2) complexity; a scoped resolver with a `WeakMap` keeps it flat.
how: Modify the timing logic in `compose.py` to pass a shared `resolver` instance during the visibility and media-sync passes of a single frame render.

title: Out-point Frame Watching
text: Use requestVideoFrameCallback to monitor a video nearing its out-point. Pause the element exactly on the last authored frame before the cut to prevent 'bleeding' frames from the next second of source material into the edit.
how: Update compose_lab.py to inject a script that uses requestVideoFrameCallback on all video elements. When within 0.5s of the data-duration end, calculate the exact frame cadence and pause on the final frame.

title: Terminal Video Hold
text: If a non-looping video clip reaches the end of the composition but is still visible, force it to hold its final frame. This prevents the element from disappearing or resetting to frame zero if the render clock overshoots slightly.
how: In the sync loop, check if currentTime >= compositionDuration. If a video is marked as terminal, clamp its currentTime to its sourceDuration and ensure it remains visible.

title: Clip-Local Volume Automation
text: Sample volume automation lanes (envelopes) using clip-local time (seconds from clip start) rather than global timeline time. This ensures that trimmed or shifted clips maintain their intended audio fades regardless of where they sit on the timeline.
how: Update the volume interpolation logic in mix.py/runtime to subtract the clip's 'origin' (start time) from the current playhead time before sampling the automation curve.

title: Reactive Codec Fallback
text: Detect unsupported video codecs (like HEVC in some Chrome builds) by checking if videoWidth is 0 during the 'loadedmetadata' event. This 'unlisted-asset rescue' trigger allows the runtime to request a proxy/transcode even if the asset wasn't pre-flagged as hostile.
how: Add an event listener in our preview runtime that monitors 'loadedmetadata'. If width is 0, trigger a diagnostic message to our doctor.py to check for transcode availability.

title: Display-Scale Aware Proxies
text: Optimize preview performance by requesting video proxies sized exactly to their on-screen CSS box multiplied by the device pixel ratio. If a 4K video is shown in a 360p UI panel, the runtime should fetch a 'light' proxy to save bandwidth and CPU.
how: In our Studio360 dashboard, pass the container's clientWidth/Height to the preview server to gate which asset resolution is served for the 'lab' look UI panels.

title: Seamless Proxy Swapping
text: Prevent black flashes during asset swaps by capturing the last successful frame as a JPEG data-URL and applying it as the video element's 'poster' attribute. Only remove the poster once the new source fires 'loadeddata' or 'seeked'.
how: Modify our preview runtime to draw the current video frame to a hidden canvas before changing the 'src' attribute, setting the result as the poster to maintain visual continuity.

title: Preserve above-unity authored gain
text: When an audio element has data-volume > 1 (e.g., 1.95 for +5.8 dB), the probe installs a shadow accessor that lets GSAP read the unclamped value while the native setter clamps to 1. The envelope stores the unclamped keyframes; render applies gain in float32 before final limiter.
how: In plan.py/script, allow authors to set volume: 1.5 for boost. In compose.py, write data-volume="1.5". Ensure mix.py's gain stage reads the envelope unclamped and applies before -14 LUFS mastering. Document in playbook.md.

title: Track-relative envelope for nested clips
text: A clip inside a nested composition has data-start local to its host. The probe resolves the absolute timeline start via a startResolver that walks composition ancestry. Envelope keyframes are stamped with absolute seek times, then normalized by subtracting the clip's absolute start (not data-start).
how: When authoring lab look scenes with nested compositions (e.g., a chart inside a panel), ensure plan.py emits data-start relative to host, and the render pipeline resolves absolute start via the same ancestry walk. Preflight probe must use absolute start for envelope normalization.

title: Native video look gamma filter
text: On macOS Chromium, canvas shows sRGB (gamma 2.4) while <video> layer applies Apple's gamma (~1.961). An SVG feComponentTransfer filter (256-entry table) applied to preview canvases makes captured stills match the video layer. Only enabled for known 8-bit SDR sources (bitDepth ≤ 8 from media scan).
how: In preflight.py's still generation (headless Chrome), inject the filter onto any canvas that draws video frames via drawImage. Use mediaSourceLookup (bitDepth from ffprobe) to gate. Ensures Gemini vision review sees colors as they'll render in final MP4.

title: Paused video frame provider for accurate stills
text: When transport is paused, decode the exact video frame at the requested timestamp via a provider (ffmpeg/WebCodecs), overlay a canvas synced to layout (transform, opacity, filters), and virtualize currentTime so seeks don't jump. Reuses surfaces, holds native snapshot during provider swap, applies native video look.
how: Replace preflight.py's current still capture (likely video.currentTime seek + drawImage) with a PausedVideoFrames session. Provider = Cloudflare FLUX or local ffmpeg. Call prepare({video, source, time}) per scene, present(), refresh() for layout changes. Guarantees Gemini sees the exact frame at the scene's in-point.

title: Mutation timing filter for efficient rebind
text: A MutationObserver filter that only triggers on timing-relevant changes: attributes data-start/data-duration/id, or insertion/removal of <video>, <audio>, <source>, <script>, or elements with those attributes. Ignores text edits and unrelated DOM changes.
how: In doctor.py / rebind logic, use this filter on the preview DOM to detect when a scene's timing actually changed, avoiding full recomposition on irrelevant mutations. Port createTimingRecordFilter to Python (lxml/mutation-observer polyfill) or keep in Node sidecar.

title: Media fetch timing for stall attribution
text: Track each media element's fetch start via `loadstart` event (or Resource Timing API) to compute `fetchMs` at any moment. When playback health reports a stall, the `heldBy` field identifies the element with the longest ongoing fetch. This distinguishes network stalls from decode stalls. Reset on seek or layout change.
how: In `review.py`, when running the headless Chrome validation, inject a script that listens for `loadstart` on all `<video>`/`<audio>` and records `performance.now()`. Expose `heldByMedia(element, nowMs)` to the Python side via CDP. Correlate with playback health `heldBy` to label stalls as 'network' vs 'decode' in the review report.

title: Keep‑playing seek for scrubbing without pause
text: `seek(time, { keepPlaying: true })` preserves playback state: it pauses, seeks, then resumes master and siblings with current `playbackRate`. Used for A/E jump‑to‑in/out shortcuts. Default seek without options pauses.
how: In our preview player (Studio360 Telegram approval), wire the scrubber to call `player.seek(t, { keepPlaying: true })` so playback continues after jump. The runtime player already supports this option.

title: Defensive timeline method invocation
text: Use `safeNum(obj, 'duration', 0)` and `safeVoid(obj, 'play')` to handle timelines where `duration` is a number property or methods are missing. Logs non‑conformant shapes via `swallow` but never throws. Keeps player resilient to user‑authored timeline‑like objects.
how: Adopt `safeNum`/`safeVoid` patterns in our compose.py GSAP timeline wrappers and any custom timeline adapters (e.g., Three.js, Lottie).

title: Media release with whole‑file buffered check
text: `releaseMedia(el, whenBuffered)` drops `src` and calls `load()` to free network buffers, but skips if the entire file is already buffered (buffered.length===1, covers duration ±0.1s). Option `whenBuffered=true` forces release even when fully buffered.
how: In our render pipeline's cleanup (doctor.py, after render), call `releaseMedia` on all media elements to reclaim memory. Use `whenBuffered=true` for long source clips we know we won't replay.

title: Raster‑hint optimization for scaled previews
text: When preview scale <1, drop `will-change: transform` on positioned layers that don't create stacking contexts. A MutationObserver + stylesheet watcher marks/unmarks layers with `data-hf-preview-raster` and sets `will-change: auto`. Batches reads then writes to avoid layout thrashing. Restores hints at scale=1.
how: Call `setPreviewRasterScale(scale)` from our preview iframe resize handler. The module auto‑observes DOM/style changes. Reduces GPU memory in Studio360 preview when zoomed out.

title: Relative Timing Expressions
text: Support 'data-start' expressions like 'intro + 2' or 'scene1 - 0.5' instead of absolute seconds. A resolver walks the DOM to find the referenced ID and calculates the start time based on the target's end (start + duration).
how: Modify 'plan.py' to output relative IDs for scenes. Implement a 'startResolver' in our JS runtime that parses these strings and updates GSAP timeline offsets dynamically, allowing scenes to shift if a previous scene's duration changes.

title: NLE-Style Audio Scrubbing
text: Play short (140ms) bursts of the music/voice track at a lower volume (e.g., 25%) when the playhead is manually dragged in the studio. Automatically pause and restore original volume/mute state after dragging stops.
how: Add 'scrubAudio.ts' logic to our Studio360 preview. It should listen for playhead drag events, lease the audio element from the main clock, and trigger short .play() calls at the target timestamp.

title: Media Proxy 202/503 Polling
text: Handle asynchronous asset generation by polling with 'Retry-After' headers. If a fetch returns 202 (Accepted/Processing) or 503 (Service Unavailable), wait the specified duration before retrying the asset load.
how: Update our asset loader in the runtime to check response status. If 202/503 is received, use a 'wallSetTimeout' based on the 'Retry-After' header before attempting to re-assign the 'src' to the video/image element.

title: Media start basis attribute prevents double-counted host offset
text: Media elements use data-hf-media-start-basis to declare whether data-start is composition-local (default, host offset added) or root-global (already absolute, host offset must NOT be added). All media-start derivations (clip manifest, visibility, WebAudio scheduling) must route through a single resolver.
how: In compose_lab.py and compose.py, when writing media elements, set data-hf-media-start-basis="composition" (default) or "root". Ensure plan.py and preflight.py use a single resolveMediaStartForElement function that respects this basis.

title: Authored track index honored verbatim including zero
text: data-track-index is parsed as integer, honoring 0 as valid top lane. Mixed-kind tracks (video + element) keep same index — no renumbering. Track index is display-only; render never reads it. Prevents track drift on every editor move.
how: In plan.py and compose.py, when writing clips, preserve data-track-index exactly as authored. In preflight.py timeline validation, do not renumber tracks by kind. Parse with parseInt(raw,10) and fallback only if NaN.

title: Persistent overlays opt-in via data-timeline-role
text: Direct children of root with data-timeline-role="overlay" or "persistent-overlay" appear as full-duration clips only when explicitly opted in. Skips script/style/link/meta and display:none elements. Prevents backdrop layers from making composition read as one long clip.
how: In compose_lab.py, for persistent UI elements (channel handle, branding), add data-timeline-role="overlay". In preflight.py timeline collection, only include such elements if role matches and computed display !== none. Assign to separate track.

title: Single-clock bridge interval with drift budget
text: Transport clock posts timeline samples every frame and at least every 80 ms (bridgeMaxPostIntervalMs). Parent-frame audio mirror requires 2 consecutive over-threshold samples before correction → worst-case A/V re-sync latency = 160 ms. Raising the interval requires auditing the drift sample count.
how: In our transport clock (review.py/doctor.py), set bridge post interval to 80 ms and drift detection to 2 samples. Add a constant cross-reference comment linking the two values so future changes keep latency < 200 ms.

title: Stacking context partitioning for timeline layering
text: Clips partitioned by nearest CSS stacking context ancestor (transform, opacity<1, filter, isolation, contain:paint, etc.). Clips without such ancestor share css:root context. An element's own z-index scopes to its parent context, not a context it creates.
how: Add resolveCssStackingContextId to our timeline module. In preflight.py, when building clip list, compute stackingContextId per clip. Use for z-order validation and thumbnail layering. Recognize 12+ stacking context triggers per spec.

title: Preserve authored media labels across source changes
text: If an element has id, data-timeline-label, data-label, or aria-label, that label persists even when src attribute changes. Fallback: decode filename from src (URL-decode, strip query, path). Works with base href = about:blank.
how: In thumb.py / compose.py, when generating clip manifests or thumbnails, read label from element.id → data-timeline-label → data-label → aria-label → decoded src filename. Ensure our asset swap logic (Muse/FLUX regeneration) keeps the label.

title: Timeline rebind policy with play-hold
text: Rebind timeline metadata periodically (every 60 frames) but hold rebinds for the first 2 seconds of playback (PLAY_REBIND_HOLD_SECONDS) to prevent async races during startup. Also respects a playing-poll timer (PLAYING_POLL_INTERVAL_MS) instead of frame counter while playing.
how: Add timelineRebindPolicy.ts logic to our render/preview loop (compose.py / render worker). Before each rebind, call shouldAttemptPeriodicTimelineBind with current tick, isPlaying, hasCapturedTimeline, currentTimeSeconds. Set PLAY_REBIND_HOLD_SECONDS=2, TIMELINE_REBIND_INTERVAL_FRAMES=60.

title: Parked transport loop with heartbeat
text: When paused and settled, stop requesting animation frames entirely. Keep a single timer (PARK_HEARTBEAT_MS=80ms) that wakes to deliver late-arriving changes: DOM mutations (new clips, duration edits), media metadata (durationchange), window.__timelines registry updates, manual-edit gestures, and adapter duration growth. Switches to 1s heartbeat when parent requests idle-heartbeat.
how: Implement in our render worker's preview loop (or headless render). After quiesce (no pending frames, timers ≤1), park: cancel RAF, start setInterval(heartbeat, 80ms). Heartbeat re-reads clip manifest, checks window.__timelines, fires MutationObserver flush. Resume RAF on play/seek/gesture. Teardown clears timer.

title: VFX chain validation rules
text: Chains must have version 1; unknown effect types or unsupported versions cause loud registration failure with zero hosts registered. Params outside def ranges are clamped (e.g., contrast 99999 → 1000).
how: In preflight.py, validate each scene's VFX chain JSON against these rules before render; reject chains with version !=1 or unknown types.

title: Hidden host capture behavior
text: visibility:hidden on self-capture host skips capture entirely (no barrier wait). Backdrop host with visibility:hidden still captures layers below (pass-through). display:none on ref ancestor hides ref (captured as empty). Ref with data-vfx-ref-visible stays captured even if host hidden.
how: In compose_lab.py, use visibility:hidden to disable self-capture without breaking backdrop pass-through. For ref layers that must persist, add data-vfx-ref-visible attribute.

title: Ref param deduplication and mandatory vs optional
text: Same ref element captured once per frame (u_src2 bound to same texture unit). Mandatory refs (luma-matte matte) require element with capture wrapper; self-reference binds u_src2=u_src. Optional refs (displacement-map map) fall back to self-pixels (u_hasSrc2=0).
how: In compose_lab.py, reuse ref elements across nodes; for mandatory refs ensure wrapper exists. Use optional refs for displacement maps with self-reference fallback.

title: Engine mode vs preview capture paths
text: Engine mode (render) uses page-composite protocol: paintVfx sets __hf_page_composite_pending, external resolver calls drawElementImage, then kernel draws. Preview path uses canvas.requestPaint() and paint event. Both clear src canvas before and after draw (except backdrop hidden).
how: In publish.py render pipeline, ensure engineMode=true is passed. For preview server, implement requestPaint/paint event loop. Verify double-clear behavior matches test expectations.

title: Canvas sizing uses layout box not transformed rect
text: Output canvas size and u_size uniform derive from host's offsetWidth/offsetHeight (layout box), not getBoundingClientRect (which includes transforms). Prevents stretched captures on scaled/rotated hosts.
how: In compose_lab.py, ensure VFX host elements have explicit width/height via CSS (not transform). Add preflight check that host offsetWidth/Height > 0.

title: VFX error signatures for automated triage
text: Errors prefix with '[HyperFrames] composition script error:' and contain patterns: 'vfx', 'version', 'unknown effect type', 'WebGL2', 'hf-vfx-src', 'nested inside another capture canvas', 'chrome://flags/#canvas-draw-element', 'measures 0×0', 'no paint arrived within 2000ms', 'BeginFrame'.
how: In review.py, parse render logs for these patterns to auto-classify VFX failures. Add specific handlers for context loss, missing capture wrapper, and paint timeout.

title: WebGL context loss monitoring
text: Runtime reports context lost once via webglcontextlost event, stops painting that host, and rebuilds on webglcontextrestored. A second loss event before restore is silent. Rebuild only occurs when context is actually restored.
how: In doctor.py, add WebGL context loss detection for Chrome render processes; trigger HyperFrames rebuildLostVfx on restore. Log contextLost events for alerting.

title: VFX registry cleanup on re-initialization
text: initVfx forgets previous composition's hosts when called again (document.body.innerHTML='' then re-init). paintVfx after re-init with empty body produces zero GL calls. Ensures no stale entries across composition reloads.
how: In doctor.py, when detecting stuck VFX jobs, call initVfx(document.body, fps) after clearing body to reset registry. Verify registry length zero before new composition load.

title: Web Audio CORS classification with opaque-document reason
text: classifyWebAudioMediaRoute returns {kind:'web-audio'} or {kind:'decode-only', reason:'cross_origin_no_cors'|'opaque_document_origin', asset}. Opaque origin (sandbox without allow-same-origin) wins over cross-origin because author can't fix by moving asset. crossorigin attribute presence (any value) is opt-in; empty string IDL property counts.
how: In mix.py/audio pipeline, before creating MediaElementSource for TTS/music beds, classify the source URL: if cross-origin without crossorigin, fetch+decodeAudioData instead; if document origin is 'null', require allow-same-origin or CORS headers. Log once per asset.

title: Four capture modes with clear bitmap/upload semantics
text: CAPTURE_TO_TEXTURE (upload, clear bitmap), CAPTURE_PASS_THROUGH (no upload, keep bitmap for backdrop), CAPTURE_VISIBLE_SOURCE (upload, keep bitmap), CAPTURE_VISIBLE_ONLY (no upload, keep bitmap). Each matches a source role.
how: When designing capture for lab look elements, classify each source: main host → TO_TEXTURE; backdrop wrapper → PASS_THROUGH; visible ref → VISIBLE_SOURCE; visible ref while host hidden → VISIBLE_ONLY. Implement in capture pipeline.

title: Deterministic VFX paint contract for export parity
text: Shaders read only (u_size, u_t, u_fps, params, u_src) — no clock, randomness, or inter-frame state. This determinism is what the exporter's gate depends on. Every failure logs with '[HyperFrames] composition script error:' prefix to fail render.
how: Ensure all custom HyperFrames shaders for lab look (stat counters, HUD, charts) are pure functions of those uniforms. No Date.now(), Math.random(), or frame counters. Any violation breaks export parity; add lint rule.

title: Wall-clock timers that ignore virtual/film time
text: wallSetTimeout/wallClearTimeout read original browser timers from __HF_VIRTUAL_TIME__.originalSetTimeout, so deadlines fire on real time even when page timers are paused or driven by seek. Test enforces no raw setTimeout/setInterval in runtime code.
how: Add a wall_clock.py module exposing wall_set_timeout/wall_clear_timeout that use time.monotonic + threading.Timer (or asyncio loop.call_later) for doctor.py self-repair, render watchdogs, and any deadline that must not stretch with film time.

title: Uniform location caching at program link time
text: resolveUniformLocations caches all gl.getUniformLocation calls once per program (size, t, fps, src, src2, hasSrc2, params). Null locations (optimised out) are stored and gl.uniform*(null,…) is a defined no-op. Eliminates per-frame driver queries.
how: In compose_lab.py's HyperFrames render path, after compiling shader programs, resolve and cache uniform locations in a dict keyed by program. Reuse in paint loop. Applies to any custom WebGL effects (stat counters, HUD, charts).

title: Ping-pong framebuffer manager for multi-pass VFX
text: ensurePingPong creates two RGBA textures+framebuffers at host size; passes alternate writing to index%2. Recreates only on size change. Deletes old GL objects on rebuild. Used when chain length > 1.
how: In compose_lab.py, when a scene has multiple chained WebGL effects (e.g., displacement → color grade → vignette), allocate ping-pong pair at scene resolution and bind alternately. Release on scene unload or resolution change.

title: Diagnostic latching with WeakSet and render-mode gate
text: reportWebAudioMediaRoute emits console.info with token [hyperframes] runtime_web_audio_bypass and posts bridge diagnostic once per element (WeakSet). Suppressed during export render (__HF_EXPORT_RENDER_SEEK_CONFIG) because producer mixes offline.
how: In mix.py, when Web Audio fallback occurs, log a structured warning with asset URL, reason, and lost processing (fx-chain, automation, audio-group, above-unity-gain) once per asset. Suppress during final render pass (offline mix).

title: Onended cleanup restores element.muted and disposes FX
text: When an AudioBufferSourceNode fires 'ended', automatically: remove from _activeSources, disconnect sourceNode and gainNode, dispose FX graph (if any), restore element.muted to priorMuted. If stopAll() already ran, the later 'ended' is a no-op (doesn't clobber restored state). Ensures no leaked audio nodes or stuck muted elements.
how: In review.py's vision/audio check, verify that after a clip ends naturally, the element is unmuted (unless it was muted before). Add a test render of a 2s VO clip; confirm no audio context leaks via Chrome DevTools. Document in brain.jsonl as 'Audio node lifecycle: onended cleanup'.

title: Media-element route for TTS and clips (no decode)
text: Route <audio> elements via createMediaElementSource instead of decoding to AudioBuffer. Preserves native playback rate, avoids resampling, keeps pitch, and uses zero extra memory. Set element.volume=1, muted=false; control level via WebAudio gain nodes. Cache the MediaElementAudioSourceNode per element+context.
how: In compose_lab.py / compose.py, when adding VO or SFX <audio> tags, set data-hf-route="media-element". In the HyperFrames runtime (or a custom render hook), detect this and call scheduleMediaElementPlayback instead of schedulePlayback. Ensure the element has crossorigin="anonymous" for CDN assets.

title: Clip duration bounding with in-point shift
text: When scheduling a clip, bound its playback to the authored window [mediaStart, mediaStart+clipDuration]. For in-progress clips: start at max(0, compTime - compStart) + mediaStart, duration = min(remaining, clipDuration - elapsed). For future clips: delay = (compStart - compTime) / globalRate. If window already elapsed, return null (don't schedule). Supports sub-composition in-point shifts via extra inPoint parameter.
how: In plan.py / compose.py, pass clipDuration and inPoint (default 0) to the scheduler. In the HyperFrames render hook, implement schedulePlayback with these bounds. Use for Ken Burns clips, B-roll trims, and VO segments that must end exactly at scene boundary.

title: Seek under dip for click-free media-element seeks
text: When seeking a routed media element, dip its gain to 0 over ~15 ms, wait for dip to settle, set element.currentTime, wait for 'seeked' event, then ramp gain back to 1. If stopAll occurs during dip, abort seek. Only applies to elements the transport routes (ownsElement).
how: In the render pipeline, when a scene change or user scrub seeks a media-element clip, call transport.seekUnderDip(el, targetTime). Implement dip using a dedicated gain node (inserted after mediaElementSource) with linearRampToValueAtTime(0, now+0.015) then ramp up on 'seeked'. Add to review.py to verify no clicks on scene transitions.

title: Generation counter for async race prevention
text: Every playback start increments a generation counter. schedulePlayback/scheduleMediaElementPlayback capture current generation; if stopAll() or new generation starts before the async scheduling resolves, the pending promise resolves null and the clip is discarded. Prevents stale schedules from playing after scene swap.
how: In WebAudioTransport wrapper, add startGeneration() returning incrementing integer. Pass gen to all schedule calls. In scheduleMediaElementPlayback, await ctx.resume() then check if gen === currentGeneration(); if not, return null. In doctor.py, verify no stuck generations after code hot-reload.

title: Wiggle easing for organic motion
text: Spring-like wiggle eases (easeOut, easeInOut, anticipate, uniform) with configurable wiggles and amplitude. Deterministic, endpoint-normalized (0→1), and oscillatory. Default amplitudes: easeOut 0.16, easeInOut 0.08, uniform 0.14, anticipate 0.12. Cached by normalized parameters.
how: Add wiggle() parser to GSAP ease map in compose_lab.py. Use for UI panel entrances, stat counter overshoots, HUD element jitter. Example: gsap.to(el, {x: 100, ease: 'wiggle(6, easeInOut, 0.1)'}).

title: Platform safe-area definitions
text: Explicit clear bands for TikTok (720×1280, two stepped bands), Reels (100×100%, 14% top, 35% bottom, 6% sides), Shorts (1080×1920, 288–1248px vertical, 48–888px horizontal). Also action-safe (90%) and title-safe (80%) percent boxes.
how: In thumb.py and compose.py, import SOCIAL_SAFE_AREAS. During layout, clamp text/graphics bounding boxes to the active platform's clear bands. Add a preflight check that validates all critical elements stay within safe zones.

title: Per-group audio buses with post-FX fader
text: Group bus chain: input → FX → fader (post-FX, data-volume × volume lane) → muteGain → output → master. Fader post-FX ensures compressors react to pre-fader signal. Bus persists across stopAll() to avoid rebuild; re-anchors automation each play generation.
how: In mix.py, when mixing stems (VO, music, SFX), route each group through a post-FX gain node. Apply group volume automation on that node. Keep bus nodes alive across renders; re-schedule automation on new generation.

title: WebGL context loss/restore handler
text: Capture-phase listeners on document: preventDefault on webglcontextlost, then on webglcontextrestored schedule a single requestAnimationFrame to call onRestored(). Returns a stop() function to remove listeners. Ensures GPU scenes repaint after context restore without duplicate frames.
how: If we add Three.js/WebGPU scenes (future 3D), wrap the renderer init with watchSceneWebglContexts(() => renderer.render()). Call stop() on scene unmount. Add to compose_lab.py's GPU composition mount.

title: AudioContext idle suspension
text: Suspend AudioContext after 10 s of silence (no active sources, no captured playing elements). Resume on next play. Handles browser-initiated suspend/resume, failed suspend retry, and tracks handed-over elements. Saves CPU/battery on preview servers.
how: In the render worker's audio setup, implement a 10 s wall-clock timer that calls audioContext.suspend() when no sources are active. Clear timer on any play/seek. Handle statechange events to reset timer.

title: Structured storyboard markdown with frame lifecycle
text: STORYBOARD.md uses frontmatter (format, message, arc, audience) and H2/H3 headings (Frame/Beat/Scene N — Title) with metadata lines (duration, transition_in, status, src, scene, voiceover, poster). Status defaults to 'outline' then 'built' then 'animated'. Unknown keys preserved in extra.
how: Replace plan.py's JSON scene plan with STORYBOARD.md writer. Parser in parseStoryboard.ts gives frames array with durationSeconds, transitionIn, status, narrative. Use status to gate render stages in doctor.py.

title: Frame poster time for contact sheet thumbnails
text: Storyboard frame accepts 'poster' metadata (seconds) — representative time past intro animation for contact sheet. Falls back to heuristic. Parsed as float from first number in value (e.g., '2.5s' → 2.5).
how: In thumb.py, read frame.poster from parsed storyboard. Seek to that time in rendered MP4 for thumbnail frame. If absent, default to 10% of frame duration.

title: Preview marking and service worker cleanup for headless validation
text: markedForStudio() checks meta[name=hyperframes-studio-preview] and not servedToAnotherSite. dropServiceWorkers() unregisters all origin workers before capture. refusedPreviewStatus() extracts HTTP status from error message. PREVIEW_ONLY_ATTRS lists attributes stripped for production.
how: In review.py's vision review, inject STUDIO_PREVIEW_MARK_META via headless Chrome. Call dropServiceWorkers() before each capture. Strip PREVIEW_ONLY_ATTRS from final render output.

title: CSS Variable Slug Collision Detection
text: `slugify` lowercases, collapses non-alphanumerics to single hyphens, trims hyphens. `detectSlugCollisions` returns groups of distinct IDs that map to the same `--slug`. Used by Figma importer and runtime to warn about variable-name collisions before they cause silent style merges.
how: In `plan.py` when generating composition variables from scene data, run `detectSlugCollisions(allVariableIds)` and log a warning if any groups >1. Append a numeric suffix to later duplicates in the variable declaration pass.

title: HTML Attribute Allowlist & URI Sanitization
text: `ALLOWED_HTML_ATTRS` (70+ entries) and `URI_BEARING_ATTRS` define a strict allowlist. `isAllowedHtmlAttribute` blocks `on*` handlers, allows `data-*`/`aria-*`. `isSafeAttributeValue` rejects `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, and `data:text/html` URIs on src/href/poster/srcset. Single source of truth for all trust boundaries.
how: Adopt these constants in `preflight.py` when validating any HTML snippets we inject (e.g., lower-third templates, end-card markup). Replace our ad-hoc attribute filtering with `isAllowedHtmlAttribute` and `isSafeAttributeValue`.

title: Local-Calendar Render Timestamps
text: `formatRenderOutputTimestamp` returns `YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS` using the local timezone (not UTC), zero-padded. Used for render output filenames and job logs. No dependencies, deterministic for a given `Date` object.
how: Standardize all our pipeline timestamps (render outputs, `stats.py` reports, `doctor.py` logs) to this format. Replace `datetime.now().isoformat()` calls with `formatRenderOutputTimestamp(new Date())` via a small Python port or Node helper.

title: WebGL2 VFX Chain for Lab Look
text: HyperFrames ships five ready-to-use GLSL ES 3.00 kernels (fractal-noise, wave-warp, displacement-map, luma-matte, noise) with versioned JSON chain schema, parameter normalization, and capture modes (self/backdrop/none). Each effect has CPU reference implementations for testing parity. The chain is stored in a `data-vfx-chain` attribute and parsed/validated at render time.
how: Add a `vfxChain` field to our scene plan schema; in compose_lab.py, emit `data-vfx-chain` on lab-layer elements. Use the provided `normalizeVfxParams` at render time. Start with `fractal-noise` for background textures and `wave-warp` for kinetic titles.

title: Canvas-Based Text Measurement for Layout
text: `pretext` exposes `prepare`, `layout`, `prepareWithSegments`, `measureLineStats`, `measureNaturalWidth` — all canvas-based, no DOM reflow. `prepare` returns an opaque measured string; `layout` gives lineCount and height for a width. Cache keyed by (segment, font) bounds memory to vocabulary size. Deliberately omits mutable `clearCache`/`setLocale`.
how: Replace any `getBoundingClientRect` or `measureText` calls in our headless Chrome render path with `pretext` functions. In `compose_lab.py`, use `measureNaturalWidth` for kinetic title width calculations and `layout` for multi-line caption box sizing before GSAP animation.

title: Exact 32-bit integer math for shader parity
text: Use Math.imul(a, b) >>> 0 for every multiplication and >>> 0 after every bitwise op to replicate GLSL uint32 overflow. The fractalNoiseHashUnit and noiseByteRef show the pattern: seed mixing, LCG steps, and final scaling must stay in 32-bit unsigned space.
how: Audit all custom GLSL kernels (lab look: kinetic titles, panel shine, HUD) and their CPU counterparts. Replace any plain * or + with Math.imul and >>> 0. Ensure constants (mulX, mulY, lcgMulA, etc.) are imported from the .frag.ts file so they never drift.

title: Config auto-disable for problematic platform combos
text: On Windows + software GPU (or --disable-gpu / --low-memory-mode) + single worker, automatically disable streaming encode (VP9) because the field signal shows 156s renders fail. Keep an escape hatch via PRODUCER_ENABLE_STREAMING_ENCODE=true or programmatic override. Log the auto-disable for telemetry.
how: In doctor.py / server config, replicate shouldAutoDisableStreamingEncodeOnWin32Compound logic: if platform==win32 and (browserGpuMode==software or disableGpu or lowMemoryMode) and workers==1 and not userExplicitlySet, set enableStreamingEncode=false and flag streamingEncodeAutoDisabledOnWin32Compound=true. Apply before renderOrchestrator starts.

title: HDR LUT generation with JS Math.round parity
text: When generating sRGB→BT.2020 (HLG/PQ) LUTs for HDR thumbnails/covers, use js_round_nonneg(x) = floor(x + 0.5) to match JavaScript's Math.round (half toward +∞). Python's round() uses banker's rounding and diverges on ~10 probe values. Keep constants (HLG_A, PQ_M1, SDR_NITS=203) in sync with the shader.
how: If thumb.py ever adds HDR cover support, port generate-lut-reference.py logic to a Python script in the studio repo. Use the same probe indices (0,1,10,32,64,96,128,160,192,224,254,255) and verify against a JS reference. Store LUTs as JSON and load in thumb.py for color conversion.

title: Deterministic CPU references for custom VFX kernels
text: Create pure TypeScript CPU mirrors of every GLSL kernel (fractal-noise, wave-warp, noise, luma-matte) using identical constants and 32-bit wrapping arithmetic (Math.imul, >>> 0). Enforce PSNR ≥ 32 dB against GPU output on 4 sample frames in preflight.
how: Add a vfx/refs/ folder mirroring packages/core/src/vfx/refs/. For each lab-look effect (stat counters, charts, flows), write a *_ref.ts that exports a pure function (p, t, params) => value. Hook into preflight.py to render a few frames headless, read pixels via CDP, compare with CPU reference, fail if PSNR < 32 dB.

title: Browser integration tests for critical runtime functions
text: Launch headless Chrome with Puppeteer, inject the real runtime IIFE (buildHyperframesRuntimeScript), and test fitTextFontSize (short text fits at base 78px, wide text shrinks, extreme hits minFontSize 42) and position edits (GSAP + GSAP-free). Output structured JSON events for CI parsing.
how: Add packages/engine/scripts/test-*-browser.ts for each runtime export (fitTextFontSize, positionEdits, svgSelectorAliases). Run in CI on every PR. Use the existing vitest.setup.ts userAgent stub. Skip gracefully if puppeteer/gsap not installed (log JSON event).

title: Enforce vitest coverage thresholds in CI
text: Set minimum coverage floors (statements 75%, branches 70%, functions 80%, lines 75%) and fail the build if they drop. Exclude test files, types, entry points. This catches untested branches in runtime code (clipTree, mediaSteer, positionEdits, etc.) before they reach production.
how: Add a vitest.config.ts to the studio repo (or extend existing test config) with coverage.thresholds matching packages/core/vitest.config.ts. Run vitest run --coverage in CI pipeline. Treat threshold failure as a blocking error.

title: Low-memory mode auto-detection
text: Engine auto-enables lowMemoryMode when total RAM ≤ 8GB (LOW_MEMORY_TOTAL_MB_THRESHOLD). It collapses pipeline: skips calibration browser, pins to single worker, prefers screenshot capture over BeginFrame. Override with PRODUCER_LOW_MEMORY_MODE env or --low-memory-mode flag.
how: In doctor.py, add system RAM check (psutil.virtual_memory().total) and set HF_LOW_MEMORY_MODE=1 when ≤8GB; also pass --low-memory-mode to hyperframes render calls.

title: DrawElement fast capture with worker encode
text: On macOS/Windows with hardware GPU and Chrome ≥151, useDrawElement + enableDrawElementWorkerEncode gives 1.65–1.96× wall-time speedup by encoding JPEG in OffscreenCanvas worker while main thread paints next frame. Auto-clamped to supported platforms; explicit opt-in via PRODUCER_EXPERIMENTAL_FAST_CAPTURE=true bypasses clamp.
how: Set env PRODUCER_EXPERIMENTAL_FAST_CAPTURE=true and HF_DE_WORKER_ENCODE=true in render worker; ensure Chrome version ≥151 (check chromeMajorCeiling).

title: Page-side shader compositing for lab look
text: enablePageSideCompositing=true runs SDR shader transitions inside Chrome via WebGL, capturing one opaque frame per output frame, skipping Node-side per-pixel blend worker pool. Default ON in config. Incompatible with drawElement (auto-disabled). Mac viability: Metal/CoreAnimation accelerated. Determinism: PSNR-based not byte-identical.
how: Keep HF_PAGE_SIDE_COMPOSITING=true (default) for lab look videos with shader transitions; ensure drawElement is off for those compositions.

title: Protocol timeout scales with canvas pixel area
text: scaleProtocolTimeoutForComposition multiplies base protocolTimeout (default 300s) by (width*height)/(1920*1080), capped at 30min. Prevents CDP timeout on large compositions (4K). Pure function, exported for tests.
how: In preflight.py, compute output resolution and pass scaled timeout to HyperFrames render call via protocolTimeout config; or set PRODUCER_PUPPETEER_PROTOCOL_TIMEOUT_MS to scaled value.

title: Static frame deduplication
text: staticFrameDedup=true (default) reuses byte-identical frames instead of re-seeking + re-screenshotting. Anchor-verified at init. Only arms in screenshot capture mode. Disable with HF_STATIC_DEDUP=false/0/off.
how: Ensure HF_STATIC_DEDUP not set to false; for static scenes (end cards, title cards) this avoids redundant capture.

title: Video layer passthrough for full-screen video
text: videoLayerPassthrough=true (opt-in via HF_VIDEO_LAYER_PASSTHROUGH) makes ffmpeg composite a full-canvas source video under the page capture, avoiding Chrome decode/render of that video layer. Useful for background video plates.
how: Set HF_VIDEO_LAYER_PASSTHROUGH=true for compositions where a single video covers entire canvas (e.g., B-roll background).

title: Frame data URI cache with byte budget
text: frameDataUriCacheLimit (default 256, min 32) and frameDataUriCacheBytesLimitMb (default 1500MB, min 64MB) evict oldest entries when byte budget exceeded. Memory-adaptive defaults: <4GB RAM → 32 entries/128MB; ≤8GB → 64/256MB.
how: Set PRODUCER_FRAME_DATA_URI_CACHE_LIMIT and PRODUCER_FRAME_DATA_URI_CACHE_BYTES_MB via env to match worker memory (e.g., 128 entries / 768MB for 8GB workers).

title: Motion blur differential verification
text: blurDifferential.ts implements trailMask (dilated changed pixels), meanFrame (average of sub-frames), compareTiles (block MAE inside/outside trail), and pinned symptom tracking (withinSymptomBand 0.5–2×). Used to verify motion-blur capture equals blur-off reference.
how: Port trailMask, meanFrame, compareTiles to review.py; for motion-blur scenes, render blur-on and blur-off, compare tiles outside trail (MAE≤8) and inside trail against meanFrame. Flag regressions.

title: Deterministic Fixture Generation for Regression Tests
text: Generate test compositions from seed using LCG (state = (state × 1664525 + 1013904223) >>> 0). Pick 1–4 features from 19 (transform, rotation, canvas2d, webgl, svgClip, mask, cssKeyframes, etc.) without repetition. Place in 6 slots (3×2 grid). Checkpoints at 2 of {0.5,1.0,1.5}s; mover at 0.2 or 1.8s. Excludes known filter-tier failures (clip-path, visibility). Produces 200+ unique fixtures for CI.
how: Adopt for visual regression suite: seed = hash of scene plan + code version. Generate fixtures in test/visual/, render with HyperFrames, compare to oracle (32-sample blur). Store seeds in brain.jsonl for reproducibility.

title: Oracle-Based Quality Thresholds
text: Ground truth: 32-sample sub-frame blur (oracle). Oracle noise = 3.94 MAE, smallest symptom = 14.47 MAE. Threshold = geometric mean ≈ 7.55 MAE. Sweep fixtures quantify defects: blend-difference 148.6, ancestor-drop-shadow 73.0, own-clip-polygon 27.6, overlapping-movers 14.5 (at oracle limit), rise-from-below 18.3. Use to set per-effect quality gates.
how: In compose_lab.py, when using motion blur on lab elements (stat counters, UI panels), tag elements with data-motion-blur-tier='capture' for simple transforms, 'filter' for complex (WebGL, clip-path, fixed children). Preflight checks tier matches expectation.

title: Parallel AAC Encoding with Pre-Roll
text: For audio >60s, split into 1–8 frame-aligned segments (1024 samples/frame). Each segment encodes with 469-frame pre-roll (≈10s) and 8-frame post-roll using `-cpuflags 0` for determinism. Keep frames [cut−preRoll, nextCut−preRoll). Join ADTS frames, then mux with `-itsoffset -1024/48000` and `setts=duration` to match single-encoder output. Cold-start loudness jump on quiet openings reduced from 2.7–3.3 dB to <0.1 dB.
how: Replace mix.py's single ffmpeg AAC encode with encodeAac() logic: plan segments, run parallel ffmpeg with pre-roll, join frames, final mux. Use existing runFfmpeg utility. Ensures deterministic bytes for caching.

title: Bake volume envelopes on float samples before 16-bit quantization
text: Apply gain automation to float32 samples output by the FX chain, then clamp to ±1.0 when writing 16-bit WAV. If you clamp first then duck, a +6 dB peaking band on a 0.9 tone clips to 1.0 and the subsequent −12 dB envelope leaves distortion baked in; preview (float throughout) never has this artifact.
how: In mix.py, after applyAudioFxChain returns float planes, run createEnvelopeWalker(keyframes) and multiply each frame across all channels before writeWav(..., float=false). Ensure writeWav clamps instead of wrapping.

title: Automatic pre-roll calculation from effect memory
text: Each effect contributes memory: delay = time_ms × −ln(0.001)/ln(feedback) / 1000; reverb = 0.6 + 1.3×size; compressor/limiter/gate = 6.9×release_ms/1000. Sum for serial chain. Windowed render uses max(floor, min(cap, needed)). Warn if capped. Floor 10 s, cap 300 s default.
how: In audioFxWarmup.chainWarmupSeconds, implement MEMORY map for our effect types. In applyAudioFxChain, call windowPrerollSeconds(chain, limits.prerollSeconds, limits.maxPrerollSeconds) and use returned seconds for segment readFrom. Log warning when capped.

title: Empty track guard prevents whole-render crash
text: ffmpeg writes valid but zero-length WAV when trim starts past source end. OfflineAudioContext(…, 0, rate) throws, bypassing per-track failure collector and killing the entire render. Detect zero frames before launching browser and return input path untouched.
how: In mix.py, after reading WAV header, if dataBytes == 0 or frames == 0, skip FX chain and return {path: input, envelopeBaked: false}. Add test: writeWav(empty.wav, Float32Array(0), 48000) → processCompositionAudio succeeds.

title: WAV I/O supports 16-bit PCM and 32-bit float, handles >2 GiB via header-only read
text: readWavHeader reads first 64 KiB, parses fmt/data chunks, resolves data size (0 or 0xFFFFFFFF = to EOF). readWav loads whole file if ≤2 GiB, else throws. writeWav emits 16-bit PCM by default (for envelope baker), float=true for group sub-mixes needing headroom. Clamps to ±1.0 before scaling to int16.
how: In our audio utils, adopt readWavHeader for quick probe. In writeWav, default to 16-bit; add float param for group mixes. Use resolveDataBytes for streamed WAVs. Reject unsupported formats (e.g., 24-bit, 64-bit float) with clear error.

title: Browser CDP transfer chunked at 8 MiB to avoid frame limits
text: Float32Array planes sent to page as base64 chunks of 8 MiB (≈11 MB base64), well under puppeteer's 256 MB WebSocket frame cap. Page reassembles into single Float32Array per channel. Output pulled back same way. Prevents OOM on long stereo tracks.
how: In audioFxRender.sendPlanesToPage/readPlanesFromPage, use TRANSFER_BYTES = 8*1024*1024. Encode plane.buffer.slice(byteOffset, byteOffset+length) to base64 in chunks. On read, decode base64 to Buffer, concat, then Float32Array(view.buffer.slice(byteOffset, byteOffset+byteLength)).

title: Staged mixing for >MAX_MIX_INPUTS tracks
text: When track count exceeds FFmpeg's filter graph input limit (MAX_MIX_INPUTS), automatically split into batches, mix each batch to a temporary float WAV, then fold batches together. Preserves unity gain and avoids clipping. Tested with 2000 tracks.
how: In mix.py, before building filter graph, count inputs. If > MAX_MIX_INPUTS (typically 256), create batch sub-mixes in workDir, then mix those. Use amix=normalize=0 and pad only final output.

title: Limit concurrent FFmpeg prep to half CPU cores
text: During track preparation (trim, atempo, etc.), run no more than floor(availableParallelism()/2) FFmpeg processes simultaneously. Prevents CPU starvation and OOM on large mixes. Verified with 40+ concurrent clips.
how: In mix.py's prepare stage, use a semaphore with limit = max(2, os.cpu_count()//2). Wrap each track's ffmpeg call. Already have OrderedConcurrencyLimiter in brain; apply to audio prep.

title: Fallback to static volume when automation expression fails
text: If FFmpeg rejects the volume automation expression (nesting limit, unsupported), retry mix with base volume only. Surface degradation notice in result.error (e.g., 'base volume'). Keeps audio instead of dropping track.
how: In mix.py, wrap automated mix in try/catch. On ffmpeg filter init error, rebuild filter without :eval=frame volume, re-run. Log warning. Add 'degraded': true to result for dashboard.

title: Filter complex via script file to avoid command-line length limit
text: Write filter graph to a temp file and pass via -filter_complex_script (or -/filter_complex) instead of inline -filter_complex. Keeps command line short regardless of track count. Retries with new flag if legacy removed.
how: In mix.py, generate filter string, write to workDir/filter_XXXX.txt, pass -filter_complex_script path. Catch 'Unrecognized option filter_complex_script' and retry with -/filter_complex. Clean up after ffmpeg exits.

title: Percent-encoded non-Latin filename resolution
text: Audio src attributes may be URL-encoded (e.g., Hindi filenames). Decode before filesystem lookup. Prevents 'file not found' for assets with Unicode names. Tested with Arabic/Devanagari filenames.
how: In mix.py's source resolution, apply urllib.parse.unquote to src before joining with projectDir. Ensure writeFileSync uses decoded name. Already have case-insensitive path normalization; add decode step.

title: Keep float mix WAV for QA alongside final AAC
text: Optionally retain the 32-bit float PCM mix (pre-encode) at a known path (keepEncoderInputAt). Enables loudness verification, clipping checks, and regression comparison without re-rendering.
how: Add keep_float_mix flag to mix.py config. When true, copy final float mix to projectDir/float_mix.wav before AAC encode. Expose in doctor.py for failed loudness checks. Clean up on success unless debug.

title: RDP Keyframe Simplification
text: Use the Ramer–Douglas–Peucker algorithm to simplify volume keyframes. Drop points within a 0.005 (0.5% linear) epsilon of the line through neighbors. This collapses linear fades to two points and eased fades to ~25 segments, staying safely under FFmpeg's expression limits while maintaining perceptual accuracy (within 0.2 dB).
how: Add a simplification utility to mix.py that processes the script's volume automation before generating FFmpeg filter strings.

title: Lossless Mono-to-Stereo Rematrixing
text: Standard `-ac 2` mono-to-stereo conversion attenuates the source by 3dB. Use an explicit pan filter: `pan=stereo|FL=FL+FC|FR=FR+FC`. This maps the front-center channel to both stereo channels at full volume, ensuring voiceovers (like our Charon voice) maintain their intended loudness.
how: Apply this specific pan filter in mix.py whenever processing mono voice tracks or SFX before the final mix.

title: Multi-stage Atempo Chain
text: FFmpeg's `atempo` filter is limited to a range of 0.5 to 2.0. To achieve extreme speed changes (e.g., 4x speed for time-lapses) without pitch shift, chain multiple filters (e.g., `atempo=2.0,atempo=2.0`).
how: Update pace.py to calculate the number of atempo stages required for the target words/sec and generate the chained filter string accordingly.

title: Cross-platform available memory parsing
text: macOS: sum free+inactive+purgeable+speculative pages from `vm_stat` × page size (16384). Linux: read `MemAvailable` from `/proc/meminfo` (kB). Windows/fallback: `os.freemem()`. All return MB, truncated.
how: In `doctor.py` or render scheduler, call a small Node helper (or port logic to Python) to size parallel workers, texture budgets, or SwiftShader thread count per machine.

title: Fingerprint-matched browser lease pool
text: Pool key = JSON-stringified immutable fingerprint (args, executablePath, captureMode, timeouts, etc.). Exact match shares browser; any mutation creates new entry. Ref-counting with graceful close (1s bound then force-kill). Leases are per-caller; ambiguous handle release is rejected.
how: Replace ad-hoc browser reuse in `render.py`/`hyperframes` CLI with this pool. Key off our capture mode (screenshot/beginframe/drawelement), GPU mode, and custom args. Guarantees identical launch flags per render job, avoids cross-job contamination.

title: Vulkan pin stripping for software renders
text: When `browserGpuMode=software` (SwiftShader), drop `VK_DRIVER_FILES`, `VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_SELECT`, `VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_DISABLE` from Chrome's env. Keep them for hardware mode. Also allowlists only safe vars (PATH, etc.), blocks secrets.
how: In `buildChromeArgs`/`browserManager`, before launching software renders, delete Vulkan ICD pins from the env passed to Chrome. Prevents SwiftShader from binding to a physical GPU and failing or producing non-deterministic output.

title: Deterministic Chrome flag set for consistent rendering
text: Use exact flag list: --disable-dev-shm-usage --enable-webgl --ignore-gpu-blocklist --font-render-hinting=none --disable-lcd-text --force-color-profile=srgb --force-device-scale-factor=1 --window-size=W,H --disable-background-timer-throttling --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows --disable-renderer-backgrounding --disable-background-media-suspend --disable-breakpad --disable-component-extensions-with-background-pages --disable-default-apps --disable-extensions --disable-hang-monitor --disable-ipc-flooding-protection --disable-popup-blocking --disable-sync --disable-component-update --disable-domain-reliability --disable-print-preview --no-pings --disk-cache-size=268435456 --autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required plus GPU-mode-specific flags.
how: Audit our current Chrome launch args in compose.py against this list. Add missing flags (especially --force-color-profile=srgb, --force-device-scale-factor=1, --autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required).

title: Windows NTSTATUS Exit Code Mapping
text: Identify specific Windows-only exit codes to debug renderer failures: 0xC0000135 (Missing Visual C++ runtime), 0xC0000017 (OOM), 0xC0000142 (DLL init failure/security block), and 0xC0000022 (Access denied/Antivirus).
how: Update doctor.py to check exit codes against this map when running on Windows, providing specific fix instructions (e.g., 'Install VC++ Redistributable') in the Telegram report.

title: WebM Audio Codec Enforcement
text: When muxing audio into WebM containers, enforce Opus encoding. If the source is AAC, it must be transcoded to Opus to maintain container standards, even if the video frames remain untouched (stream copied).
how: Update mix.py to check the output extension; if .webm, ensure the FFmpeg command specifies -c:a libopus instead of copying AAC streams.

title: Deep Warning Cloning
text: Always deep-clone mutable detail arrays (sources, failureReasons, subprocess evidence) in error/warning objects before they cross async or ownership boundaries to prevent state leakage or mutation during logging.
how: Apply this pattern in the shared brain (knowledge/brain.jsonl) logging logic to ensure error snapshots are immutable.

title: FFconcat Injection Guard
text: Strictly validate filenames before generating ffconcat lists. Refuse any input paths containing line breaks (\n) or NUL characters (\0), as these break the FFmpeg list format and can lead to unintended file reads or command injection.
