how: Add a validation check in publish.py or any script using concatVideoFiles. Throw an error if a clip's path contains forbidden characters before passing it to FFmpeg.

title: B-Frame Suppression for Mobile
text: Disable B-frames using `-bf 0` for H.264/H.265 encodes. Standard B-frames create negative DTS (Decode Time Stamps) which cause several mobile browsers and VS Code's preview to freeze on the first frame or show a black screen while audio plays.
how: Add `-bf 0` to the FFmpeg command in `compose.py` and `compose_lab.py`. This ensures PTS == DTS, maximizing compatibility for Instagram/Facebook Reels on iOS.

title: AAC Priming Preservation
text: When muxing audio into MP4, copy the AAC sidecar (`-c:a copy`) instead of re-encoding. Re-encoding creates a new priming interval that FFmpeg writes as an empty leading video edit list, which Safari and QuickTime often render as a black first frame.
how: In `mix.py`, ensure the final muxing step uses `-c:a copy` for the audio stream if the source is already AAC, rather than defaulting to a generic re-encode.

title: Strict Frame Read Validation
text: Use `-xerror` in FFmpeg. By default, FFmpeg stops at the first unreadable frame but exits with code 0, resulting in a truncated video. `-xerror` forces a non-zero exit code on read failure.
how: Add `-xerror` to all FFmpeg commands in the pipeline to ensure `preflight.py` or `doctor.py` can accurately catch and report corrupted frame sequences.

title: Anti-Banding for Lab Look
text: Apply `aq-mode=3` via `-x264-params` or `-x265-params`. This redistributes bits to dark, flat areas and gradients, significantly reducing 'banding' artifacts in videos with dark backgrounds or subtle glows.
how: In `compose_lab.py`, append `aq-mode=3:aq-strength=0.8:deblock=1,1` to the encoder parameters when generating the 'lab' look videos.

title: BT.709 Color Space Tagging
text: Explicitly tag output with BT.709 metadata: `-colorspace:v bt709 -color_primaries:v bt709 -color_trc:v bt709 -color_range tv`. This prevents browsers from applying incorrect color transforms (like orange/warm shifts) to sRGB screenshots.
how: Add these flags to the final render step in `compose.py`. This ensures tech explainers in 'Kaise Tech' look identical across all devices and browsers.

title: Atomic Chunked Encoding
text: Split long videos into fixed-frame chunks (e.g., 300 frames), encode them with closed-GOP (`-g [size] -keyint_min [size] -sc_threshold 0`), and concat them using the FFmpeg `concat` demuxer with `-c copy` for faster, resumable renders.
how: Implement a new `chunk_compose.py` that utilizes the 'closed-GOP' logic to allow parallel encoding of scenes before a final lossless merge.

title: Even-Dimension Padding Filter
text: Automatically pad odd-dimension compositions to even numbers using `pad=ceil(iw/2)*2:ceil(ih/2)*2`. Most hardware and software encoders (YUV420p) will crash or reject frames with odd widths or heights.
how: Add this as a video filter (`-vf`) in the `compose.py` logic to prevent render failures when dynamic assets result in non-standard dimensions.

title: Root Compositor Prop Correction
text: The `drawElementImage` snapshot ignores the captured element's own `transform` and `opacity`. These must be manually re-applied to the canvas context: use `ctx.transform` for the matrix and `ctx.globalAlpha` for the opacity ratio.
how: In the capture script, read `getComputedStyle(root)` and apply its transform and alpha to the 2D context before calling `drawElementImage`.

title: Strict Frame Sequence Validation
text: Validate extracted frame sequences by enforcing a `frame_%05d.jpg` pattern and detecting gaps or duplicates early. Ordinals should be 1-indexed in filenames but 0-indexed in the internal map.
how: Update `research.py` or any frame-extraction logic to use a strict regex-based validator for frame filenames to prevent pipeline crashes during long renders.

title: Pipelined Worker JPEG Encoding
text: Parallelize produce and encode phases by transferring frames as `ImageBitmap` to an `OffscreenCanvas` in a Web Worker. This hides the ~7-10ms JPEG compression cost behind the next frame's DOM seek/paint work.
how: Implement a Web Worker in the browser instance that receives bitmaps via `postMessage` and returns base64 strings to a Node/Python callback for streaming to FFmpeg.

title: Software GL Detection Fallback
text: Detect SwiftShader/llvmpipe environments (common in Docker/CI) and fallback to standard screenshots. `drawElement` provides no speedup in software rendering and may drop sub-layers on transparent backgrounds.
how: Add a pre-render check using a temporary WebGL context to read `UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL`. If it contains 'SwiftShader' or 'llvmpipe', disable the fast-capture path.

title: Frame gap detection on cache rehydration
text: rehydrateCacheEntry() verifies frame sequence has no gaps (frame_00001.jpg, frame_00002.jpg...). Throws on missing index so a corrupted cache entry never silently produces short frame list. Format-agnostic: counts any frame_* files.
how: In preflight.py when loading cached frames for a clip, after getting frame list, verify contiguous indices from 1 to totalFrames. If gap, treat as cache miss and re-extract. Add to review.py as post-render check.

title: Schema version prefix for cache invalidation
text: SCHEMA_PREFIX = 'hfcache-v10-' bumped whenever extraction writes different frames for same key. Old generations (hfcache-v3-, v6-) become inert and are GC'd by prefix match. Prevents stale frames serving across deploys.
how: Define CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION in config.py for each cache type (frames, thumbs, assets). Prefix cache dirs with schema version. In doctor.py GC, match all hfcache-v* prefixes. Bump version when frame extraction params change (fps, format, transform).

title: Chrome process classification for memory telemetry
text: classifyChromeProcesses(browserPid, CDP processInfo[]) splits rows into browser, renderers[], gpu[] by type. Ignores utility, browser (except pid). Used to sample renderer/GPU memory via /proc/<pid>/statm. Requires CDP session on browser target (not page target).
how: In doctor.py or a new monitor, connect CDP to browser target, call SystemInfo.getProcessInfo, classify, then sample RSS of renderer/GPU pids. Log to results.md. Alert if renderer > 2GB or GPU > 1GB. Helps diagnose OOM in long renders.

title: LRU cache eviction with size cap and minimum age
text: gcExtractionCache(root, {maxBytes, minAgeMs}) scans cache-looking children (hfcache-v* and .partial-*), evicts oldest complete entries (by sentinel mtime) until under maxBytes, but skips entries younger than minAgeMs. Also removes aged partial dirs (crashed writers). Dry-run mode for observability.
how: Add gcExtractionCache call to doctor.py every 10 min for frame cache, thumbnail cache, and asset cache. Set maxBytes per cache (e.g., 5GB frames, 1GB thumbs). Expose evictedEntries/evictedBytes in dashboard (stats.py). Run dry-run first to log pressure.

title: Discard warmup capture with perf counter restoration
text: discardWarmupCapture() runs one capture frame (default frame 0, time 0) but restores capturePerf (frames, seekMs, beforeCaptureMs, screenshotMs, totalMs, frameMs[]) and BeginFrame damage counters (hasDamageCount, noDamageCount) to pre-warmup values even if inner capture throws. Returns no result so buffer can't escape.
how: In compose.py render pipeline, before actual frame batch, call discardWarmupCapture(session) to warm Chrome/GPU. Ensures first real frame has stable timing. Add to HyperFrames capture service if we control it.

title: Hidden Asset Optimization
text: Do not wait for video or image readiness if the element is inside a hidden node (`display: none` or custom `data-hidden` attributes). These assets often don't trigger decode/load events in headless Chrome, causing unnecessary timeouts.
how: Update the asset polling script in `research.py` or `compose.py` to filter out elements where `el.closest('[data-hidden]')` is true before waiting for `complete` or `readyState`.

title: Script Load Cause Classification
text: When a render fails due to asset timeouts, classify the cause: Local (404), CDN (Network Reset/503), or Remote. Specifically identify common libraries (GSAP, Three.js) in the error logs to distinguish between infrastructure issues and script bugs.
how: In `review.py`, parse the Puppeteer error logs for `net::ERR` codes and specific URL patterns (jsdelivr, unpkg) to provide better error messages in the Telegram dashboard.

title: Function Name Polyfill for Browser Scripts
text: When using transpilers like `esbuild` with `keepNames: true`, functions are wrapped in `__name()`. Puppeteer's `toString()` serialization breaks these. Install a no-op `window.__name = (fn) => fn` shim via `evaluateOnNewDocument` to prevent ReferenceErrors in the browser.
how: Add `page.evaluateOnNewDocument(() => { window.__name = (f) => f; })` to the browser initialization in `compose.py` to ensure GSAP or custom UI scripts don't crash.

title: Disqualify compositions with tl.call() from static dedup
text: Any GSAP timeline.call() (zero-duration callback) makes a composition ineligible for static-frame deduplication because callbacks are not seek-idempotent: verifying a later run can fire a callback that corrupts an earlier run's capture. Detect hasTimelineCall during GSAP interval scan and skip static dedup entirely.
how: In compose_lab.py's GSAP introspection (preflight), check for tl.call() usage. If present, disable static dedup for that composition and log a warning. This prevents silent corruption like a beat-6 counter value baking into beat-1 title card.

title: Structured sub-timeline warnings with actionable remedies
text: On timeout: warn with pending composition IDs and suggest adding data-no-timeline to intentional static hosts. On script_failure: name the failed script URL or the composition whose script threw (e.g., 'GSAP not loaded yet — load GSAP before first gsap use'). Hook onSubTimelineScriptFailure can abort render early. Ignores unrelated errors when timelines registered.
how: In review.py's vision review, parse these warning codes (sub_timeline_readiness_timeout, sub_timeline_script_failure) and surface in the dashboard with the suggested fix. Add data-no-timeline to static UI panels in lab look templates.

title: Transparent PNG verification background clearing
text: For transparent PNG capture (format=png, transparent=true), the verification page must clear its background via CDP Emulation.setDefaultBackgroundColorOverride so screenshots match the capture's transparent output. For opaque PNG or JPEG, keep page background.
how: In preflight.py's stills audit, when generating verification screenshots for transparent compositions, ensure the verification page runs the CDP background clear. Add a flag in the capture session options.

title: Locked warmup ticks for deterministic distributed renders
text: Force the BeginFrame warmup loop to run exactly 60 iterations (LOCKED_WARMUP_TICKS) regardless of page-load speed, so beginFrameTimeTicks becomes host-independent. This guarantees byte-identical captures across Cloudflare workers or local machines.
how: In the render worker (where HyperFrames is launched), set lockWarmupTicks=true when initializing the capture session. Ensure deriveBeginFrameTimelineTicks uses the locked tick count. Add a config flag in doctor.py to enforce this for all distributed renders.

title: Video metadata hints for layout-before-load
text: Apply intrinsic video dimensions (width/height) as CSS hints so videos layout correctly before metadata loads. Handles width-only, height-only, both, max-width, bordered flex items. Prevents layout shift during capture's first frames.
how: In compose.py / compose_lab.py when placing video clips (Muse image-to-video), call applyVideoMetadataHints with the known dimensions before capture starts. Ensures Ken Burns / card layouts don't jump.

title: WSL Wayland display handling for GPU probe parity
text: When running under WSL, launch the render browser without WAYLAND_DISPLAY iff the GPU probe required that to reach the GPU. This matches the probe's environment and avoids headless-shell crashes on Wayland.
how: In the render worker launch script (Cloudflare worker or local), call captureWithoutWaylandDisplay() from browserManager; if true, strip WAYLAND_DISPLAY from the browser process env. Already tested in frameCapture-wslWayland.test.ts.

title: Sanitized diagnostic URLs in logs
text: sanitizeDiagnosticUrl strips credentials, query strings, fragments from all URLs in diagnostics. data: and blob: URLs become 'data:<redacted>' and 'blob:<redacted>'. Relative paths keep only path component. Prevents token leakage in CI logs and Telegram alerts.
how: Apply sanitizeDiagnosticUrl in stats.py and review.py before writing any URL to results.md, Telegram, or dashboard. Wrap all console.error/console.log calls that may contain URLs.

title: In-page MP4 encoding eligibility gate
text: In-page encoding (MediaRecorder) only eligible when: captureMode=drawelement, format=mp4, codec=h264, hdr=false, transparent=false, workers=1, hls=false, videoLayer=false, encoderSupported=true. Any blocker returns {eligible:false, reason}. Clean fallback to FFmpeg path.
how: In compose.py/compose_lab.py render pipeline, call resolveInPageEncode before choosing encoder. If eligible, use page-side MediaRecorder for faster single-worker MP4; else use existing FFmpeg pipeline. Track encoderSupported via a one-time page.evaluate check.

title: Frame independence verification test
text: Ensures frames rendered in any seek order (forward, backward, random) are byte-identical to a fresh page render. Uses --disable-partial-raster Chrome flag to eliminate tile-redraw non-determinism. Test scene: rotated cards with per-frame opacity changes.
how: Add a CI job (frameIndependence.test.ts) that launches Chrome with --disable-partial-raster, captures frames 0–59 forward and backward, compares each to a fresh-page baseline. Fail if any pixel differs. Run on both hardware and SwiftShader GPU modes.

title: HLS packaging with GOP-locked segments
text: FFmpeg stream-copies video/audio into MPEG-TS segments with -hls_time, -hls_playlist_type vod, -hls_flags independent_segments. GOP locked to segmentSeconds * FPS via -force_key_frames and x264-params. Audio-only variant stripped from master playlist so players never select audio without video. Validates segmentSeconds as positive integer.
how: Add packageHls function to publish.py for future HLS delivery (e.g., Instagram Reels backup). Use lockedVideo() GOP settings from chunkEncoder.js. Ensure outputDir has no '%' char. Return master playlist path for CDN upload.

title: Page tab loss resilience with exit code reporting
text: openPage retries once if browser stays connected after a tab closes during startup. If browser exits, throws PageTabLostError with exit code and signal (e.g., 137 = OOM kill). Never retries a dead browser. Closes orphaned tabs before retry.
how: Wrap browser.newPage in doctor.py's Chrome lease pool with this logic. On PageTabLostError(browserRunning=false), mark host as unhealthy, trigger VM replacement. Log exitCode for OOM tracking.

title: DrawElement verification with PSNR/blank classification
text: DrawElementVerificationError carries structured kind ('psnr' or 'blank'), frameIndex, failedDb, verifyThresholdDb. Kind is a structural field, not parsed from message. Survives wrapping in cause chains. Enables precise failure categorization in distributed renders.
how: In preflight.py's still comparison, compute PSNR between rendered and reference frames. Throw DrawElementVerificationError with kind='psnr' if below threshold (e.g., 32 dB). For blank frames (all alpha=0), kind='blank'. Catch in doctor.py to retry only psnr failures.

title: Structured error classification for FFmpeg infrastructure vs per-sample noise
text: isFfmpegInfrastructureFailure matches: spawn ENOENT (missing binary), "No such filter" / "Unknown filter" stderr (libpostproc-less build). Explicitly does NOT match: EACCES/EPERM on frame read, psnr parse failures. Known collision: fs ENOENT reading frame shares code with execFile ENOENT → classified as infrastructure (acceptable false positive). Returns false for null/string/number errors.
how: In mix.py/encode.py FFmpeg error handling, wrap errors with isFfmpegInfrastructureFailure. On true: trigger doctor.py binary check/reinstall, alert ops. On false: treat as transient per-sample, retry frame. Log classification for analytics.

title: Frame distribution strategies: contiguous vs interleaved with stride
text: distributeFrames splits frames contiguously by default (worker 0: 0-24, worker 1: 25-49). For interleaved, frameStride on task (e.g., stride=3) means worker captures startFrame, startFrame+stride, ... Expected frames = ceil((endFrame-startFrame)/stride). selectVerifySampleIndicesForTask filters verification samples to task's range and stride lattice.
how: If studio adopts parallel rendering, use contiguous for simplicity. For verification (preflight.py), apply selectVerifySampleIndicesForTask to assign sample frames per worker. Store frameStride in task metadata for flagSilentWorkerExits accuracy.

title: Navigation timeout error augmentation with env/CLI/Docker hints
text: Augment Puppeteer navigation timeout errors with the effective timeout value, plus three remediation paths: (1) PRODUCER_PAGE_NAVIGATION_TIMEOUT_MS env var (ms), (2) --browser-timeout CLI flag (seconds), (3) HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH to swap browser binary. On darwin/arm64 with CSS 3D + audio, also suggest --docker (field signal ts=1784146416). Preserve original error via cause.
how: Wrap page.goto calls in renderOrchestrator/frameCapture with augmentPageNavigationTimeoutError(err, effectiveTimeoutMs, {platform, arch, hasCss3D, hasAudio}). Add hasCss3D compile-time scan (transform-style: preserve-3d, perspective, rotateX/Y, matrix3d) to enable Docker hint.

title: Parallel capture peer abort on first fatal failure with diagnostics
text: When any worker hits a pool-fatal failure (authoring, io, or any non-cancelled on streaming path), immediately abort all peers via shared AbortController. Collect each worker's browser console lines (filter: HTTP404, REQUESTFAILED, FrameCapture:ERROR). Format failure message: "Worker N: error (M other workers stopped)". Preserve first failure as abort reason. Silent exit detection uses frameStride-aware expected frame count (field signal ts=1784042064).
how: In parallel render path (if adopted), use executeParallelCapture pattern: createPoolFailureHandler({streaming, peerController, hooks: {onWorkerFailure}}). Classify failures via isPoolFatalWorkerFailure(kind, streaming). Run flagSilentWorkerExits(results) after capture. Keep selectWorkerDiagnostics(logs, 2) for compact error context.

title: Static analysis test banning real timers in page-side code
text: AST scan of all engine TypeScript sources ensures no bare setTimeout/setInterval in functions passed to page.evaluate/evaluateOnNewDocument or in page-script strings. Allows only virtual timer shim: window.__HF_VIRTUAL_TIME__.originalSetTimeout. Catches timers in named functions, arrow functions, and template literal scripts. Test fails if any found.
how: Add similar vitest test in studio repo scanning compose.py/compose_lab.py generated page scripts. Use TypeScript compiler API to parse .ts files, find CallExpressions to setTimeout/setInterval inside pageArguments (evaluate, evaluateOnNewDocument, etc.) and string literals containing setTimeout. Fail CI if violations exist.

title: Worker GPU verification for software render mode
text: shouldVerifyWorkerGpu returns true only for worker 0 when browserGpuMode: 'software'. All other workers and hardware mode skip verification. Prevents redundant GPU checks in parallel software renders.
how: In parallel render config, if using software GPU mode (common for headless CI), run GPU probe (WebGL context, drawElement test) only on worker 0 session init. Skip for workers 1+. Add to initializeSession in frameCapture.

title: Contention-aware scaling for large/expensive renders
text: For totalFrames >= largeRenderThreshold (default 1000) or weightedFrames (frames * captureCostMultiplier) >= contentionThreshold, cap workers at cpuCount / (coresPerWorker * captureCostMultiplier). coresPerWorker=2 default, 1.75 for Apple GPU disk. Prevents SwiftShader compositor + shader-blend thread pool starvation that surfaces as CDP timeouts. 8 cores→2 workers, 16→5, 32→10.
how: Set captureCostMultiplier in HyperFrames config per composition type: lab look with WebGL VFX = 2-3, classic Ken Burns = 1. Pass via config.captureCostMultiplier. Monitor boundBy='contention' in telemetry.

title: Secure capture proxy with SSRF protection
text: HTTP/HTTPS proxy that resolves hostnames via DNS + system lookup, validates every A record is public IPv4 (blocks private, link-local, carrier-grade, reserved, IPv6). Pins upstream connection to the checked numeric IP (preserves SNI, rejects non-identity encoding). Supports optional upstream HTTP proxy via HYPERFRAMES_CAPTURE_PROXY. Refuses URL credentials, non-http(s) schemes, and private literals before dialing. Logs refusal class (private, link-local, carrier-grade, internal-name, ipv6) for audit.
how: Integrate startCaptureProxy in compose.py's asset fetch step (Muse, FLUX, Pollinations). Set browser proxy args via browserProxyArgs(proxyUrl, pageServerDirectHost). Ensures all asset downloads go through validated path, preventing SSRF from malicious URLs in JSON data.

title: Network isolation for render pages via host-resolver-rules
text: Chrome launch flag --host-resolver-rules=MAP <private-host> 127.0.0.1 forces DNS rebinding protection: public DNS resolves to public IP, but connections go to localhost. Combined with PRODUCER_RESTRICT_PAGE_NETWORK=true, the capture server blocks all page-initiated fetches to private IPs (localhost, RFC1918) from page, iframes, workers, service workers, WebSockets, WebRTC, prefetch/preload, and redirects.
how: In browserManager.buildChromeArgs, add the host-resolver-rules flag mapping the render file server origin to 127.0.0.1. Set PRODUCER_RESTRICT_PAGE_NETWORK=1 in capture session env. Prevents SSRF and data exfil from user compositions.

title: Video frame injection respects ancestor visibility with !important
text: When injecting __render_frame__ images for videos, skip injection if the video's host has [data-composition-src] or [data-composition-file] and computed visibility:hidden (display:none always skips). For plain [data-start] hosts, still inject — the image's explicit visibility:visible overrides ancestor per CSS spec. Hide stale frames with style.setProperty('visibility','hidden','important') so layer mask !important rules cannot revive them.
how: In injectVideoFramesBatch and syncVideoFrameVisibility, check host element for data-composition-src/file and getComputedStyle visibility. Use setProperty with 'important' priority. Update compose_lab.py video replacement logic accordingly.

title: Capture budget guards: scan budget and risk frame fraction
text: Effect scan budget: 120s total, 240 frames per chunk. If a chunk yields no answer within remaining budget, abort hybrid. Projected total time > budget aborts early. Risk frame cap: 60% of frames. Memory check: riskSessionFits(availableMb, outputPixels) requires 1GB added + 1.5GB headroom at 1080p, 4× at 4K.
how: In frameCapture.js, before hybrid capture, call riskSessionFits with available memory (from OS) and outputPixels. If false, force screenshot. During scan, enforce SCAN_BUDGET_MS and MAX_RISK_FRAME_FRACTION. Log abort reasons for doctor.py alerts.

title: Hold replaced videos at preload=none from parse time
text: Videos that will be replaced by extracted frames (__render_frame__ images) must have preload=none set before Chrome starts loading. Use evaluateOnNewDocument to install a MutationObserver that sets preload=none on matching video IDs (by id or data-hf-render-id). This prevents double decode and network contention.
how: In compose_lab.py, collect all video IDs that will be frame-replaced. Pass to page.evaluateOnNewDocument(holdRenderFrameVideos, ids, 'data-hf-render-id') before navigation. Ensures preload=none at parse, not after.

title: Supersampled screenshot capture via deviceScaleFactor
text: Page.captureScreenshot accepts clip.scale = deviceScaleFactor. For 1080p output at 2×, set clip: {width:1920,height:1080,scale:2}. Chrome renders at 3840×2160 and downscales. Works for any integer factor (e.g., 720p→4K = 3×). Only applies when deviceScaleFactor > 1; default 1 uses scale:1.
how: In screenshotService.pageScreenshotCapture, pass deviceScaleFactor from composition spec (e.g., 2 for 'lab' 4K export). Ensure clip.scale matches. Already used in tests; verify compose_lab.py sets it for high-quality thumbnails.

title: Transparent background init with composition-root preservation option
text: initTransparentBackground injects a style #__hf_transparent_bg__ that sets background:transparent on html,body (and optionally [data-composition-id]). Uses Emulation.setDefaultBackgroundColorOverride with alpha=0. Calling twice with different clearCompositionRoot replaces the rule (single style element). Must run before transparent capture, after reference background read.
how: In frameCapture.js, call initTransparentBackground(page, {clearCompositionRoot: false}) for standard transparent pass; true for HDR layered DOM pass. Ensure it runs after readReferenceBackground() but before first frame capture.

title: Upstream proxy for capture requests with CONNECT tunnel
text: Set HYPERFRAMES_CAPTURE_PROXY=http://user:pass@host:port to route all capture-time fetches through an HTTP proxy. Engine opens a CONNECT tunnel with 15s timeout, sends proxy-authorization Basic auth. Only HTTP proxy supported. Unset means direct dial.
how: In capture session startup, read HYPERFRAMES_CAPTURE_PROXY. If set, pass to frameCapture.createCaptureSession which uses openUpstreamTunnel for each origin. Useful for corporate egress or geo-specific asset fetching.

title: Damage-Aware Frame Caching
text: Use the 'hasDamage' flag from BeginFrame to skip redundant screenshot encoding. If a seek results in no visual change (no damage), reuse the previous frame's buffer. This significantly reduces CPU load and disk I/O for static scenes or slow-moving animations.
how: Integrate a WeakMap cache in the render loop. Check the damage flag after every seek; if false, skip the screenshot call and reuse the last Buffer.

title: Late Stream Offset Handling
text: Chrome paints nothing for video streams that start late (e.g., first frame at 1.5s) until the playhead is within 1s of the first frame. When extracting frames for clips, ensure the extraction window accounts for 'itsoffset' or 'output_ts_offset' to prevent blank frames at the start of a clip.
how: Update the research.py or clip-processing logic to detect stream offsets via ffprobe and adjust the start-time padding when generating image sequences for Muse/HyperFrames.

title: Video Frame Sibling Injection
text: Native
how: Add to the HyperFrames runtime. Before rendering, scan for video tags and create siblings. During the render loop, update these images instead of trying to capture the raw video element.

title: Deterministic Encoder Threading
text: FFmpeg bitstreams for x264/x265 can vary based on thread count. Explicitly set '-threads' based on the assigned CPU quota (Math.floor(parallelism)) rather than letting FFmpeg guess from host cores. Cap libx265 at 16 threads to avoid errors on high-core systems.
how: Modify the FFmpeg command generation in compose.py and compose_lab.py to include the calculated -threads argument based on the server's available CPU resources.

title: Alpha-Preserving PNG Capture
text: Chrome's 'optimizeForSpeed' flag in captureScreenshot often crushes alpha values to 0 or 255. For transparent overlays, disable this flag and use 'Emulation.setDefaultBackgroundColorOverride' to {r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0} to ensure smooth, high-quality transparency in PNG exports.
how: Update the screenshot logic in the HyperFrames renderer to toggle background transparency and disable speed optimization specifically when format='png' is requested for overlays.

title: QuickTime H.265 Compatibility
text: When encoding H.265/HEVC video for Apple devices, always include the `-tag:v hvc1` flag. Without this, the default `hev1` tag used by FFmpeg often prevents the video from playing in QuickTime or on iOS devices.
how: Add `'-tag:v', 'hvc1'` to the FFmpeg argument list in `publish.py` or the encoding service when the codec is set to H.265.

title: Closed GOP for Segmented Delivery
text: For videos intended for HLS or chunked concatenation, lock the GOP (Group of Pictures) using `-g`, `-keyint_min`, and `-sc_threshold 0`. This ensures keyframes land exactly on segment boundaries, preventing glitches at seams.
how: When a 'series' or 'chunked' flag is set, add `-x264-params "open-gop=0:scenecut=0"` to the FFmpeg arguments.

title: Frame Reorder Buffer
text: Implement an async barrier that allows parallel workers to generate frames out of order but ensures they are written to the FFmpeg pipe sequentially. Use a Map to store pending resolvers and a cursor to track the next expected frame index.
how: Integrate a `FrameReorderBuffer` class into the render loop. Workers call `waitForFrame(n)`, write their buffer, then call `advanceTo(n+1)` to release the next worker.

title: Cgroup-Aware Memory Detection
text: Detect memory limits from `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max` (v2) or `memory.limit_in_bytes` (v1) to correctly size worker pools in Docker or Lambda environments. Host-level `os.totalmem()` often overreports available RAM in containers, leading to OOM crashes.
how: Add a `systemMemory.py` utility that checks these Linux paths before `os.totalmem()` to set the concurrency limit for Muse/Cloudflare workers.

title: Background Video Layer Compositing
text: Overlay transparent HTML/GSAP frames onto a background video using FFmpeg's `filter_complex`. Use `[1:v]fps=30,format=gbrp[v];[0:v]format=rgba[o];[v][o]overlay` to composite piped frames (input 0) over a source video (input 1).
how: Modify `buildStreamingArgs` to accept an optional background video path and inject the corresponding `-i` and `filter_complex` arguments.

title: Never execute helper binaries from project directory
text: Tests verify that nvidia-smi, vm_stat, ps are never resolved from the project folder (which could be a malicious binary). The renderer's PATH must not have the project dir first. This prevents supply-chain attacks where a compromised repo places a fake helper.
how: In doctor.py and any subprocess spawn (ffmpeg, ffprobe, yt-dlp), ensure the binary is resolved via absolute path or system PATH only. Never prepend project directory to PATH. Add a startup check in doctor.py that verifies ffmpeg/ffprobe paths are in /usr/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, etc., not in the repo.

title: B-frame aware final frame extraction at source end
text: When a window ends exactly at the source's end (e.g., last 8 frames of a 45-frame B-frame clip at 1/600 timescale), the extractor must request frames up to the last PTS, not just duration. The test synthesizes a 1.5s clip with B-frames (bf=2, timescale 600) and verifies the last 8 frames (indexes 37–44) are extracted correctly.
how: In our clip trimming (compose.py when using video clips), ensure the ffmpeg seek/trim uses -ss before -i for input seeking and -t for duration, but for the final segment, allow the extractor to read to EOF. If we ever implement local clip extraction, use the same frame-accurate logic.

title: Force PNG for color-critical UI frames
text: Default JPEG extraction shifts high-chroma reds (ΔE up to 10+). Forcing PNG keeps extracted frames within ΔE ≤5 of source. Chrome also requires PNG frames to carry an sRGB chunk and no cICP chunk to display code values untagged.
how: In compose_lab.py when extracting frames for UI-heavy scenes (stat counters, charts), pass format='png' to extractAllVideoFrames. Ensure preflight.py verifies PNG chunks contain sRGB and lack cICP.

title: Tail frame counting for VFR sources
text: tailFramesFromFinalFrame computes exact frame count for tail windows using startTime, firstFrame, outputFps, sourceFps, finalFrameSeconds, and optional streamLeadSeconds/lastPacketSeconds. Returns null when uncertain (avoids wrong counts).
how: In compose.py when using frameRanges for tail segments, call tailFramesFromFinalFrame with probed metadata (from ffprobe) to validate frame count before render.

title: ProRes 4444 alpha preserved in PNG frames
text: ProRes 4444 (yuva444p10le) extracts to PNG with exact alpha (128±1 at 50% opacity). ProRes 422 (no alpha) extracts to JPG. Format auto-selected by alpha presence.
how: In compose.py for overlay assets (lower thirds, UI), export as ProRes 4444. Extractor will output PNG with alpha. Verify preflight.py checks alpha channel for such clips.

title: Deferred range extraction for remote assets
text: When deferRangeExtraction=true and source is remote (urlByAbsentLocalPath), extractor counts frames via metadata without decoding, only decoding tail windows that reach source end. Saves bandwidth and time for long remote clips.
how: In scout.py/research.py when fetching remote reference clips, set deferRangeExtraction: true and provide urlByAbsentLocalPath. Use for B-roll preview without full download.

title: Progress callbacks during long frame extraction
text: extractVideoFramesRange accepts onProgress(p) with planned/done frames. Uses ffmpeg -stats_period 0.1 and real-time pacing (-re) to report incremental progress. Stall timeout adds GOP-aware buffer (keyint seconds).
how: Wire onProgress in compose.py to update job status in dashboard (Server tab). Set ffmpegProcessTimeout with GOP buffer: timeout + (keyint_seconds * 1000).

title: Geometric Playback Ramps
text: Calculate the source frame index for non-linear playback rates (e.g., 1x to 3x ramp) using the integrated source time: source(t) = duration * (target_rate^(t/duration) - 1) / ln(target_rate). This ensures visual sync during speed-up effects.
how: Integrate this formula into 'compose_lab.py' for UI panels or 'flows' that require dynamic speed changes for a high-tech look.

title: JPEG BT.601 Full-Range Filter
text: When extracting frames as JPEGs, use 'scale=out_color_matrix=bt601:out_range=pc:flags=neighbor,format=yuv420p' to ensure colors match the standard web video expectation (BT.601 full range).
how: Update the FFmpeg command in compose.py for all .jpg frame extractions to include this specific color matrix and range flag.

title: VFR-to-CFR Sampling Logic
text: Handle Variable Frame Rate (VFR) sources by using a specific FFmpeg filter chain: 'settb=intb/2, setpts=PTS-lte(TB,0.001), fps=target_fps:round=up'. This ensures every output slot has a valid frame even if the source has timestamp gaps.
how: In compose.py, use ffprobe to detect VFR (isVFR). If true, append this specific filter chain to the frame extraction command to prevent 'frozen' frames in synthesized clips.

title: Injection Cache Hygiene
text: Only record a frame as 'successfully injected' if the browser confirms the element was actually updated. If an ancestor is hidden (e.g., a scene not yet active), the injection might be skipped; recording it as 'done' causes the first visible frame to appear blank.
how: In our preflight.py or render loop, ensure the feedback loop from the browser (returning IDs of updated elements) is used to update our local 'last_rendered_frame' map.

title: Video Layer Passthrough Qualification
text: Identify 'passthrough' candidates: a single video covering the full timeline, no grading, no loops, and 1.0x playback rate. These can be muxed directly via FFmpeg instead of being re-rendered frame-by-frame, saving significant CPU.
how: Add a check in plan.py; if a background video meets these criteria, flag it for 'direct-mux' in the final FFmpeg assembly step.

title: RIFF/WAV Chunk Alignment
text: When parsing WAV files for analysis, always check for word-alignment. Odd-sized chunks (like metadata LIST chunks) are followed by a pad byte that is NOT included in the declared chunk size. Ignoring this leads to reading garbage data.
how: Update our audio analysis scripts to use a generator that correctly offsets by '8 + size + (size % 2)' when walking RIFF chunks.

title: Byte-Bounded LRU Frame Cache
text: Implement a two-bound LRU cache for frame data URIs using both entry count (e.g., 256) and a byte budget (e.g., 1500MB). Base64 strings are ~1.4x raw size. If a single frame exceeds the budget, skip caching to prevent 'self-eviction' thrashing.
how: Update our image/clip loading logic in compose_lab.py to use a central cache manager that tracks string lengths and evicts oldest entries when memory limits are hit.

title: CDP-Based Frame Transport
text: Instead of bloating the DOM with massive data URIs, use Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) 'Fetch.fulfillRequest' to serve frames as virtual network responses (e.g., /__hyperframes_video_frames__/uuid/1). Set 'Cache-Control: no-store' and 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *'.
how: Modify our Puppeteer/Chrome controller to enable 'Fetch' domain and intercept requests to a specific virtual prefix, fulfilling them from our Node.js frame buffer.

title: WebGL Context Auto-Release
text: Prevent 'Too many active WebGL contexts' errors in long videos by explicitly losing contexts of canvases in hidden or ended clips using the 'WEBGL_lose_context' extension once their playback window has passed.
how: In our GSAP timeline, add a callback at the end of scenes containing WebGL elements to trigger the loseContext() extension on the associated canvas.

title: HDR SDR-White Reference Mapping
text: When mapping sRGB (0-255) to HDR (16-bit), do not map 255 to peak 65535. Map sRGB 255 to 49151 (75% signal) for HLG or 38055 (~58% signal/203 nits) for PQ. This headroom allows HDR highlights to exist above the standard white level without blowing out.
how: Update our 'lab' look (compose_lab.py) color constants to use these reference points for UI panels and text, ensuring our tech explainers have professional HDR range.

title: Z-Significant Matrix Warning
text: When parsing CSS transform matrices, check for Z-axis components (m31, m13, m33). If they are significant (e.g., rotateY), the engine should project to 2D but warn the editor that the 3D effect will be lost in the final render.
how: Add a check in preflight.py to scan GSAP plans for 3D transforms and alert the user if a 'lab' look flow uses unsupported perspective.

title: Percentile-Based Capture Diagnostics
text: Track p50, p95, and p99 per-frame capture times. p50 shows steady-state speed, while p95/p99 identify 'long-tail' spikes caused by heavy paint operations, GC pauses, or font/image decoding that averages (avgTotalMs) hide.
how: Modify review.py and stats.py to calculate these percentiles from render logs. Use p99 spikes to flag specific scenes in research.py that need optimization.

title: Anti-Aliased Rounded Clipping
text: Use a distance-from-center circle formula (roundedRectAlpha) to calculate fractional alpha for corner pixels. This provides smooth anti-aliasing for rounded corners in the renderer rather than jagged CSS clipping.
how: Integrate a rounded-rect mask function into compose.py for our 'cards' and UI panels to improve the 'lab' look's geometric precision.

title: Shader Transition Metadata Protocol
text: Standardize scene transitions using HfTransitionMeta: start time, duration, shader ID, easing (GSAP), and from/to scene IDs. This allows the producer to pre-compute ranges and capture specific buffers for compositing.
how: Update plan.py to output transition metadata in this format, allowing compose.py to handle complex shader-based scene swaps instead of simple cuts.

title: 16-bit RGB48LE Blitting
text: Process frames in 16-bit little-endian (rgb48le) to preserve precision. Use a lookup table (LUT) for fast sRGB-to-HDR conversion during the blit of 8-bit DOM elements over the 16-bit background.
how: Upgrade our composition engine to handle 16-bit buffers for the 'lab' look, preventing banding in dark gradients and HUD glows.

title: In-memory Alpha Blitting
text: Perform alpha compositing of 8-bit RGBA overlays onto 16-bit rgb48le HDR frames directly in Node.js using zlib and Buffer manipulation. This replaces per-frame FFmpeg spawns for compositing, significantly reducing process overhead. Includes bilinear interpolation for affine transforms (matrix/matrix3d) and anti-aliased rounded rectangle masking.
how: Integrate into `compose_lab.py` or a new Node-based renderer. Instead of piping every frame through an FFmpeg filter complex for UI overlays, apply the UI 'props' to the raw video frame buffer in memory before the final encode step.

title: Alpha Plane Integrity Probe
text: Detect if a video file declaring an alpha channel is actually transparent or effectively opaque. It scales a 3-frame sample to 8x8 and checks the alpha byte of every pixel. This identifies 'fake' alpha files caused by improper remuxing (where the alpha tag remains but the data is dropped).
how: Add to `preflight.py`. When a user or Muse provides a WebM/ProRes clip for a story, probe it. If it's tagged alpha but decodes as 100% opaque, trigger a warning in Telegram (Studio360) to prevent 'black box' visual bugs.

title: Restricted Port Guard
text: Automatically detect and skip 'restricted ports' (e.g., 1, 22, 4045, 6000) that Chromium refuses to load due to security (net::ERR_UNSAFE_PORT). Uses a retry loop with `server.listen(0)` until the OS provides a port not in the `RESTRICTED_PORTS` set.
how: Update the local server logic in `compose.py`. Instead of blindly using the first port provided by the OS, wrap the listener in a safety check to ensure the Muse browser or headless Chrome never hits a blocked port error.

title: Private Asset Root Enforcement
text: Strictly block the render engine from accessing sensitive project files (e.g., `.env`, `.git/`, `.ssh/`, `certs/`) even if they are within the project directory. Uses a containment check to ensure assets only come from approved subfolders like `media/` or `downloads/`.
how: Implement in `research.py` and `compose.py`. Before passing a file path to FFmpeg or a browser, validate it against a 'private path' denylist to prevent accidental exposure of credentials in automated tech explainers.

title: Node-side Object-Fit Resampling
text: Implement CSS `object-fit` (cover, contain, fill) and `object-position` logic for raw image buffers using bilinear resampling. This allows pre-sizing assets to their layout boxes before they reach the compositor, ensuring visual parity with browser rendering.
how: Use in `compose.py` to pre-process images from Muse/Cloudflare. Instead of letting FFmpeg handle scaling (which can be inconsistent), pre-resample images to the exact 'HyperFrame' dimensions in the pipeline.

title: HDR PNG cICP fallback
text: If ffprobe fails to report color metadata for PNGs, manually parse the 'cICP' (Coding-Independent Code Points) chunk. 4 bytes: Primaries (e.g., 9=BT.2020), Transfer (e.g., 16=PQ/SMPTE2084), Matrix (e.g., 0=GBR), and Full Range flag.
how: Use this logic in research.py to correctly identify HDR assets from Muse/Cloudflare that need tonemapping for our SDR lab look.

title: GOP health analysis for seek safety
text: Flag videos as 'problematic' if they have only one keyframe (Single GOP) and are longer than 2 seconds. Calculate avgIntervalSeconds by dividing duration by keyframeCount. High intervals cause slow previews and frame-extraction failures.
how: Add to research.py. If a downloaded stock clip is 'problematic', force a re-encode to a standard GOP (e.g., 30 frames) before it enters the edit pipeline.

title: CLI path separator guard
text: Always insert a double-dash '--' before the file path in ffprobe/ffmpeg commands. This prevents files starting with a hyphen (e.g., '-clip.mp4') from being interpreted as command-line options, which can crash the process or cause security leaks.
how: Standardize all subprocess.run calls in research.py, compose.py, and publish.py to use the ['--', path] pattern.

title: Audio cover art exclusion
text: Ignore video streams where 'disposition: attached_pic' is 1. These are just album art in MP3/AAC files and should not be treated as visual video tracks by the automated editor.
how: Update research.py to classify assets correctly; prevents the studio from trying to 'edit' a static JPEG inside a music file.

title: Robust Rational FPS Parsing
text: Parse frame rates using strict Number() conversion for both rational (30000/1001) and plain forms. Reject values with more than one slash, non-finite results, or rates <= 0. Floor extremely slow rates to 0.01 instead of 0 to prevent fallback to 30fps defaults.
how: Update research.py and compose.py to use this logic when reading metadata from yt-dlp or ffprobe, ensuring FFmpeg -r flags never receive 'Infinity' or 'NaN'.

title: GPU Probe Minimum Dimensions
text: When probing GPU encoder availability, use a minimum frame size of 320x240. Some NVIDIA SKUs (L4/T4) reject frames below ~257px, causing false-negative 'unusable' reports for hardware acceleration.
how: If implementing local rendering, set the dummy probe video size to 320x240 in the hardware detection script.

title: Asymmetric Black-Pixel Diagnostic
text: Detect hardware-GPU capture bugs by identifying 'black-only-in-A' pixels (solid black in hardware render, content in software render). Use a blackSumThreshold (R+G+B <= 12) and a contentSumThreshold (R+G+B >= 32) to isolate artifacts from legitimate dark content.
how: Add to review.py: when a video is flagged by vision review for glitches, run a single-frame comparison between the GPU render and a CPU-only screenshot to confirm if black rectangles exist.

title: GPU Preset Mapping Table
text: Map standard libx264 presets (ultrafast, medium, slow) to hardware-specific presets. For NVENC, map to p1-p7. For QSV, map 'ultrafast' to 'veryfast' as it is not supported. This prevents 'Invalid Argument' errors during hardware encodes.
how: If we deploy a local GPU worker, update the FFmpeg command generator to use a mapping function before setting the -preset flag based on the detected encoder.

title: HDR10 Mastering Metadata
text: Use standard HDR10 mastering strings for FFmpeg x265 encoding: BT.2020 primaries, SMPTE 2084 (PQ) transfer, and specific mastering metadata (e.g., G(13250,34500)B(7500,3000)R(34000,16000)WP(15635,16450)L(10000000,1)).
how: Add these flags to the final FFmpeg export command in publish.py when HDR assets are detected, ensuring the 'lab look' glows correctly on HDR-capable mobile screens.

title: SSRF Network Blocklist
text: Block asset fetching from non-public IP ranges (10.0.0.0/8, 127.0.0.0/8, 169.254.0.0/16, etc.) and their IPv6/NAT64 equivalents to prevent Server-Side Request Forgery.
how: Apply this filter in the research.py and scout.py modules when resolving URLs from GitHub or HN to ensure the studio doesn't accidentally probe internal infrastructure.

title: Managed Process Wrapper
text: Wrap FFmpeg/Chrome processes with inactivity timeouts, deadline caps, and a two-stage termination (SIGTERM then SIGKILL after a grace period). Redact sensitive query strings (like S3 signatures) from stderr logs.
how: Replace raw subprocess calls in render.py and research.py with a ManagedChildProcess class. Implement the inactivity timer to kill stuck FFmpeg jobs that stop emitting progress.

title: Safe Media Path Segments
text: Map media IDs to file paths using a deterministic hash suffix (e.g., id~sha256_12chars). This prevents collisions on case-insensitive file systems (Mac/Windows) and sanitizes unsafe characters like colons or slashes.
how: Modify the asset downloader to use this naming convention for local storage, preventing 'Intro.mp4' and 'intro.mp4' from overwriting each other during parallel runs.

title: JPEG Header Guard
text: Validate JPEG Quantization Tables (DQT) and SOI markers in memory. Specifically check for invalid DQT precision (>1) which causes FFmpeg image2pipe failures.
how: Add to doctor.py or as a gate in compose_lab.py before sending frames to the encoder to catch corrupted frames generated by the browser.

title: FFmpeg Progress Parsing
text: A regex-based stats reader that parses FFmpeg's stderr for `frame=` and `time=` updates. It handles chunked stream data where lines might be split across buffers, providing a clean stream of frames and seconds processed.
how: Add to `runFfmpeg` logic. Use the parsed `seconds` and `frames` to update the Studio360 dashboard in real-time, giving better visibility than a generic 'running' state.

title: Metadata Provenance Stamping
text: Stamps the MP4/WebM container with custom metadata tags (`hyperframes_renderer`, `hyperframes_version`) using `-metadata` and `-movflags +use_metadata_tags`. This allows tracking which version of the studio code generated a specific file without burning watermarks into the video.
how: Add these flags to the FFmpeg command in `publish.py` or the final muxing step. Useful for debugging 'which version of the lab look produced this' from a downloaded Reel.

title: Cross-Platform RAM Monitoring
text: Sampling Resident Set Size (RSS) per PID across Linux (`/proc/pid/status`), POSIX (`ps`), and Windows (`tasklist`). It allows the pipeline to monitor the memory footprint of individual FFmpeg or Chrome processes.
how: Add to `doctor.py` to monitor render jobs. If a specific render process exceeds a MiB threshold (e.g., 2GB), kill it and restart to prevent OOM crashes on the server.

title: Uint16Array Alignment Rules for Hot-Path Optimization
text: Buffer.read/writeUInt16LE accept odd byteOffsets; Uint16Array requires 2-byte alignment. rgb48le (6 bytes/pixel) guarantees even row strides (width×6), so Buffer.alloc canvases yield aligned subarrays. Sliced Buffers at odd offsets (e.g., from parent.subarray(1)) throw on Uint16Array construction. Safe pattern: if (buf.byteOffset % 2) buf = Buffer.from(buf).
how: When optimizing alphaBlit.ts or shaderTransitions.ts for Uint16Array views (2× throughput), audit all Buffer sources. Ensure working canvases are Buffer.alloc (not sliced). Add a realign(buf) helper used before view creation. Document in CONTRIBUTING.md.

title: HDR PQ/HLG ↔ Linear LUT Conversion
text: Precomputed 65536-entry Uint16Array LUTs for PQ EOTF/OETF and HLG EOTF/OETF, plus cross-transfer (HLG↔PQ) composite LUTs. Converts in-place at ~100× speed vs per-pixel Math.pow. Used before/after shader transitions so UV-warping effects work in linear light.
how: In the render pipeline (pre-encode), call hdrToLinear(buf, 'pq') on captured frames, run transition, then linearToHdr(buf, 'pq'). Add to the frame-processing step in compose_lab.py or the FFmpeg prep stage. Set transfer from composition metadata.

title: SSRF-Safe Asset Downloader with Throughput Guards
text: downloadToTemp() rejects private IPs (10/8, 192.168/16, 169.254/16, ::1, fc00::/7) via DNS lookup before fetch. Enforces identity Content-Encoding only. Byte limit via HYPERFRAMES_MAX_DOWNLOAD_BYTES (pre-flight Content-Length + streaming cutoff). Free-space guard via HYPERFRAMES_DOWNLOAD_MIN_FREE_BYTES (statfsSync). Throughput floor 32 KiB/s over 60s rolling window, absolute deadline HYPERFRAMES_MAX_DOWNLOAD_MS, 300s stall cap. Retries once on timeout.
how: Replace current asset fetch in compose.py/compose_lab.py (Muse, Pollinations, FLUX) with this downloader. Set env vars in .env: MAX_DOWNLOAD_BYTES=50000000, MIN_FREE_BYTES=100000000, MAX_DOWNLOAD_MS=120000. Wrap in a fetchAsset(url, dest) helper used by image/clips download steps.

title: Signed URL Diagnostic Redaction
text: Strictly redact 'X-Amz-Signature' and other sensitive query params from error messages and telemetry. Never echo the full URL in logs if the download fails.
how: Update 'doctor.py' and error handlers to regex-strip sensitive params from URLs before sending failure reports to Telegram or 'results.md'.

title: IPv6 Literal Host Rejection
text: In restricted environments, block IPv6 literal hosts and IPv6-only DNS results to prevent bypasses of IPv4-based security rules or proxy configurations.
how: Configure our downloader's DNS lookup to use 'resolve4' exclusively when 'PRODUCER_RESTRICT_PAGE_NETWORK' is enabled in our production environment.

title: Unpacked Byte Cap for Gzip
text: When fetching text assets (CSS/JS) with 'content-encoding: gzip', enforce a strict limit on the unpacked size during stream consumption to prevent 'zip bomb' memory exhaustion.
how: Update our asset downloader to track total bytes written while decompressing. If it exceeds a safety limit (e.g., 1MB for CSS), abort the stream immediately.

title: Playlist Segment Path Guard
text: When downloading m3u8 or similar playlists, validate that all segment paths are relative and sit beside the playlist. Reject any paths that attempt to escape the directory (e.g., starting with '/' or containing '..').
how: Add a validation step after downloading any playlist file in our pipeline before passing it to FFmpeg for processing.

title: FFmpeg demuxer whitelist for safe media reading
text: When FFmpeg/ffprobe reads a URL, restrict -format_whitelist to only self-contained container demuxers: mov,mp4,m4a,concat,hls (excludes dash, imf, lavfi, etc.). For local files or plain HTTP, allow the same set. For HTTPS on a restricted render service, further restrict -protocol_whitelist to https,tls,tcp and force the self-contained format list. The whitelist is derived at runtime by parsing `ffmpeg -formats` output, with a safe fallback list.
how: Ensure the studio's HyperFrames render pipeline (which shells out to FFmpeg) passes these args. If the studio ever calls FFmpeg directly (e.g., in mix.py or thumb.py), apply urlInputArgs(input, {tool, caBundles}) to get the safe argument array.

title: Content-addressed URL declarations for cacheable probes
text: Call declareContentAddressedUrl(url, sha256) for operator-controlled assets (e.g., pre-built project tarballs, known-good media). Subsequent ffprobe/ffmpeg reads of that URL skip the proxy and demuxer restrictions because the hash proves the content is immutable and safe. The hash is stored in a Map keyed by URL without query string.
how: When the studio downloads a clip/image and verifies its SHA-256 (e.g., in preflight.py), call declareContentAddressedUrl() so later FFmpeg probes of the same URL are fast and unrestricted. Store the mapping in a JSON file loaded at startup.

title: Disk headroom guard for parallel downloads
text: Before streaming a response, claim the declared Content-Length (or 0 if unknown) against a per-volume free-space budget (default 512 MiB). Re-check free space every 4 MiB received. If free space would drop below the budget, abort with a retryable 'filesystem' error. Tracks unreceived bytes per device across concurrent downloads.
how: Add a DiskHeadroomGuard class to the studio's download helper. Configure via HYPERFRAMES_DOWNLOAD_MIN_FREE_BYTES env. Call guard.claim(declared) before streaming and guard.receive(chunk_len) on each chunk.

title: TLS verification with CA bundle fallback for HTTPS assets
text: For every HTTPS input, FFmpeg receives -tls_verify 1 -ca_file <path> where <path> is the first existing file from [/etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt, /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt, /etc/ssl/cert.pem]. Also sets -rw_timeout 30000000 -reconnect 1 -reconnect_delay_max 2, and for ffmpeg (not ffprobe) adds -reconnect_on_network_error 1. Fails fast if no CA bundle exists.
how: Add a get_ca_bundle_path() helper that mirrors the fallback list. Pass the resulting args to any FFmpeg invocation that reads HTTPS (e.g., in compose.py when pulling remote clips).

title: Chrome binary resolver with env overrides and fallbacks
text: Resolves Chrome/headless-shell path in order: 1) PRODUCER_HEADLESS_SHELL_PATH (engine override), 2) HYPERFRAMES_CHROME_PATH (Dockerfile-set), 3) a hardcoded fallback list (/opt/chrome/chrome-headless-shell, /usr/bin/chrome-headless-shell, /usr/bin/google-chrome, /usr/bin/google-chrome-stable, /usr/bin/chromium, /usr/bin/chromium-browser). Throws ChromeBinaryUnavailableError with the searched paths if none exist. Pure function, no side effects.
how: Adopt this exact resolver in the studio's Chrome launch code (likely in HyperFrames engine integration). Set HYPERFRAMES_CHROME_PATH in the studio's Dockerfile/render container. Catch ChromeBinaryUnavailableError to surface a clear 'Chrome missing' error instead of a generic puppeteer failure.

title: Proxy configuration for restricted network renders
text: When PRODUCER_RESTRICT_PAGE_NETWORK=true, a local capture proxy (HTTP on 127.0.0.1:random) is started. FFmpeg/ffprobe receive -protocol_whitelist http,https,tls,tcp,httpproxy -http_proxy http://127.0.0.1:<port> and the child env gets http_proxy set (and no_proxy/NO_PROXY cleared). The proxy itself enforces public-only DNS resolution. For FFmpeg <4.4 which ignores -http_proxy for HTTPS, the env var http_proxy is also set.
how: If the studio ever runs renders in a locked-down environment (e.g., shared Cloud Run), integrate withPublicOnlyProxy(args, inputIndexes) to inject the proxy args and env. The proxy startup is in captureProxy.ts; the studio would need to port or spawn it.

title: Explicit protocol versioning with v1 rejection
text: The handler only accepts PlanProtocol v2 (or absent, defaulting to v2). Any explicit v1 or mixed v1/v2 locators throw PLAN_PROTOCOL_UNSUPPORTED (non-retryable) before touching GCS. The workflow also validates protocol at orchestration level.
how: In plan.py, embed a protocol_version field in the plan JSON (current: 2). In render.py/assemble.py, assert protocol_version == 2; raise a custom ProtocolVersionError if not. In doctor.py, treat ProtocolVersionError as non-retryable. Document version in brain.jsonl.

title: Health check endpoint for container orchestration
text: The Hono app exposes GET /healthz returning {status: 'ok'}. Cloud Run uses this for startup/liveness probes. The server logs a structured 'server_listening' event on boot.
how: Add a minimal FastAPI/Flask endpoint in a new server.py (or extend doctor.py's HTTP interface) at /healthz returning 200 OK. Ensure it's lightweight (no DB/GCS calls). Log a JSON 'server_start' event on boot. Deploy behind the same process as the render worker.

title: Stale reference detection after source edit
text: When project files change, fingerprint mismatches invalidate the session. Existing element refs (hfId/selector) become 'stale-ref' on next query. Forces re-inspection with fresh selectors, preventing ghost animations.
how: In plan.py, after any template edit (compose_lab.py, thumb.py), increment a template_version. Store version in brain.jsonl. Preflight checks version; if mismatch, re-run selector resolution and discard cached animation plans.

title: Serialized query queue with idle teardown
text: Inspector serializes all operations via a promise chain (tail). After each query, a 120s idle timer tears down the browser context and proxy server. Concurrent calls share the same generation and page.
how: Wrap our render/inspect steps in a serialize() helper that chains promises. Add an idle timer in doctor.py that disposes headless Chrome after 2min of inactivity. Reuse browser across renders; only restart on source change or crash.

title: Strict request validation with byte limits
text: Inspect requests validate: 1-20 targets, each with exactly one of selector/hfId/ref, maxBytes 2048-256000, time >=0. Timeline requests enforce mutual exclusivity of at/range/boundary, valid component spec, and offset pagination requiring generation.
how: Add validateInspectRequest() and validateTimelineRequest() in preflight.py. Enforce maxBytes on Gemini responses, target counts in plan.py, and time ranges in compose.py. Return structured error codes (invalid_request, stale_generation) for Telegram approvals.

title: Bounded JSON responses with continuation tokens
text: Inspect responses cap at maxBytes (default 12KB). Omitted snippets return IDs; caller re-requests with generation + snippet IDs to fetch more. Ensures Telegram/message-size limits never truncate critical data.
how: Modify publish.py and stats.py to paginate large JSON (insights, brain dumps). Add maxBytes param to our internal APIs. Return {data, omitted:[ids], generation}. Client can fetch omitted by IDs.

title: Timeline boundary queries for retention editing
text: Inspector timeline API supports boundary, at, range, and component (selector/hfId/ref) queries. Returns events with relation: crosses/starts/ends/instant, precise start/end times, stagger groups, nested timeline offsets, playback-rate ramps, and co-target lists. Example: boundary: 2.5 on #bars shows 7 crosses, 1 start, endpoint handoff detection, and stagger member exclusion notes.
how: In review.py or new retention editor, call inspector.timeline({boundary: dropTime, component: {selector: element}}) to find animations crossing viewer drop-off points. Use relation 'crosses' to identify mid-animation exits. Map to scene timestamps for re-edit.

title: Composition hierarchy mapping for nested debugging
text: mapInspection reports every composition root and host enclosing a targeted element, with file:line IDs. Handles root-relative and host-relative mounts, Windows paths, repeated mounts (candidates), and deduplication. Shows composition root, composition host, html opening tag, matched CSS candidate kinds. Omits tags already shown in other snippets.
how: When preflight.py Gemini review flags a visual bug, use inspector.inspect() on the element to get full composition ancestry. Feed the snippet chain (root → host → nested root → element) to Gemini for context-aware fix suggestions.

title: Service worker cache busting for preview
text: Inspector test shows service worker serving stale HTML (STALE) even after index.html edit (NEW). Inspector detects source change via fingerprint (ignoring data-hf-id stamps), increments generation, reloads page, and fetches updated content. pageLoads increments only on actual navigation.
how: In doctor.py or preview server, ensure service worker unregisters or updates on source change. Use fingerprint(dir) that ignores .hyperframes/ folders and data-hf-id attributes. Trigger page reload only when liveFingerprint changes (content change, not HF ID stamps).

title: Fingerprinting ignores HF ID stamps
text: liveFingerprint(dir) ignores data-hf-id attribute additions/removals on existing elements. Only changes when actual content (class, structure, text) changes. fingerprint(dir) (standalone) does change on HF ID stamps. PREVIEW_IGNORED_DIRS (.hyperframes, .git, etc.) excluded from both.
how: In doctor.py cache invalidation, use liveFingerprint for 'content changed' decisions (re-render needed). Use fingerprint for 'source file touched' decisions (re-index needed). This avoids re-renders when only HF IDs are stamped during preview.

title: Concurrent source map isolation
text: bundleToSingleHtml with scriptProvenance callback keeps default HTML unchanged (no hf-inspect- markers). Concurrent maps on different directories are isolated: each map only sees its own marker variables (marker0 vs marker1). Plain output identical to mapped minus sourceURL comments.
how: In preflight.py parallel composition validation, run bundleToSingleHtml with scriptProvenance per composition. Ensures source maps don't leak across compositions. Use provenance maps to attribute runtime errors to correct source file/line in review.py.

title: Templating token skip for asset validation
text: Asset linting must skip src values containing unresolved templating tokens (<<token>>, {{ token }}, ${token}) before URL cleaning (which truncates at ?/#). Also ignore data-var-src bindings; only validate real src.
how: Update preflight.py asset checks to regex-skip token patterns on raw attribute values; ensure cleanAssetUrl not applied before token check.

title: Fast linear HTML scans for linting
text: Replace regex-based HTML scanning with single-pass linear scans (block comments, script/style tags, protected blocks) that process 4 MB pages in <1 s vs minutes for regex. Uses indexOf and a tiny state machine for tag tracking.
how: Integrate into preflight.py to audit HyperFrames layout before render; add linearScans functions to detect unclosed tags, invalid script closes, empty style blocks, and protected ranges.

title: HEVC video detection with proxy hint
text: Lint step runs ffprobe on local video files; if codec_name=hevc (tags hvc1/hev1), emit info finding naming the file and noting automatic H.264 proxy caching. Skips missing, remote, or unprobeable files.
how: Add to preflight.py or a new lint-video.py; call ffprobe via subprocess, cache results per run, warn if HEVC found so proxy generation can be prepared.

title: Inline transcript requirement
text: Caption compositions must embed transcript as var TRANSCRIPT = [{text,start,end},...] in script. Fetching /assets/transcript.json breaks studio caption editor. Inline + fetch is ok; fetch-only is error.
how: Modify plan.py caption generation to always inline TRANSCRIPT. Add preflight check for caption compositions.

title: Caption container positioning
text: Caption elements must use position:absolute. position:relative on .caption-* containers breaks stacking and causes overflow. Error if found.
how: Add to compose.py caption CSS template. Preflight scan for position:relative on caption selectors.

title: Text-shadow on group vs word
text: Tweening textShadow on caption group container (.caption-group, #cg-*) creates visible rectangle behind semi-transparent inactive words. Apply textShadow only to active word elements; use scale on group for pulsing.
how: Update plan.py caption GSAP template. Preflight regex check for textShadow on group selectors.

title: Duplicate audio track detection
text: Collect all audible clips (audio + video with audio) from root through mounted sub-compositions. For each data-track-index, check if time windows overlap. Overlaps on same track play simultaneously and stack in Studio lane — flag as warning.
how: Implement collectMainTimelineAudio logic in review.py or new lint_audio.py. Run after script plan but before TTS. Use existing data-track-index from plan.py output.

title: Shader unbounded cosine pow detection
text: Scan authored .js/.mjs/.cjs scripts (skip minified, vendor, node_modules) for GLSL pow(1.0 - max(dot(vN,vV),0.0), exponent) without clamp. Causes NaN on back-facing pixels. Flag at original line/column.
how: Add shader lint step in preflight.py for lab look compositions. Use regex from shaderDomainOffsets. Only check scripts actually linked in HTML.

title: Adapter script presence validation
text: If composition uses GSAP (gsap.*), Lottie (lottie.* or data-lottie-src), or Three.js (THREE.* or import 'three'), verify a matching <script src> or ESM import exists. Sub-compositions inherit from host — skip check there.
how: Add in preflight.py after script injection. Parse window.__timelines script content for adapter usage. Error if missing with CDN fixHint.

title: Project structure lint: single root, no blank index
text: Error if multiple root .html files have data-composition-id (except known pages). Error if index.html has no renderable content but a standalone composition exists in compositions/ — render commands open index.html and capture only background.
how: Add in doctor.py or preflight.py. Scan project root for .html with data-composition-id. Check index.html for blank root with mounted compositions.

title: Sub-composition Style Scoping
text: Styles for sub-compositions must reside inside the <template> tag. Styles placed in <head> or outside the template are lost when the sub-composition is mounted dynamically.
how: Modify 'compose_lab.py' to ensure any component-specific CSS is injected directly into the <template> block of the sub-composition.

title: Static Selector Analysis Guard
text: Ban template literals in 'document.querySelector' calls within composition scripts. Using backticks with variables (e.g., `${id}`) prevents the linter from statically verifying element existence.
how: Add a check in 'preflight.py' to flag backticks inside querySelector/querySelectorAll calls in inline scripts.

title: Composition File Line Limit
text: Limit composition HTML files to 300 structural lines (excluding <style> blocks). Files exceeding this should be refactored into nested sub-compositions to prevent render-process memory bloat.
how: Add a line-count utility to 'preflight.py' that strips <style> content and checks the remaining HTML length.
